text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 👼👼👼Baby Cherub Angel Sings Phonic Songs, Week One: Prenatal Development:  👶 Pregnancy Days 1 to 7 (Week 1)
Your baby is not here yet. Not one tiny cell. So why is a little cherub named Pip already flying down from heaven with four songs in his hands, ready to sing baby music over a home with no baby in it? Here is the secret God whispered to him.
🩺 What Week One Really Is
Doctors count week one from the first day of your last period. Conception comes about two weeks later. So this week there is no baby yet. There is a home God is getting ready, and a child He already knows by name.

🌌 Before the Stars
Once upon a time, before one star, before the oceans learned to sing, there was God. His heart was full of a song He had been singing forever. He smiled and said, "I want to make someone to love. Someone brand new. And I will know them before anyone else does."

👼 The Angel Who Could Not Wait
High above the clouds, where the air hums like lullabies, lived the smallest angel in the choir. Pip had wings like spun sugar and a voice like a silver bell. Every morning he pressed his ear to the shelves of heaven's golden library, where God keeps every name.

One morning Pip heard a name no one had ever spoken. "God, whose name is that?" God leaned close. "That is a baby I am preparing. I knew that little one before the world was made." Pip's wings trembled. "Can I go see them?" "Soon," said God. "And you will carry songs."

📖 God Knew You First
✝️ "Before I formed you in the womb, I knew you. And before you went forth from the womb, I sanctified you." (Jeremiah 1:5, CPDV)

This is God's plan. He knows your child before your child is formed. That is why GLAL School starts singing before the baby is even here. Phonic songs are not for a test. They are a love song from God, sung over the home He is preparing.

🎶 The Four Songs of Heaven
God placed four songs in Pip's hands. The Song of Recognition says, "I see you." The Song of Attachment says, "You belong." The Song of Curiosity says, "Wonder with Me." The Song of Comfort says, "You are safe." All the lullabies, nursery rhymes, and kids music on earth echo one of them.

🏡 Pip Finds an Empty Cradle
Pip flew down on a beam of morning light to a little house with a garden. A mother was sleeping. Pip looked everywhere for the baby. No baby. "God," he whispered, "did I come too early?" And God laughed softly. "No, Pip. You came right on time."

"This is the week I prepare the home. Sing over the mother. Sing over the house. Sing over the cradle that is still empty." So Pip sang baby music over the whole house, soft as nursery rhymes at bedtime, kids music for a child who is not here yet.

💭 Why Sing Before There Is a Baby?
Because God does. He sang over creation before there was anyone to hear. When you sing this week, you are not performing for an audience. You are joining the oldest song there is, the one God has been singing over your child since before time began.

🎧 This Week's Baby Cherub Song
Play this week's Baby Cherub song. It is baby music in a little angel's voice, full of phonic songs: the soft "m" of mama, the long "ooh" of lullabies, like nursery rhymes from heaven. Hum along. If Dad or Grandma puts on the headphones and sings along too, even better.

📝 Week One Journal
Write one line this week: "God, You already know my child's name." Then write down any sound from the phonic songs that stays with you. Kids music starts here, not in a classroom, but in a mother's heart that sings first.

🙏 Week One Prayer
🕊️ "Father, You knew my child before the stars. Prepare my body, my home, and my heart. Let our house be full of Your song. In Jesus' name, Amen."

🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Deep Dive: Week 1 (Days 1 to 7): Baby Cherub Sings Phonic Songs, Prenatal Development

📚 The Library of Names
In the golden library of heaven, the shelves stretch farther than any eye can see. Each shelf holds a book, and each book holds a name. Not a nickname. The true name, the one God has for that person and no one else in all of history.

Pip had spent a thousand years reading those shelves. He found Abraham, who left everything because God called him. He found Moses, who argued with God at a burning bush and still said yes. He found Ruth, who chose loyalty over comfort, and Esther, who found courage she did not know she had.

But the new name was different. Reading a name in a book is one thing. This was like hearing a song for the first time and knowing, somehow, that the song was about you. Something stirred in Pip's little chest that he had no word for. "God," he said, "I want to meet them."

"You will," God said. "But first you must understand what you are carrying." Then God opened His hand, and four notes of light lay in His palm, each one humming a different tune. This is where the four songs of heaven begin.

👀 The Song of Recognition
The first note was no bigger than a snowflake. When Pip looked closely, he saw it was made of thousands of tiny sounds woven together. "This is the song of recognition," God said. "It is the sound a soul makes when it is finally seen. Every child is waiting to be known."

In heaven, this song is made of consonants, the little sounds that say "I know you." Pip practiced until his bell voice could sing every one, from the soft "m" of mama to the strong "b" of beloved. These are the building blocks of phonic songs, the sounds a child will one day read.

"On earth," God went on, "there are mothers who sing to a child they cannot see yet. They do not always know why. They hum. They sing nursery rhymes. They say a name out loud. That is this song. That is recognition. That is the sound of 'I see you.'"

Pip thought of Elizabeth. When Mary, carrying Jesus, came to visit, the baby John leaped inside Elizabeth's womb. Even before he was born, John recognized the presence of the Savior. Elizabeth could not keep it in. She cried out:

✝️ "For behold, as the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the infant in my womb leaped for joy." (Luke 1:44, CPDV)

"The child knows," God said. "Spirit to spirit, the child always knows." That is the heart of GLAL School. Long before a baby understands words, God's song can reach their spirit. Recognition comes first. Reading comes later. This is God's plan.

🎀 The Song of Attachment
The second note was long and soft. It stretched out like a ribbon of gold. "This is the song of attachment," God said. "It is the sound of belonging. It is what a mother hums when she rocks her baby. It says, 'You are mine, I am yours, and nothing will change that.'"

This song is made of vowels, the sounds that stretch out long and warm, "oooh" and "aaah," wrapping around a baby like a blanket. Pip held the note to his ear and heard lullabies from every corner of the earth, in languages he did not speak, from places he had never been.

And under all those lullabies, one steady rhythm: the heartbeat. God showed Pip how, months from now, when the baby's ears are ready around the middle of pregnancy, a mother's heartbeat becomes one of the first sounds her child hears. The first music. The sound of home.

Mary knew this song. While she carried Jesus, she visited Elizabeth, and her heart overflowed into a song the Church still sings today. Her long, warm vowels carried her love for God and for the baby she was carrying:

✝️ "My soul magnifies the Lord. And my spirit leaps for joy in God my Savior." (Luke 1:46-47, CPDV)

Pip also thought of the mother of Moses. She hid her baby for three months, then placed him in a basket among the reeds and trusted God with him. We can only imagine the lullabies she hummed as she let him go. God heard her heart, and Pharaoh's daughter found the basket.

Moses grew up to lead a nation out of slavery. "Even when a mother cannot see the way," God said, "the song goes on." Attachment is not only holding on. Sometimes it is trusting the One who holds your child even better than you can.

✨ The Song of Curiosity
The third note sparkled. It jumped and danced in Pip's hand like it could not sit still. "This is the song of curiosity," God said. "It is the giggle, the coo, the 'da da da' a baby makes when they find their own toes. It is the hundredth 'why?' It is a mind waking up."

This is where kids music begins. Not in a classroom. Not on a stage. In the wonder of a small voice discovering sound. And it began with God. In the garden, He brought every animal to Adam to see what Adam would call it.

Picture it. God holds up a feathered little creature. "What will you call this one?" Adam laughs and says, "Bird!" And God laughs too, because naming things is one of the greatest joys there is. Naming was not a chore. It was an invitation to explore, to wonder, to ask.

✝️ "And God saw everything that he had made. And they were very good." (Genesis 1:31, CPDV)

Pip thought of the disciples, who walked with Jesus for three years and still asked questions every single day. Teach us to pray. Who is the greatest? How many times should I forgive? Jesus never grew tired of them. He answered with stories, with silence, and with questions of His own.

"Curiosity is holy," God said. "It is the sound of a soul reaching toward Me." That is why GLAL School fills a child's world with nursery rhymes, kids music, and phonic songs. Each new sound is a door, and God loves to watch His children walk through it.

🕯️ The Song of Comfort
The fourth note was the quietest. It did not sparkle or dance. It simply glowed, steady and warm, like a candle in a window. "This is the song of comfort," God said. "It does not fix anything. It does not explain anything. It simply stays."

It is the steady beat, the "shhh, shhh, shhh" that says you are safe, you are held, you are home. Young David sang it in the fields while he watched his sheep. And on the night before He died, Jesus sang a hymn with His disciples before He walked into the dark:

✝️ "And after a hymn was sung, they went out to the Mount of Olives." (Matthew 26:30, CPDV)

Pip thought of Job, who lost his children, his wealth, and his health, and sat in the ashes. His friends came to comfort him, but their long explanations only made things worse. Then God spoke out of the whirlwind, not with answers, but with wonder:

✝️ "Where were you, when I set the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding." (Job 38:4, CPDV)

Job had demanded answers. What he found instead was presence. God Himself had come close. And Job's whole heart changed in one sentence:

✝️ "By paying attention with the ear, I have heard you, but now my eye sees you." (Job 42:5, CPDV)

"Comfort is not the absence of trouble," God told Pip. "Comfort is the presence of love in the middle of trouble." Pip thought of Jesus praying in the garden of Gethsemane, in such agony that His sweat became like drops of blood. God did not take the cup away. But He sent help:

✝️ "Then an Angel appeared to him from heaven, strengthening him." (Luke 22:43, CPDV)

Presence. Not rescue. Presence. "That is the song," God said. "That is the one a child needs most." It is why the quiet lullabies at bedtime matter so much. They are not just baby music. They are a mother saying, "I am here, and God is here too."

🌱 How God Grows a Person
Now you might wonder: if God already knows everything about us, why does He take so long to grow us? Why not make us grown-ups from the start? Because God is not in a hurry. God is a gardener, not a factory. King David knew it. He sang:

✝️ "For you have possessed my temperament. You have supported me from the womb of my mother." (Psalm 138:13, CPDV)

A gardener knows a seed does not become a tree in a day. A seed becomes a sprout. A sprout becomes a sapling. And only after many seasons of sun and rain and wind does the tree bear fruit. Week one is the soil being made ready. God is patient with the soil.

🧥 Joseph
God grew Joseph slowly. Joseph was the next-to-youngest of twelve brothers, and they were jealous because their father loved him so much. They threw him into a pit and sold him to traders headed for Egypt. But God was not finished with Joseph.

In Egypt, Joseph worked hard and stayed honest. Even when he was thrown into prison for something he did not do, he kept trusting God. Then Pharaoh had a dream no one could explain, and Joseph, who had learned to listen to God in the dark, told him what it meant.

Pharaoh made Joseph the second most powerful man in Egypt. When famine came, Joseph had food stored up, and he saved his own family, the very brothers who had betrayed him. He forgave them, and he told them the truth about what God had done:

✝️ "You devised evil against me. But God turned it into good." (Genesis 50:20, CPDV)

That is character. That is what God grows in us. Not just strength, but forgiveness. Not just success, but mercy. And it grows slowly, one season at a time, like a song a mother sings over and over until her child knows every word.

🐑 David
God grew David slowly too. He was the youngest of eight sons, so small that when the prophet Samuel came to anoint a king, David's own father did not even call him in from the fields. Samuel looked at the tall older brothers. But God said no to every one.

✝️ "For man sees those things that are apparent, but the Lord beholds the heart." (1 Samuel 16:7, CPDV)

God chose David's heart. A heart that sang. A heart that danced before the Lord. A heart that wrote songs people are still singing three thousand years later. The shepherd boy's psalms became some of the most loved songs in history, and they began alone in a field with sheep.

🌸 Mary
God grew Mary slowly too. She was a young woman in a small town, nobody famous by the world's standards. But when the angel Gabriel told her she would bear a son and call His name Jesus, she did not say, "I am too young." She did not say, "I am not ready."

✝️ "Behold, I am the handmaid of the Lord. Let it be done to me according to your word." (Luke 1:38, CPDV)

That is trust. That is what God grows in us: the courage to say yes even when we do not understand the whole plan. Every mother in week one is standing where Mary stood, at the start of a story she cannot see the end of, saying yes to God.

⭐ The Baby Who Changed Everything
And then there is the baby at the center of it all. Jesus did not come as a king in a palace. He came as a baby in a manger, with animals breathing warm air around Him and shepherds hurrying in from the hills. And the angels sang over Him that night:

✝️ "Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will." (Luke 2:14, CPDV)

Think of that. The very first song sung over the newborn Jesus came from angels. Heaven's choir, the same choir where little Pip sings, filled the sky over Bethlehem. Angels have been singing over babies from the very beginning.

And that baby grew. He learned to walk and to talk. He learned the songs His mother sang. At twelve He stayed behind in the temple, listening to the teachers and asking questions, and everyone who heard Him was amazed.

✝️ "And Jesus advanced in wisdom, and in age, and in grace, with God and men." (Luke 2:52, CPDV)

Even the Son of God grew up slowly. Even He learned. Even He had a mother who sang to Him and a father who taught Him to work with wood. God does not rush. God grows.

🤱 The Mothers Who Sang
As Pip flew down through the clouds, he saw the mothers. He saw Hannah, who prayed for a child for years. When God gave her Samuel, she brought her little boy to the house of the Lord to dedicate him, and she sang a song of praise so strong it is still in the Bible today.

He saw Mary singing her Magnificat while Jesus grew inside her. He saw Elizabeth rejoicing as her baby leaped. And he saw mothers in every time and every place, singing lullabies and nursery rhymes to babies they could not yet see, humming melodies they did not know they knew.

"They are all singing My song," God said. "They just do not always know it." Mom, that includes you. Every time you hum this week's phonic songs, you are joining a choir of mothers that stretches all the way back to Hannah and Mary.

🔨 The Fathers Who Built
Pip saw the fathers too. He saw Joseph the carpenter teaching the boy Jesus to measure wood and drive nails. He saw Joseph wake in the night when an angel warned him in a dream, and take Mary and the baby to Egypt to keep them safe from King Herod.

He saw Zechariah, the father of John the Baptist. Zechariah did not believe the angel's message, so he could not speak for months. But when his son was born and named, his very first words poured out as a song:

✝️ "Blessed is the Lord God of Israel. For he has visited and has wrought the redemption of his people." (Luke 1:68, CPDV)

Silence turned to song. That is what God does. Dad, this week is your week too. Put on the headphones and sing along with the Baby Cherub song. A father's voice is part of the home God is preparing, long before the baby arrives.

🧒 The Children God Chose
And Pip saw the children, chosen by God while they were still small. He saw the boy Samuel, sleeping in the temple, hearing a voice call his name in the night. Three times he ran to old Eli. The fourth time, he answered God Himself:

✝️ "And Samuel said, 'Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.'" (1 Samuel 3:10, CPDV)

He saw David, a shepherd boy with a sling and five smooth stones, facing a giant because he trusted God more than he feared Goliath. He saw Josiah, who became king at eight years old and grew into a king who turned the whole nation back to God.

And he saw the little boy who offered his five loaves and two fish to Jesus, and watched them feed five thousand. God does not wait for people to be grown. God calls them while they are still small. Even before they are born.

📝 Your Week One Practice
This is God's plan for week one: sing first. Play the Baby Cherub song once a day this week. Let it be baby music for a home that is getting ready. Hum the vowels. Say the consonants out loud. Do not worry about getting it right. Heaven is not grading you.

Teach it three ways, the way the best preschool teachers do. First, listen. Second, hum along. Third, sing it with someone: your husband, your mom, your older children. Kids music is meant to be shared. The same song three different ways is how a lesson truly lands.

Journal prompts for this week: Which sound in the song stayed with me? What do I want my child to know about God first? Which Bible mother do I feel closest to right now: Hannah, Elizabeth, Mary, or the mother of Moses? Write one line for each.

One practical gift: doctors recommend a daily prenatal vitamin with folic acid before and early in pregnancy to help protect the baby's developing brain and spine in the earliest weeks. Ask your doctor or midwife which one is right for you. The songs are a spiritual gift. They are not medical care.

💛 The Promise
At last Pip reached the little house with the garden. The mother was still sleeping, and the cradle was still empty. Pip was not worried anymore. He understood now. He opened his wings, and the four notes of light rose from his hands and began to sing.

The song of recognition. The song of attachment. The song of curiosity. The song of comfort. The notes filled every room. They settled on the mother like sunlight. They settled on the empty cradle like a blanket, so that when the baby comes, the songs will already be there.

"Before you were formed," Pip sang into the quiet, "God already knew your name. You will be wrapped in peace before you ever open your eyes. The angels will stay near. You will never be alone. You are already loved." And far above, God rejoiced:

✝️ "He will rejoice over you with gladness. In his love, he will be silent. He will exult over you with praise." (Zephaniah 3:17, CPDV)

In the great golden library, a new book appeared on the shelf. It had no pages filled in yet. Just a name, and a song, and a promise. God was not finished. God never is.

🌅 The End, or Rather, the Beginning
Because that is the truth of it, little one. Your story will not start the day you are born. It will not start with your first breath or your first word. Your story started before the stars, before the oceans, before time itself, in the heart of God.

He looked at all that light and all that love and said, "I want to make someone to love." And He is making you. He is preparing your home right now. He is not done. Next week, Pip has a new song to carry, so keep the baby music playing.

🕊️ "Father, thank You for knowing my child before the world began. Fill our home with Your four songs: recognition, attachment, curiosity, and comfort. Grow us slowly and grow us well. In Jesus' name, Amen."

text:
What could become the next big protein flavour in India? While researching India’s protein beverage market, one question kept coming up for me: Why does protein have to be sweet?

I asked Richa Joshi Kaul, co-founder of rightkind, who has been experimenting with savoury protein.

Her view is that there is a real gap for consumers who are tired of sweet protein flavours or simply prefer something more familiar and savoury. She also pointed to parents, elderly consumers and vegetarians who may want more protein but may enjoy sweet shakes less. 

There is also a reason protein products have traditionally stayed sweet.

Richa says much of sports nutrition has borrowed from developed markets, where sweet protein powders became the norm. Chocolate, vanilla and coffee also help mask some of the bitter, metallic and astringent notes that protein ingredients can bring.

rightkind’s answer to this is Coastal Kokum.

At recent sampling events, Richa says it became their standout flavour, stocked out, and even outsold Kesar Kulfi. Consumers were initially surprised by the idea, but many liked how light and refreshing it felt.

One story Richa narrated really stood out to me. A woman who was highly averse to protein drinks tried Coastal Kokum after her husband encouraged her to taste it. She immediately bought a 15-serve pack and said: “This is something I can have every day.”

That line captures the opportunity well.

Savoury protein can feel less like a supplement and more like something that fits naturally into everyday life.

Richa points to familiar Indian drinking occasions such as chaas, solkadhi and sattu. She sees savoury protein fitting into breakfast, a 4pm snack, or even alongside a meal.

Trial also seems important. rightkind offers single-serve sachets, which help people taste the product first and can lead to larger-pack purchases later.

The harder part is making savoury protein work in RTD form.

Taste, chalkiness, off-notes, separation, sedimentation, shelf life and price all need to be solved. Richa estimates that getting around 20g of high-quality protein into an RTD could push the retail price above ₹150, which makes frequent impulse consumption tougher. She also thinks hybrid protein blends could help manage raw-material costs.

For me, this is one of the more interesting white spaces in India’s protein market.

Can savoury protein become tasty, familiar, convenient and affordable enough to become an everyday habit Would you try one?

text:
Most commercial oil brands offer "health" packaged in artificial fragrances, chemical bleaching, and synthetic preservatives. Aayushi Khandelwal exposed their dark secrets, took a recipe from her grandmother, and built a ₹100 Crore organic empire. 

Here is how transparency disrupted a commodity market.

In 2019, Aayushi faced chronic health issues. Heavy prescriptions weren’t effective, but switching to her Nani's traditional food recipes radically improved her health. 

The secret? Her grandmother trusted only pure, unadulterated, traditionally processed ingredients.

This led Aayushi to research the ugly truth about Indian kitchens: the base of our food—cooking oil and ghee—is often heavily processed with artificial flavors, bleaching agents, and toxic preservatives to appear "clean."

In 2020, she and her co-founders launched Anveshan, a farm-to-fork organic food startup dedicated to chemical-free, traditional food production. 

However, they faced an immediate challenge. 

The organic food market was oversaturated, with many brands making similar claims about being "pure" and "natural." Why would customers trust a new brand over established players?

They implemented a genius operational strategy: Radical Traceability. 

Instead of merely labeling their products, they developed a robust supply chain tech infrastructure. 

Each bottle of Anveshan oil came with a custom QR code. When scanned, customers could see the exact farm, location, and date of the raw seeds' harvest.

They didn’t just sell purity; they proved it. 

This trust shifted consumer behavior from skepticism to extreme loyalty. In just 5 years, Anveshan has expanded across 10+ product categories and achieved a ₹100 Crore run rate.

The key takeaway is clear: In a crowded market, shouting louder than competitors doesn’t work. 

True differentiation comes from empowering consumers with control and data. When your supply chain becomes your biggest marketing asset, you not only gain attention—you build a moat.

📊 Why 2027 Could Be Tough for US Markets

🔹 Paul Tudor Jones Issues Warning
Legendary hedge fund manager Paul Tudor Jones believes 2027 could be a very challenging year for US equities, citing a deteriorating market flow picture and rising risks.

🔹 AI IPO Wave Could Increase Share Supply
Potential IPOs from OpenAI, Anthropic, along with recent offerings like SpaceX, could flood the market with new equity issuance, increasing supply and pressuring stock prices.

🔹 End of Buyback Support?
For years, share buybacks and M&A activity reduced the number of shares in circulation, helping support stock prices. Jones believes this trend could reverse as companies raise capital for AI expansion.

🔹 Dot-Com Bubble Comparison
Jones sees similarities to the 1999-2000 dot-com era, when a surge in IPOs and secondary offerings increased market supply before the tech bubble eventually burst.

🔹 Valuation Concerns
He highlighted a widening gap between AI winners and the rest of the market, suggesting many stocks currently offer limited value.

🔹 US Fiscal Deficit Remains a Major Risk
Jones warned that growing government deficits may eventually force higher taxes or spending cuts, creating additional pressure on financial markets.

🔹 Higher Oil Prices Could Hurt Equities
He expects oil prices could rise by $20-$25 per barrel after the US midterm elections, which would increase inflationary pressures and weigh on corporate earnings.

🔹 Bearish Market Stance
Jones indicated he remains cautious and expects the combination of: 
✅ Massive AI-related equity issuance 
✅ Rising fiscal concerns 
✅ Higher oil prices could create a difficult environment for investors in 2027.

The AI revolution may continue creating opportunities, but if OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX and other large tech firms tap public markets simultaneously, the surge in equity supply could become a significant headwind for US stocks, echoing some characteristics of the late-1990s tech boom.

- 𝗔𝗜-𝗗𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆: Focus on AI data infrastructure and proprietary technology platforms like Arya and MindVoice.
- 𝗗𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝘀𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲: Serves multiple key sectors, reducing reliance on any single industry.
- 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝗔𝗰𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗥𝗲𝗰𝗼𝗿𝗱: Demonstrates capability for strategic growth.
- 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗥𝗲𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗵𝗶𝗽𝘀: Includes 22 Fortune 1000 companies.
- 𝗥𝗼𝗯𝘂𝘀𝘁 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: Significant increase in revenue and PAT.

𝗪𝗲𝗮𝗸𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀:

- 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: The top five clients contribute 39.55% and the top ten clients account for 49.66% of revenue, posing a risk if any major client is lost.
- 𝗚𝗲𝗼𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗵𝗶𝗰 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: High revenue dependence on the US and Canada (85.26%).
- 𝗗𝗲𝗯𝘁: While manageable, the company has outstanding borrowings that are being prepaid using IPO proceeds.

𝗩𝗲𝗿𝗱𝗶𝗰𝘁:

Fusion CX Ltd. presents a compelling investment opportunity with its strong global presence, focus on AI, and impressive financial growth. The IPO is priced reasonably, and the GMP indicates positive investor interest. However, investors should be mindful of the customer and geographic concentration risks. The company's strategic expansion into AI and its diversified industry exposure are significant positives. Overall, it appears to be a promising IPO for long-term investors willing to accept the inherent risks.

text:
The Talmud has no modern equivalent. But imagine, for a second, that someone transcribed every oral argument ever heard in the U.S. Supreme Court—1790 to the present—every hypothetical ever suggested, every story told, every flight of reasoning, regardless of whether it ultimately made any legal difference to the court’s decision.

Every brilliant quip made by Oliver Wendell Holmes, every sharp question from Potter Stewart, every wry observation from Ruth Bader Ginsburg or Antonin Scalia, every stalwart and imperious judgment of John Marshall.

Even ill-advised jokes and personal confessions caught on a hot mike.

That transcript wouldn’t be authoritative law—not by a long shot. It wouldn’t look anything like the Constitution or the tax code, for instance. But it would tell you quite a bit about the unique and exquisite constitutional culture of the United States, and the passion with which our democratic nation debated and shaped the interpretations of its most foundational document.

That’s a lot like the Talmud—a record of arguments made by prominent rabbis between the third and sixth centuries over the meaning of the Torah. Its dozens of brick-like volumes contain somewhere between 1.8 and 2.3 million words of hypotheticals and reductio ad absurdums and stories that resolve no legal questions. It is not a legal compendium, and most of its statements are not binding Jewish law. Those who study it do so despite—and really, because of—the fact that it provides few simple answers; tracing the back-and-forth between ancient rabbis is very much the point.

Nonetheless, this influencer offered me the standard conspiracist fare with confidence and gusto. “Zionists who are controlling our planet are all pedophiles and read the Talmud,” was something she told me she had posted on social media. Zionists and “Talmudic Jews” are not the real Jews, she said; they are “Satanists.” Also, they “control our banking system” seek “global domination” and control America on behalf of Israel.

She wanted to be clear, she wasn’t speaking about “all Jews”—lest I think she was antisemitic, presumably.

She declined to give me her thoughts on 9/11, except to say that what “we were told” wasn’t true. But she sounded a lot like your friend. Her brain, wriggling with the same worms.

Leah, it’s been 25 years since 9/11. Twenty-five years, during which we have conducted massive, extraordinarily thorough investigations and collected an immense volume of information. (The 9/11 Commission alone interviewed more than 1,200 people and reviewed more than 2.5 million pages of documents.) If you believe today that Israel somehow convinced 19 Saudi, Emirati, Egyptian, and Lebanese hijackers to participate in a plot orchestrated by their supposed dupes, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and Osama bin Laden—if you believe Israel compelled George W. Bush to go along with it—and that most Americans have been fooled for a quarter century, then you’ve ceased to metabolize information. You’ve ceased to think rationally at all.

2/

text:
⚡🇮🇳 Tamil Nadu Power Mission 2036 — From Expensive Power Purchases TO AN ELECTRICITY-SURPLUS STATE! Please take action.

@TVKVijayHQ @CTR_Nirmalkumar @CMOTamilnadu

A comprehensive 100-Day, 1-Year, 3-Year & 10-Year Power Sector Transformation Proposal

Proposal: Organize a THREE-DAY TAMIL NADU POWER CONCLAVE 2026

Theme: "POWERING TAMIL NADU 2036 — Reliable Power. Affordable Industry. Energy Independence. Net Power Exports."

An important request to our Thalapathy Chief Minister C. Vijay anna, our Electricity Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar, the Energy Department, TNEB and all Tamil Nadu power-sector organizations.

Tamil Nadu is one of India's major industrial and renewable-energy states. Yet rising peak electricity demand, shortfalls in dependable generation, renewable intermittency, expensive emergency purchases and distribution infrastructure challenges are putting pressure on our power system.

Tamil Nadu requires a coordinated, technically sound strategy to address today's shortage and prepare for the next decade.

Our long-term aspiration: Tamil Nadu should meet its electricity requirements reliably, produce competitively priced power and become a net electricity exporter when surplus generation makes commercial sense.

🚨 1. TAMIL NADU'S CURRENT ELECTRICITY CHALLENGES

Reported October 2026 situation:

⚡ Peak demand: approximately 21,700 MW.

⚡ Comparable demand last year: approximately 16,800 MW.

⚡ Increase in demand: approximately 29%.

⚡ Reported shortfall against expected central allocation: approximately 1,800 MW.

⚡ Expected wind contribution: approximately 3,500 MW.

⚡ Actual wind contribution reported by the Minister: approximately 500 MW.

⚡ Emergency purchase quotations: approximately ₹32–₹37 per unit.

⚡ Power-sector outstanding debt reported in the June 2026 white paper: approximately ₹2.47 lakh crore.

These figures require serious attention.

However, the reported central and wind shortfalls must not be confused with Tamil Nadu's final measured net demand-supply deficit. They describe unavailable expected supply, while other generation and purchases may compensate for part of that gap.

The fundamental challenge is not simply total installed capacity. It is dependable power available at the right hour, in the right location and at an affordable cost.

🏭 2. WHY EXPENSIVE MARKET POWER PURCHASES ARE A LONG-TERM RISK

Emergency purchases can be justified to prevent outages during unexpected demand surges.

However, repeated dependence on exceptionally expensive short-term procurement creates serious risks:

❌ Increased operating expenditure for TNPDCL.

❌ Financial pressure on a heavily indebted electricity system.

❌ Reduced predictability of future procurement costs.

❌ Potential pressure on tariffs or government subsidy requirements.

❌ Less financial capacity for new substations, transformers and maintenance.

❌ Greater uncertainty for industries, MSMEs and commercial consumers.

❌ Dependence on power availability and market prices outside Tamil Nadu's control.

Illustrative calculation:

1,500 MW purchased for six hours at ₹35/unit would cost approximately ₹31.5 crore in gross procurement expenditure for that evening.

This is a hypothetical full-dispatch calculation, not the state's verified daily expenditure or financial loss.

The government should publish actual dispatch, average procurement cost, cheaper alternatives considered and the net incremental expenditure.

The answer is not to stop all market purchases. A competitive national electricity market is important.

The answer is to reduce dependence on crisis-driven purchases through an affordable, diversified long-term supply portfolio.

📊 3. ESTABLISH A PUBLIC DEMAND–SUPPLY FORECAST THROUGH 2036

The Energy Department should commission an independently reviewed Tamil Nadu Power Adequacy and Generation Planning Report.

Forecast demand for:

• Summer 2027.

• 2028–2029.

• 2030–2031.

• 2033.

• 2036.

Model hourly electricity demand, not only annual consumption.

Incorporate:

✅ Residential cooling and rising temperatures.

✅ Industrial expansion and manufacturing investments.

✅ Semiconductor, electronics and data-centre demand.

✅ Electric vehicle charging and railway electrification.

✅ Agricultural pumping and water infrastructure.

✅ Wind and solar seasonality.

✅ Central generating-station allocations.

✅ Plant outages and maintenance schedules.

✅ Battery and pumped-storage availability.

✅ Transmission import/export constraints.

Publish scenarios for ordinary weather, prolonged heat, weak wind generation and unexpected plant outages.

Tamil Nadu should plan using MW for peak demand, MWh for energy requirements and a clear reserve-margin and reliability standard.

🏗️ 4. IDENTIFY AND PREPARE DPRs FOR SIX FLAGSHIP POWER INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES

I propose that the state establish a technical steering committee within 15 days and initiate feasibility work on at least three priority opportunities within 90 days.

PROJECT A — 1,600 MW NEW FIRM GENERATION OPPORTUNITY

Assess a potential 2 × 800 MW flexible, high-efficiency thermal or other firm-generation development, preferably at suitable existing industrial or power-generation sites.

Examine coal and water availability, fuel costs, emissions, environmental impacts, financing, plant flexibility and grid connection before selecting technology or location.

Invite NTPC, NLC India, Adani Power, Tata Power, JSW Energy and other qualified generators to participate through a transparent process.

PROJECT B — 2,000–3,000 MW WIND–SOLAR HYBRID DEVELOPMENT

Identify resource-rich locations with suitable grid connectivity for utility-scale hybrid projects.

Develop competitively bid opportunities combining solar, wind, forecasting and storage.

Prioritize land and transmission readiness before issuing large tenders.

PROJECT C — 500 MW / 2,000 MWh BATTERY STORAGE PROGRAMME

Study strategically located battery systems capable of delivering 500 MW for four hours.

Prioritize substations facing major evening peaks, renewable curtailment or congestion.

Assess lifecycle costs, safety standards, recycling, fire protection and competitive tenders.

Storage shifts energy between hours. It does not create primary electricity.

PROJECT D — WIND TURBINE REPOWERING MISSION

Review 1,000–2,000 MW of older wind-project capacity for repowering potential.

Tamil Nadu has long-established wind corridors around Coimbatore, Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Tenkasi and Kanyakumari regions.

Explore replacing ageing low-capacity turbines with modern machines, where economically and environmentally viable.

Work with existing wind owners, manufacturers, investors and the National Institute of Wind Energy.

PROJECT E — PUMPED HYDRO & WATER-BASED ENERGY STORAGE

Expedite the remaining work, testing and safe commissioning of the 500 MW Kundah Pumped Storage Project, subject to its current technical status and regulatory requirements.

Undertake a fresh feasibility and environmental review of the previously proposed 2,000 MW Sillahalla Pumped Storage Project.

Study additional off-stream or closed-loop pumped storage where land, water and ecological conditions are suitable.

Avoid treating pumped storage as new net energy generation: it stores surplus energy for use during peak hours.

PROJECT F — INDUSTRIAL SOLAR & DISTRIBUTED ENERGY PARKS

Prepare a proposed 1,000–2,000 MW pipeline of industrial rooftop solar, group-captive renewable systems and suitably located distributed energy installations.

Target manufacturing clusters in Coimbatore, Tiruppur, Erode, Salem, Hosur, Sriperumbudur, Chennai, Ranipet and Thoothukudi.

Create standard project templates and simplified approvals for MSMEs.

Important: These are proposed project-development opportunities, not sanctioned projects, confirmed sites or guaranteed new capacity. All require feasibility studies, financial assessment and applicable regulatory approvals.

☢️ 5. NUCLEAR POWER — EXPAND LONG-TERM FIRM ENERGY SUPPLY

Tamil Nadu already hosts nationally significant nuclear infrastructure.

Kudankulam:

✅ Units 1 and 2: 2 × 1,000 MW operational.

✅ Units 3–6: four additional 1,000 MW reactors in the construction pipeline.

Request the Department of Atomic Energy and NPCIL to publish independently validated commissioning milestones, Tamil Nadu's expected power allocation, transmission readiness and outstanding requirements.

Kalpakkam:

The 500 MW Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor achieved first criticality in April 2026.

First criticality is not equivalent to full commercial electricity generation.

Coordinate with BHAVINI, NPCIL, DAE and AERB on commissioning progress, safety requirements and future power availability.

Examine longer-term nuclear expansion opportunities only through the Centre-led siting, public consultation, environmental and nuclear safety approval processes.

Nuclear expansion is a multi-year national infrastructure undertaking, not an immediate substitute for emergency procurement.

💧 6. HYDROPOWER & PUMPED STORAGE — TAMIL NADU'S STRATEGIC OPPORTUNITY

Hydropower and pumped storage should be important components of long-term planning.

Review:

• Kundah Pumped Storage Project.

• Sillahalla feasibility and environmental status.

• Existing hydropower station modernization.

• Pumped-storage opportunities involving suitable existing reservoirs.

• Off-stream storage with limited ecological disturbance.

• Better hydrological forecasting and reservoir coordination.

Work with CEA, NHPC, THDC India, SJVN and experienced private hydro developers.

All projects must consider water availability, biodiversity, land rights, communities, project costs and climate risks.

☀️ 7. AGGRESSIVELY ACCELERATE ROOFTOP SOLAR FOR 365 DAYS

Tamil Nadu already offers combined Central and State subsidies of up to ₹1 lakh for eligible residential 3 kW installations.

The announced target is one lakh homes by March 2027.

I suggest a 365-day execution mission:

✅ District-level solar enrollment and awareness camps.

✅ Faster net-metering and commissioning.

✅ Transparent empanelled-vendor pricing and quality checks.

✅ Bank financing and simplified consumer support.

✅ Solar installations at government schools, hospitals, offices and public buildings.

✅ Separate commercially viable solutions for MSMEs, factories and warehouses.

✅ Agricultural solar-pump programs through eligible national schemes.

✅ Public reporting of applications, installed systems, pending approvals and actual generation.

Solar must be planned alongside evening storage and grid upgrades.

The success metric should be useful electricity generated and consumer savings, not installation announcements alone.

🏭 8. REDUCE ELECTRICITY COST PRESSURE ON INDUSTRIES & MSMEs

Tamil Nadu's industrial competitiveness depends partly on electricity price and reliability.

Priority sectors include:

• Tiruppur textiles and garment exporters.

• Coimbatore pumps, foundries and engineering units.

• Erode textile and food-processing industries.

• Hosur automobiles, electronics and precision manufacturing.

• Chennai automotive, electronics, IT and logistics.

• Sivakasi manufacturing clusters.

• Rice mills, cold-storage facilities and agricultural processors.

Proposed measures:

✅ Commission a comparative industrial electricity tariff study with competing manufacturing states.

✅ Review demand charges, peak-hour charges, open-access charges and power-quality costs.

✅ Introduce time-bound, funded relief for qualifying MSMEs if affordability and public finances permit.

✅ Facilitate rooftop, group-captive and renewable open-access projects.

✅ Expand energy-efficiency financing and motor-efficiency upgrades.

✅ Develop reliable industrial feeders with measurable power-quality standards.

✅ Study competitively priced power-supply arrangements for new industrial parks.

Tariff revisions should follow TNERC's lawful regulatory process and protect the financial sustainability of the power utility.

Affordable and reliable electricity supports manufacturing competitiveness, exports, employment and investment.

🔧 9. MODERNIZE TNEB, TNPDCL, TNPGCL, TNGECL & TANTRANSCO

Modernization must cover the complete electricity value chain.

Generation — TNPGCL:

Improve thermal plant availability, outage planning, preventive maintenance, fuel handling and project execution.

Renewables — TNGECL/TEDA:

Accelerate viable renewable and storage projects with transparent approvals and grid integration.

Distribution — TNPDCL:

Prioritize transformer replacement, feeder upgrades, loss reduction, better billing, faster connection approvals and outage restoration.

Transmission — TANTRANSCO:

Accelerate substations and transmission capacity in growing industrial and renewable-energy corridors.

Holding and financial coordination — TNEB Limited:

Strengthen financial reporting, utility accountability, long-term procurement planning and the implementation of the existing restructuring framework.

The June 2026 white paper already identified approximately ₹49,532 crore of infrastructure measures, including 469 substations and major recruitment requirements.

Publish a project-by-project dashboard showing:

• Sanctioned projects versus completed projects.

• Capital expenditure and cost overruns.

• Feeder reliability and transformer failures.

• Aggregate technical and commercial losses.

• Plant availability and generation performance.

• Staffing vacancies and safety performance.

• Consumer complaints and resolution times.

• Debt, interest costs and subsidy payments.

Modernization must involve engineers, utility employees, trade unions, regulators and consumers.

Smart-metering and public-private proposals require transparent contracts, cybersecurity protection, affordability safeguards and meaningful consultation.

🇮🇳 10. REQUEST CENTRAL GOVERNMENT COOPERATION

I request the Tamil Nadu Government to organize a formal Energy Cooperation Meeting in New Delhi with the Union Ministry of Power, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, CEA, NTPC, NLC India, POWERGRID, NPCIL and relevant financing institutions.

Specific agenda:

1️⃣ Address verified central generating-station allocation gaps and outage coordination.

2️⃣ Review Neyveli/NLC supply availability and maintenance schedules.

3️⃣ Seek technical support for a state resource-adequacy plan.

4️⃣ Accelerate transmission corridors and interregional electricity exchange.

5️⃣ Coordinate Kundah pumped storage, other suitable hydro projects and energy-storage approvals.

6️⃣ Review nuclear project commissioning and future allocations.

7️⃣ Explore financing support through PFC, REC, IREDA and eligible Union schemes.

8️⃣ Maximize Tamil Nadu's participation in PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and national renewable initiatives.

9️⃣ Consider competitively priced long-term central-sector and interstate power arrangements.

🔟 Develop a transparent mechanism for Tamil Nadu to export economically viable surplus electricity.

Centre–State coordination can reduce project delays, improve reliability and support lower-cost electricity procurement.

🏛️ 11. ORGANIZE A THREE-DAY TAMIL NADU POWER CONCLAVE 2026

Theme: POWERING TAMIL NADU 2036

Subtitle: Generation | Grid Modernization | Energy Storage | Industrial Competitiveness | Investment

Proposed venue: Chennai.

Proposed participation: senior policymakers, generating companies, utility chief engineers, investors, financial institutions, regulators, researchers, industries, MSMEs, journalists, consumer organizations, labour representatives and civil society.

DAY 1 — ELECTRICITY REALITY & DEMAND–SUPPLY PLANNING
Morning:

• Inauguration and presentation of the current electricity situation.

• Technical review of October demand, central allocations, wind variability and peak procurement.

• Publication of an hour-by-hour supply and demand assessment.

Afternoon:

• Forecasts for 2027, 2030 and 2036.

• Existing plant availability, fuel security and maintenance.

• Utility finances, debt, tariffs, outages and manpower.

• Expert session on climate, cooling demand and changing weather patterns.

Day 1 Deliverable: Agreed baseline assumptions and a publicly documented Power Adequacy Study.

DAY 2 — POWER PROJECTS & INVESTMENT SUMMIT

Invite leading thermal, hydro, nuclear, solar, wind, battery and hybrid-energy stakeholders.

Conduct dedicated investment sessions for:

⚡ Firm generation and brownfield modernization.

☀️ Utility-scale and rooftop solar.

🌬️ Wind repowering and hybrid systems.

💧 Pumped storage and hydropower.

🔋 Battery storage and grid flexibility.

☢️ Nuclear project coordination.

🏭 Industrial and MSME energy solutions.

🌐 Transmission investment and interstate trading.

Allow developers and technical experts to submit project concepts and expressions of interest.

Day 2 Deliverable: A screened investment opportunity register and priority DPR preparation pipeline.

DAY 3 — IMPLEMENTATION, UTILITY REFORMS & PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY

Morning:

• TNEB/TNPDCL/TNPGCL/TNGECL/TANTRANSCO modernization workshops.

• Distribution infrastructure and workforce planning.

• Regulatory and power-tariff consultations.

• Central funding and private investment mechanisms.

Afternoon:

• Technical recommendations and project ownership.

• 100-day implementation calendar.

• One-year and three-year milestones.

• Ten-year power development vision.

• Press conference with public questions.

Day 3 Deliverable: Publication of the Tamil Nadu Power Mission 2036 Action Charter, with project owners, study budgets, deadlines and accountability.

🏢 12. INVITE 20 MAJOR POWER GENERATION COMPANIES IN INDIA

Proposed shortlist of significant public-sector and private-sector electricity generators, not a strict installed-capacity ranking:

Participation or project investment should not be assumed before formal invitations and commercial discussions.

🌞 13. INVITE 10 MAJOR SOLAR & RENEWABLE DEVELOPERS
Adani Green Energy

ReNew

Also invite relevant equipment and technology suppliers such as BHEL, L&T, Suzlon, Inox Wind, Waaree Energies, Vikram Solar, Siemens Energy, Hitachi Energy and battery manufacturers.
Ensure fair and open competitive opportunities for startups and smaller developers alongside established groups.

👥 14. KEY CENTRAL GOVERNMENT LEADERS & INSTITUTIONS TO INVITE
Union Government — named contacts, without X tags:

🇮🇳 Shri Manohar Lal — Union Minister of Power.

🇮🇳 Shri Shripad Yesso Naik — Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy.

🇮🇳 Shri Pankaj Agarwal — Secretary, Ministry of Power, as listed in the government directory.

Institutional representation:

Ministry of Power, MNRE, CEA, GRID-INDIA, POWERGRID, NTPC, NLC India, NHPC, NPCIL, BHAVINI, AERB, CERC, PFC, REC, IREDA, SECI, BHEL and the Southern Regional Power Committee.

Tamil Nadu participation should include senior officials from Energy, Finance, Industries and Environment; all relevant power utilities; TNERC; chief engineers; district representatives; TIDCO/SIPCOT; industrial bodies such as CII, FICCI, CODISSIA, SIEMA and TANSTIA; academic experts from IIT Madras, Anna University and NIT Tiruchirappalli; utility employee organizations; journalists; and independent consumer representatives.

📅 15. PROPOSED DELIVERY ROADMAP

FIRST 30 DAYS

✅ Establish a Power Mission steering committee and independent technical advisory group.

✅ Release a reconciled demand–supply and procurement data dashboard.

✅ Publish the status of existing generation projects.

✅ Invite national and private-sector technical participation.

✅ Announce the Power Conclave.

FIRST 90–120 DAYS

✅ Complete the three-day Power Conclave.

✅ Initiate at least three technically prioritized DPRs/feasibility packages.

✅ Review pending generation and transmission project bottlenecks.

✅ Produce a summer 2027 electricity adequacy and procurement plan.

✅ Review industrial tariff competitiveness and distribution reliability.

✅ Publish the official Power Mission 2036 Action Charter.

WITHIN ONE YEAR

✅ Deliver the published rooftop solar targets.

✅ Commission competitively selected storage and renewable projects where feasible.

✅ Improve grid reliability and reduce costly emergency procurement exposure.

✅ Begin prioritized transmission and distribution modernization.

WITHIN THREE YEARS

✅ Expand dependable generation and storage availability.

✅ Deliver staged grid and substation improvements.

✅ Establish transparent industrial power competitiveness metrics.

✅ Advance hydro, renewable and eligible firm-generation projects.

✅ Strengthen financial sustainability across the electricity utilities.

TEN-YEAR VISION — 2036

🎯 Reliable electricity supply through seasonal demand peaks.

🎯 Competitive power costs for industry, MSMEs and households.

🎯 A diversified generation system combining renewables, firm power and storage.

🎯 Financially sustainable, professionally managed power utilities.

🎯 A modern, resilient electricity grid.

🎯 Commercially viable surplus generation and net power exports over time.

Net electricity exports should be measured against total imports over defined periods, with peak-hour reliability separately verified.

📢 16. WEEKLY ELECTRICITY PERFORMANCE REPORT

Hon'ble Electricity Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar:

Please consider a fixed weekly professional press briefing with a government-branded backdrop, clear presentation screens, data charts, published documents and a structured media Q&A.

Publish:

• Peak demand and actual generation.

• Power purchased and average cost.

• Available firm capacity and reserve margins.

• Wind, solar, hydro and thermal output.

• State-wise and central supply arrangements.

• Project milestones, commissioning progress and delays.

• District-wise outage and restoration performance.

• Substation upgrades, manpower and maintenance progress.

• Renewable applications and commissioning statistics.

Transparency will help industries, investors, journalists and the public assess actual progress.

🇮🇳 CONCLUDING REQUEST TO HON'BLE CM VIJAY

Electricity is not merely a utility service. It is foundational infrastructure for Tamil Nadu's manufacturing economy, employment, agriculture, services, public welfare and long-term prosperity.

The next decade requires coordinated investments in dependable generation, clean energy, storage, nuclear and hydro development, grid modernization, industrial competitiveness and disciplined utility management.

My central request: Organize the three-day Tamil Nadu Power Conclave, commission a credible Power Mission 2036 roadmap, and begin technically justified DPRs within the next 90 days.

Let the final plan be evidence-based, financially responsible, environmentally sound and publicly accountable.

AFFORDABLE POWER. RELIABLE SUPPLY. STRONGER INDUSTRIES. ENERGY SECURITY.

After Typhoon Odette in 2021, Marcos and Sara Duterte brought aid to Siargao and other devastated areas. 

That included cash, rice, solar panels, 10 sets of water bucket filters, and water purifier systems that could produce 180 gallons of clean water per hour.

Sara was part of it. They handed over practical tools that turned available water into safe drinking water for communities that had none.

Sara’s “wala na” and info drive does not.

🚨 2. NEXT 90–120 DAYS — EMERGENCY PROCUREMENT & FOOD PRICE STABILIZATION

text:
The Party and the Country: Kenyan Millennials & Their Political Responsibility

Nairobians have always loved a good party.

And Nairobi throws the best parties in Africa.

Nairobi nightclubs are so big, man. One Quiver could host the entire Nairobi Agricultural Show, with DS Njoroge's International Disco, the prize bulls, the tractors and the presidential pavilion, and still have room for three Gikomba markets, complete with escape lanes for the routine fire.

Every few years, the city reinvents its nightlife. One party district dies and another resurrects, like clockwork. Westlands. The CBD. Lang'ata. Kilimani. Mombasa Road. The outskirts. Wherever Nairobi expands, somebody arrives with a sound system before the sewer line.

I have been part of these nightly rendezvous for two decades, chronicling the proceedings as a newspaper journalist, a blogger, and later in my books and on social media. Been there, done that, got the T-shirt, and possibly an illegitimate child out there. Who knows? Nairobi keeps some of its own records.

So this is a confession as much as a complaint.

No city drinks like Nairobi, either. Aluta drinking could only be a Nairobi invention, and we cannot even blame Covid-19 for it. We were treating Monday as a malicious rumour long before the pandemic.

This past weekend, two nostalgia-fuelled shindigs took place in Nairobi, and both were wildly successful.

The first was Fred Obachi Machoka's 50th anniversary as an entertainer. His jamboree brought together rumba enthusiasts from four generations: boomers, Gen Xers, millennials and Gen Zs. Three continental icons, Koffi Olomide, Mama Mbilia Bel and Sam Fan Thomas, were in the house, alongside younger cats like Alicios Theluji and a host of local acts who entertained folks way into the night. Koffi Olomide's shenanigans cannot take away the success of the event.

The second was the Millennial Cookout.

2026 has been the year of nostalgia. In August, Nameless delivered a flawless 25th anniversary in music, which was essentially a millennial celebration, seeing as Nameless is the godfather of Kapuka and Genge, the soundtrack of our lives. Redsan had his event. There have been well-attended brunch karaoke sessions (read: drunken brunches) and all manner of themed parties. It is like millennials cannot catch a break. Folks keep inventing nostalgic reasons for us to part with our money and buy back our youth, this time with a booking fee.

Our old songs have become a pension scheme for everybody except us.

Seeing Nonini perform Kadhaa at the Millennial Cookout warmed my heart bigly, because that song is the ultimate millennial sherehe anthem. A few bars and you remember who you were, whom you fancied, and the extraordinary confidence with which you approached a future you had done absolutely nothing to prepare for.

Less talked about is the year the song came out, where Kenya was then, what it represented, and whether we have lived up to the dreams it called us to celebrate. That is a subject for future correspondence. For now, allow me to offer a lament.

We rarely address why millennials party so hard.

Some of it is simple. The music is good, the company is familiar, and adulthood has become an elaborate collection of invoices. Sometimes you need a few hours in which nobody calls you about school fees, your mother's medication or a contribution to a funeral committee.

But there is history here. We came of age when Moi was voted out. Kibaki liberalised the country, with all that FM station madness and an economic boom that made it possible for millennials to get jobs, following the exponential expansion of university education in the decade to 2015. By the time we were young men and women, the economy was stronger and ARVs had restored dignity to those living with HIV. Those were the two things that had slowed Kenya down in the 1990s. Millennials, thus, could play risky, irresponsible games. Now we watch Gen Z take it a step further.

Millennials were also the last generation to receive what I can call a proper education, in a very aspirational and commercial sense. We attended good academies, excelled in KCPE and KCSE, and joined public and private universities at the peak of their commercial success, when enrolment and business were booming. After university, many walked into decent jobs, some earning six figures before their 26th birthday. Therefore, we knew how to dream. A job. A car. A house somewhere beyond the city. Perhaps a plot whose location required three phone calls and the assistance of a man called Maina.

That dream built Nairobi's satellite towns. Ruiru, Juja and the entire Thika Road and its bypasses. Utawala, Syokimau, Mlolongo, Kitengela and Athi River. Rongai, Ngong and its many parts, Kiserian, all the way to Thogoto. All of them expanded in the Kibaki years, which spilt into the early years of the Uhuru administration, before Uhuru borrowed all the money, externally and internally, and froze that exponential growth.

By the time Uhuru Kenyatta took over in 2013, older millennials were rampaging around town, the true Cheers Baba generation. We rarely compare Uhuru's fiscal recklessness, all that borrowing that sank the nation into debt, with the individual recklessness of that decade. All those rugby matches, Safari Rallies and non-stop partying, and the later unravelling of the Cheers Baba generation's social lives. Few marriages in that cohort survived. Some of us mistook a good weekend for evidence that life was going well. Then Monday arrived with the country attached.

Younger millennials were not as lucky. Those graduating from 2013 onwards did not inherit the same advantages, despite being sold the same promises of what education bestows on an individual. And they live in a very exhibitionist city. We all have classmates who got good jobs, tenders, deals, crime and what have you, and they never hesitate to show us what they got. You, meanwhile, are told to be patient and trust the process. The process has stopped answering your calls. These things have a way of eating into your psyche, which is why this city revels in schadenfreude whenever a formerly proud and showy individual is humbled.

So we party to celebrate. We party to forget. We party because, for one night, the DJ returns us to a time when our prospects looked better than our knees do now. I understand it. I have bought the ticket. Understanding our exhaustion, however, does not release us from our responsibilities.

The 2024 Gen Z demonstrations were, in truth, two generations coming together to fight diminished opportunities. Millennials born in the late 1980s and the 1990s, as well as older Gen Zs, have been on the receiving end of terrible governance under Uhuru Kenyatta and his successor. Yet we cannot keep outsourcing the hardest political work to people younger than us while we supply solidarity from a table with an ice bucket. We are old enough now to carry more of the burden.

But my focus is on millennials, and here is where I want to call them out.

In truth, I am not one of those people who say the middle class doesn't vote and therefore deserves to be screwed. That is nonsense. If anything, millennials are deeply involved in this country's politics. I vote in Starehe, at South B Primary School to be precise, and there is no hood more middle-class than South B. Even though a huge section of that station's electorate comes from down the Mukuru valley, I have voted there three times and seen plenty of middle-class voting.

I have also worked for and with NGOs and other institutions headed or run by millennials, and I have seen the amount of work they put in to keep the country running. In healthcare, so many dedicated millennial women fight for causes the government should take care of. Because most of the funding comes from outside and volunteers do the work, the state neglects them. In education, I have seen millennials lobby Parliament and the relevant government bodies relentlessly. Little of this work gets covered, because the media died too, killed by our overreliance on social media and by what Uhuru Kenyatta did to the press.

What we often forget to say is that learned millennials are outnumbered three to one. For every university graduate, there are three or four Kenyans who will never see the inside of a college or get any form of tertiary education, and all votes are equal. If our ideas cannot speak to someone who never attended university, we have failed to persuade. We will not fix Kenya from a WhatsApp group of people who went to good schools and agree that everyone else is the problem.

Now, I am not saying graduates are better than non-graduates. Far from it. Graduates are responsible for some of the worst corruption scandals that have impoverished this country. They can explain procurement law beautifully while stealing the hospital.

Still, I think millennials are the first generation equipped with the knowledge and values to fix the country. We are teachers, doctors, engineers, lawyers, journalists, business owners, public servants and parents. We have the skills, the networks and access to information our parents could scarcely imagine. We understand the machinery, and we have enough years ahead of us to live with the consequences of leaving it broken. Millennials in Parliament have not demonstrated this, and defending them is hard. But hear me out.

The president, for all his hard work and his rush to expand our road network, housing and refineries, lacks one fundamental thing necessary for growth, both as an individual and collectively for his generation. He talks about Kenya becoming the next Singapore, yet he rarely talks about the values of the Singaporean and other Asian Tiger leaders who turned their countries around. In August 2016, long before he joined Ruto, David Ndii wrote a very good column in the Daily Nation titled "Lessons from Asian tigers that you won't hear from political leaders." He concluded that nobody has figured out why their leaders chose to enrich their countries, while Africa's leaders enriched themselves.

So I want to call out millennials on their values.

For nearly five decades, this country has been dysfunctional. Planning collapsed. Education collapsed. Healthcare collapsed. Security collapsed. The rot did not start with Ruto, or Uhuru, or even Kibaki, but it has accelerated with each passing administration. Under Ruto, one can argue that we have no functional education system, no functional healthcare system and no functional transport system, especially in Nairobi and our ever-growing towns. Boda boda is not a transport strategy, and it is a poor way of employing young men. As for security, goons have more say than our security agencies.

We do have a semblance of a functional country, I must say. The whole thing has not collapsed. We are simply paying too much for what should ideally be free or affordable.

The temporary solution was to go private. Private academies for education. Private hospitals for healthcare. Private security for our homes and estates. Everyone in Kenya wants to make it, move to Karen or Runda and leave everyone behind. Put the children in a private school. Buy medical cover. Hire a guard. Install a tank. Add a generator. Then call the resulting collection of emergency arrangements a lifestyle. This is the worst legacy of colonialism. We have the worst class structure.

Except that we cannot afford it, and not for long. And no, I am not some rabid communist calling for socialism. Your SUV still needs a usable road. Your borehole still needs a viable water table. Your lovely house still needs somewhere for the sewage to go. We have built our homes, yet nothing stops your neighbour from erecting an ugly flat as the population expands. In Kamulu, people have to build private roads. In Kitengela, developers pour raw sewage onto the road when it rains. One medical condition sends a family into poverty. Eventually, the country climbs over your perimeter wall.

And the values question applies to us, too. If our objection to corruption lasts only until a friend gets a tender, we have very little to offer. If we demand accountability from another community's politician and invent excuses for our own, we are rehearsing the same old politics with newer phones. Our values have to survive contact with an opportunity to benefit.

Meanwhile, we are overwhelmed with responsibilities. We are the sandwich generation, taking care of our parents and our young ones at the same time. Well-to-do millennials are burdened by black tax. The rest are battling stalled mobility, watching their dreams die right before their eyes.

Some of the big problems, like Nairobi traffic, sewerage for our growing populations, employment and social welfare, will need hard conversations, and Gen Xers and older folks are in no mood for them. I saw Ruto launch a national conversation on what should succeed Vision 2030. Not to dismiss Anyang' Nyong'o and the professors who drafted the proposal, but we need to look inward and think for ourselves as millennials.

In the coming decade, the party and the partying will have to stop, one way or another, and we must reckon with what to do with our lives. We can choose to keep partying, and this is no virtue signalling, or we can choose to be more deliberate.

We should bring to these questions the organisational genius we bring to sherehe. We find venues, raise money, coordinate transport, sell tickets and bring thousands of people together. A millennial can organise a destination birthday for fourteen people with incompatible budgets and three unresolved affairs. Surely a ward meeting is within our capabilities.

Start small, at the community level. Know your representatives and what they are responsible for. Follow the county budget. Attend public participation meetings and ask questions that demand answers. Organise around the school, the drainage, the clinic, the road. Seek elective positions. Hold those elected accountable. Bring up good ideas for the problems we will face. And keep at it after the hashtags fade, because a country is repaired through work that is repetitive, inconvenient and spectacularly unsuitable for Instagram.

This is how a sandwich generation lessens its burdens. A reliable public school is a financial reprieve. A functioning public hospital protects a family's savings. Affordable transport gives people back money and time. Paying over Sh50,000 to a private school because you live in Kitengela, a town of well over 150,000 people with hardly a public school worth the name, is not normal. We went through ordinary schools, and we turned out normal, if a little traumatised.

Yes, we are tired. That is precisely why this matters. We cannot leave our children our playlists and a bigger collection of problems, and we cannot keep asking Gen Z to take all the risks while we wait to see how things turn out. We have reached the age where "someone should do something" increasingly means us. That is the political responsibility of Kenyan millennials.

So let Nonini sing Kadhaa. Sing along. Enjoy yourself. But also listen to Nonini's new jam with Kitu Sewer, Michele and Kacha. Then let us give our children a country they will want to remember, too.

text:
Japan may believe it understands China well enough to judge that a conflict over Taiwan is not imminent. That could make the current moment look like an opportunity: internationalize the Taiwan issue, strengthen its position within the U.S. alliance, rally domestic support, and accelerate its military buildup under the banner of turning Japan into a “normal country.”

There is a political logic behind this.

Japan’s conservative right has long sought to loosen the constraints of its postwar security framework and expand the country’s military role. A harder line on Taiwan can help advance that agenda, justify greater military capabilities, and strengthen Japan’s strategic importance to Washington.

Tokyo may not want to break away from the United States; it may instead want to become a more powerful ally, with greater influence over regional security and more room to pursue its own interests.

Japan’s history also offers a relevant warning. From the Russo-Japanese War to the attack on Pearl Harbor, Japanese leaders have, at critical moments, been willing to take enormous strategic risks in the hope of changing their country’s position.

These episodes do not mean Japan will repeat the past, but they illustrate a recurring possibility: when leaders believe the strategic window may close, they may choose to gamble rather than accept the status quo.

Tokyo may be making a similar calculation today. If its leaders believe a conflict over Taiwan is not imminent, they may see an opportunity to strengthen Japan’s military position and strategic autonomy now, while assuming that the most serious costs can be avoided.

The question is whether that confidence is justified.

2003年前后，胡锦涛提出"马六甲困境"：中国约八成的进口石油要经过马六甲海峡，而美国海军随时可以在那里掐住中国的脖子。此后二十年，这个词在西方战略界一直被当成中国的阿喀琉斯之踵。

中国的替代方案，握在中国自己手里: 管道穿过的是友好邻国，海军是自己的。

日本的替代方案，全都握在别人手里:
绕行的印尼海峡——要靠印尼的中立和许可。 
护航的海军——要靠美国，而美国正在中东流血、在为柴油价格求普京、在跟中国开峰会。 
离日本最近的能源——萨哈林，在俄罗斯手里。日俄交恶比中日交恶更加严重。

日本最大的问题就是：战后七十年战略外包，导致自主思考退化。
中国把它当成自己必须尽快解决的问题，于是修了二十年管道。
日本把它当成美国会替它解决的问题——美国海军会永远保持海上航线畅通——于是什么都没修。

高市说台湾有事，就是日本有事，意思是：台湾出事，日本会参与防卫。
张地图说了同一句话，但意思不一样：台湾出事，日本会被勒住死，不管它参不参与。

而更要命的是如果按高市的说法，日本把台湾有事视为"存立危机事态"、成为交战方，那它的航线就不再是附带损伤，而是正当目标。

中国根本不需要去封马六甲。它只需要让南海和菲律宾海变得危险就够了——而那正是日本油轮唯一能走的路。

高市那句话，把日本从"可能被波及"推到了"必须被瞄准"。

要するに、タンカーマンとしては遠いし危ないし、こんなよく分かんねぇ海域を通りたくねぇってことです。

🇾🇪|Taiz: Ansar Allah Opens the Road to Aden

And The Mercenaries Flee, the Puppet Government Collapses

October 14, 2026 | Taiz

The besieged Saudi-backed mercenaries trapped in Jabal Han and the Sharab junction on the western front of Taiz have been given a choice. They chose to run.

Ansar Allah has allowed the encircled forces to withdraw from their positions and leave the city, heading toward the temporary capital of Aden. This is not a military defeat in the conventional sense. It is a strategic and moral victory that exposes the rot at the heart of the Saudi-led coalition and the so-called "legitimate government" it props up.

💥 The Collapse of the Western Front

For weeks, the Saudi-backed factions, the Islah Party militias, the mercenaries paid in riyals to kill Yemenis have been crumbling. The western front of Taiz, anchored by the strategic highlands of Jabal Han and the Sharab junction, was their last line of defense against the advancing forces of Sana'a. These positions overlooked the transport route connecting Taiz to Al-Turbah and Aden the lifeline that kept the puppet government's forces supplied.

That lifeline is now severed. On October 4, Ansar Allah forces took Al-Turbah, the administrative center of Al-Shamayateen District, cutting the main supply route between Taiz and Aden. The Saudi-backed forces fled in disarray over 20 military vehicles and five trucks loaded with weapons and ammunition were seen withdrawing toward the Sharjab road and from there to the Tur Al-Bahah area of Lahij. Some fled via the Al-Sihi–Hazaz and Al-Zariqa routes. The collapse was described as "unprecedented".

By October 13, Ansar Allah forces had reached the southern entrance of Taiz, completing the encirclement of the city. They had already positioned themselves at the eastern and western approaches.

📜 The "Safe Passage" That Exposes the Puppet Government

Now Ansar Allah has done what the puppet government's Western masters never would: it chose to prevent bloodshed.

A local source told Lebanon's al-Akhbar daily that Yemeni authorities were seeking to prevent bloodshed by allowing the Riyadh-aligned troops to leave the city under guarantees of safe passage. The general amnesty remains available to everyone except those who have "committed crimes and were subject to private legal claims and legal accountability".

Ansar Allah's political bureau member, Hezam Al-Asad, confirmed that Yemeni forces did not cut the road between Taiz and Aden they secured it. This is the distinction the Western media will never make: Ansar Allah is not interested in starving the people of Taiz. It is interested in liberating them. The roads are open. The siege is on the mercenaries, not the civilians.

And what have the mercenaries done? They have taken the offer and run. Several military, political, and party leaders have already left Taiz with the green light from Ansar Allah, under the protection of its forces, arriving in Aden and Ma'rib. The Saudi-backed forces are not fighting for Taiz. They are fighting for their own escape. The moment the road to Aden was opened, they took it.

🎯 The Saudi Regime Presses Them to Fight On

While the mercenaries flee, Saudi Arabia is pressing them to stay and die. Al-Akhbar reported that Riyadh is urging the remaining forces to fight on. The Saudis are not on the front lines. They are not in Taiz. They are not in Jabal Han. They are in Riyadh, sipping tea, while their paid proxies are told to sacrifice themselves for a war that serves Washington and Tel Aviv, not the people of Yemen.

The "legitimate government" in Aden the one the United Nations recognizes, the one the United States funds, the one that sits in luxury hotels while Yemeni children starve has said nothing about the safe passage. It has said nothing about the amnesty. It has said nothing about the fact that its own forces are abandoning their posts and fleeing to Aden. It cannot say anything, because to acknowledge the truth would be to admit that its entire claim to legitimacy is a fiction. The puppet government does not govern. It occupies. And when the occupation collapses, it runs.

⚔️ The Humanitarian Catastrophe That Was Always a Lie

For years, the Western media has parroted the line that Ansar Allah's siege of Taiz is a "humanitarian disaster." The Saudi-backed health ministry warned of a "humanitarian catastrophe" in the city, with medicine, medical equipment, and fuel "on the verge of running out". The New Arab ran headlines about Taiz facing a "humanitarian disaster as Houthis tighten siege".

But if Taiz is facing a humanitarian catastrophe, who is responsible? The Saudi-led coalition has bombed Yemen for twelve years. It has imposed a naval and air blockade. It has killed hundreds of thousands of Yemenis. It has created the conditions for famine, cholera, and disease. Ansar Allah did not create the catastrophe in Taiz. The Saudi regime did. And now Ansar Allah is doing what the Saudi regime never did: opening the roads, allowing safe passage, and preventing bloodshed.

The mercenaries in Taiz were not defending the city. They were holding it hostage. They were using the civilian population as human shields, knowing that Ansar Allah would hesitate to attack a city full of civilians. Ansar Allah called their bluff. It encircled the city, cut the supply lines, and offered the mercenaries a choice: leave or die. They left.

🔻 The Road to Aden Is Open. The Road to Liberation Is Clear.

The fall of Taiz is not just a military victory. It is a political earthquake. Taiz is Yemen's third-largest city, the most populous in the governorate, and a strategic hub linking the highlands to the south. Its liberation or its peaceful handover would be the most significant gain for Sana'a since the war began.

The mercenaries who fled to Aden are not safe. Aden is the "temporary capital" of a government that does not control its own territory. It is a city riddled with infighting, where the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council fights the Saudi-backed Islah Party for control of the port and the oil facilities. The mercenaries who fled Taiz are fleeing into another trap, another battlefield, another proxy war between masters who see Yemen only as a chessboard.

The people of Taiz, meanwhile, are watching. They have watched the Saudi-backed forces loot, extort, and oppress them for years. They have watched the "legitimate government" do nothing for them. They have watched the Western media ignore their suffering while amplifying every Israeli claim about Gaza. And now they are watching Ansar Allah open the roads, offer amnesty, and allow the mercenaries to leave without a fight.

The contrast could not be starker. The Saudi regime bombs. Ansar Allah builds. The puppet government flees. Ansar Allah stays. The West funds the mercenaries. The resistance protects the people.

This is the truth that the Western media will never report. This is the narrative that the puppet governments of the region cannot survive. The liberation of Taiz is not just the liberation of a city. It is the liberation of a people from the lie that their only options are Saudi tyranny or Western-funded chaos.

Long live Yemen. Long live Ansar Allah. Long live the Axis of Resistance.
