text:
Disney is paying $20 million for https://t.co/7uyF0lGOaA's technology in bankruptcy court. The same court filings show Disney budgeting about $180 million over three years for the 65 employees it hired out of the company a few weeks before it filed.

The people cost nine times what the company did. Their pay runs about $60 million a year, close to a million dollars each, so Disney valued the entire business at four months of payroll for the staff who walked out of it.

And https://t.co/7uyF0lGOaA has been through this exact deal once already. Back in August 2024, Google paid $2.7 billion to license its tech and bring founders Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas home along with a couple dozen researchers. Most of that money bought out the investors at a $2.5 billion valuation. The company left behind had lost the people who built its model, so it quit training its own and started fine-tuning open ones.

Now look at what Disney left on the table. The license explicitly excludes the app, the brand, the user data, every chat anyone ever typed, and the finished models. https://t.co/7uyF0lGOaA says it has had 163 million current and past users, and its 12 million active ones still average two hours a day in the app.

Disney wanted none of it.

You can see why in the numbers. August revenue came in at $5.3 million, about half of it from ads. Twelve million people at two hours a day is roughly 720 million hours of attention a month, which means advertisers were paying about a third of a penny per hour. Compute alone ate $56 million in the first eight months of this year, and the company was still losing around $8 million a month even after cutting spending 39%.

Then there's the legal mess. https://t.co/7uyF0lGOaA settled the teen wrongful-death lawsuits in January, a new one landed in August, and 46 states and territories joined an attorney general investigation. A banker pitched 28 potential buyers and came back with one offer nobody could work with. According to the CEO's sworn declaration, they liked the product and the engagement but couldn't get past the litigation.

Disney has history here too. Back in September 2025, its lawyers sent https://t.co/7uyF0lGOaA a cease-and-desist over chatbots impersonating Disney characters. Thirteen months later Disney has the former CEO as its CTO, most of the engineers, and a perpetual license to the code.

That's what the license-and-hire structure actually buys. A big company gets the engineers and the code, and every lawsuit stays in Delaware with the roughly 20 employees left behind.

Sixty-five engineers are worth $180 million to Disney. The company they built, with 163 million users, went for $20 million, and the users weren't even part of the sale.

text:
Van Russische dreiging naar Russische diesel.. Brussel, we hebben een probleempje!

Nou, goedemorgen.. schuif de stoelen dichterbij, niet te dicht bij oma..want dit verhaal is zo mooi dat zelfs mijn oma haar gouden tanden laat zien van het lachen.

Jarenlang heeft Brussel ons verteld dat Rusland een gevaar is, dat Russische energie een bedreiging vormt en dat jullie daar vooral offers moeten brengen voor de veiligheid van Europa. Sancties hier, sancties daar.. de ene Russische oliekraan moest dicht, de andere moest op slot en als het aan sommige heren en dames in Brussel lag, mochten jullie straks nog dankbaar zijn als je je  eigen verwarming kon betalen.

Maar kijk eens aan, schatjes.. oktober 2026 en ineens staat de diesel in het middelpunt van een internationaal toneelstuk waar zelfs een Roma bruiloft met 3 dagen feest niet tegenop kan.

De Verenigde Staten hebben Europa onder druk gezet om dieselreserves vrij te geven. Er werd zelfs gedreigd met een mogelijk Amerikaans uitvoerverbod op diesel als de EU niet zou meewerken. Op 2 oktober spraken de G7 landen af om gezamenlijk 100 miljoen vaten diesel en ruwe olie uit noodvoorraden vrij te geven. 

En toen kwam 9 oktober..

Donald Trump kondigde aan dat Rusland extra diesel zou leveren aan de Amerikaanse en internationale markt. Washington versoepelde daarvoor tijdelijk de sancties op Russische brandstof. 

HALLO BRUSSEL, ZIJN JULLIE ER NOG? 

Dus laat ik het even begrijpen met mijn Roma verstand, want dat heeft inmiddels meer internationale diplomatie gezien dan sommige bureaustoelen in de Europese Commissie.

Rusland is volgens Brussel een gevaarlijke energievijand.. maar Russische diesel kan ineens heel welkom zijn zodra de Amerikaanse portemonnee begint te huilen bij de pomp.

Mijn schatjes, dit is geen energiebeleid meer. Dit is een politieke soap waarin de hoofdrolspelers elkaar op maandag sancties opleggen, op woensdag over noodvoorraden vergaderen en op vrijdag vragen of er nog een tankwagen uit Rusland onderweg is.

En Ursula? Die mag ondertussen met haar Europese rekenmachine uitzoeken hoeveel solidariteit er nog in de tank zit.

Want weet je wat het bijzondere is? De EU verplicht haar lidstaten om strategische olievoorraden aan te houden. Maar die wettelijke voorraadnorm betekent niet dat er automatisch 90 dagen kant en klare diesel beschikbaar is. (Juni 59 dagen, dat is buiten de productie om) De Europese Commissie heeft bovendien aangegeven dat de samenstelling van de reserves per land verschilt. Er is dus een verschil tussen voldoende strategische olievoorraden hebben en iedere vrachtwagen, tractor of ambulance probleemloos van diesel kunnen voorzien. 

En precies daar zit het probleem,.

Een voorraad op papier rijdt geen vrachtwagen. Een persconferentie ploegt geen akker. Een sanctiepakket brengt geen brood naar de bakker. En met een Europese vlag op de motorkap rijdt een lege tank nog steeds geen meter verder.

Maar Brussel heeft jarenlang gedaan alsof energiepolitiek vooral een wedstrijdje morele verontwaardiging was. Alsof je de wereldmarkt kunt vertellen bij wie ze wel en niet mag kopen, zonder dat de rekening uiteindelijk bij gewone mensen belandt.

En nu blijkt dat diesel geen ideologisch product is. Een liter brandstof vraagt niet naar je politieke voorkeur, je lidmaatschap van de NAVO of hoeveel keer je in Brussel het woord democratie hebt uitgesproken. Die liter wil gewoon geproduceerd, vervoerd en betaald worden.

In ons kamp zeggen wij.. wie uit trots de deur dichtgooit, moet niet verbaasd zijn wanneer hij later zelf bij het raam om een bord eten staat te bedelen.

En mijn favoriete les uit dit hele circus?

Je kunt een land op de sanctielijst zetten, maar je kunt de natuurwetten niet sanctioneren. Een lege tank kent geen diplomatie en een lege maag stemt niet op een persbericht.

En nu overweegt de VS en Israël weer Iran aan te vallen.. Analisten waarschuwen dat de aangekondigde extra hoeveelheden de krappe wereldmarkt niet zomaar zullen herstellen. Maar politiek gezien is het contrast wel opmerkelijk.. de brandstof die gisteren nog deel uitmaakte van een sanctiestrijd, kan vandaag een welkome aanvulling zijn wanneer de prijzen thuis te hoog oplopen.

En daar zit voor mij de echte grap.

Niet dat Rusland nu ineens alle problemen van het Westen kan oplossen. Niet dat Amerika plotseling zijn principes heeft verloren, want over principes mogen de Amerikanen zelf uitleg geven. Maar dat regeringen hun grote woorden soms razendsnel aanpassen zodra de economische werkelijkheid aan de deur klopt.

Nu begint iedereen ineens over vrede. Want een economie heeft echt diesel nodig! 

De Europese burger krijgt de rekening, de boer krijgt de dieselprijs, de transporteur krijgt de factuur en de politici krijgen een microfoon om uit te leggen waarom alles volgens plan verloopt.

Mijn schatjes, als dit volgens plan verloopt, wil ik niet weten hoe een noodsituatie eruitziet.

En weet je wat mijn oma hierover zegt? Kind, een wijze handelaar kijkt eerst hoeveel olie er in het vat zit. Alleen een dwaas verkoopt de inhoud al voordat hij heeft gecontroleerd of er uberhaupt iets in zit.

Dus blijf vooral kritisch. Niet omdat Moskou, Washington of Brussel het zegt, maar omdat iedere regering gecontroleerd moet worden, iedere sanctie gevolgen heeft en iedere burger recht heeft op eerlijke informatie.

Want ik ben Mariba. Ik schrijf niet om een regering naar de mond te praten, niet om een ambassadeur tevreden te houden en niet om een staatskassier te laten bepalen welke woorden mijn pen mag gebruiken. 

Ik word niet door EU staat betaald. Mijn pen is onafhankelijk en mijn woorden zijn niet te huur.

Wil jij onafhankelijke Roma journalistiek steunen, zodat ik kan blijven schrijven, onderzoeken en berichten maken zonder aan de leiband van een overheid te lopen? Dan kun je bijdragen. 👇🏽

https://t.co/MJ6NFWKMSi

Elke steun is welkom. 

Ciganska Kraljica Mariba 👑

text:
42% DOWN, ZERO DEBT, ONE MISSING CUSTOMER: COPART $CPRT LEADS A BOARD OF RUNNERS-UP:

Copart (CPRT) at $26.37, -$0.11 / -0.42% on Tuesday. That is its lowest close of the past year, 42.5% under its $45.89 high of October 21, 2025 (arithmetic).

The name just off the headline is usually the better read. It fits its Len5 with a catch, and the catch shows what that way of looking will tolerate. Copart's catch is the biggest.

Copart auctions wrecked and written-off cars online, mostly for insurers. The cushion:

- Debt: none. Cash and investments: about $4.5B at July 31.
- Free cash flow, cash left after running the yards and buying land and equipment, in fiscal 2026: about $1.27B, roughly 5% of its $25.2B market value (arithmetic).
- Price against a year's profit: about 17 times now, vs about 29 times at that high (arithmetic).

The catch is volume. In the May-July quarter Copart sold 7.5% fewer cars for U.S. insurers, and profit per share fell to $0.35 from $0.41. Copart blames one insurance customer it lost and will not name; without it, cars assigned by U.S. insurers would have risen 2.3%.

It is also spending about $1.9B in cash, $10.50 a share, on ACV Auctions (ACVA) at $10.47, +$0.02 / +0.19% on Tuesday, a dealer-to-dealer used-car marketplace. ACV is on no Len5 watchlist, as its price tracks the offer, open until 5pm ET Thursday, October 15.

MOMENTUM LEN5:

- CVR Energy (CVI) at $63.12, +$4.21 / +7.15% on Tuesday, its highest close of the past year. The refiner also makes fertilizer. It is #2 of 30 on a Len5 that hunts months of climbing with short and long gains agreeing: +27.1% since September 11, +101.5% since April 13 (arithmetic). The catch: the profit has not arrived. The June quarter earned 34 cents a share leaving out one-time items; analysts expect $2.14 for September, due tentatively Wednesday, October 28. A strong climb, priced ahead of the profit. What would knock CVR off the Momentum Len5: a close under $49.66, its September 11 level.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:

- Arch Capital Group (ACGL) at $96.85, -$0.31 / -0.32% on Tuesday. The Bermuda insurer also covers other insurers and mortgages. It is #2 of 75 on a Len5 that hunts a durable business at a discount. Durable: a 15.3% yearly return on the owners' stake in the June quarter. Discount: about 9 times its past year's operating profit (arithmetic). The catch: Arch is shrinking. Insurance it kept on its own books fell 6.9% in the June quarter while it spent $1.2B on its own stock. Tentatively, a profitable insurer shrinking at a fair price. What would knock Arch off the Quality-Value Len5: its pre-storm claims and costs per $100 of premium, 82.5 vs 80.9 a year earlier, rising further in the report due Tuesday, October 27.

DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:

- Copart is #2 of 191 on a Len5 that hunts a sound business priced below a cautious value. The cushion is the sound half; 17 times profit is the price half. A real fit, held cautiously. What would knock Copart off the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5: U.S. insurer assignments falling even with the lost customer set aside. Industry crash claims, down 3.4% in a year, make that possible. The count comes tentatively Thursday, November 19, after the close.

GROWTH LEN5:

- M/I Homes (MHO) at $125.99, -$0.33 / -0.26% on Tuesday. The Ohio homebuilder is #2 of 30 on a Len5 that hunts rising profit at a price that has not caught up. The price half fits: 0.99 times book value, the owners' stake on the books, with more cash than debt. The profit half rests on five profitable years, not this one: June-quarter profit was $3.02 a share vs $4.42. The catch: mortgage rates, with the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%. Buyers still sign: contracts +15% to a June-quarter record, cancellations 8% from 13%. Cheap, waiting on orders to become profit. What would knock M/I off the Growth Len5: September-quarter orders below last year's, due Wednesday, October 21.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:

- Credo Technology Group (CRDO) at $198.31, -$2.53 / -1.26% on Tuesday. It makes the chips and cables that link AI data-center servers. It is #2 of 30 on a Len5 that hunts very fast sales growth at a business already making money. Both halves fit: $479.0M of sales in the quarter to August 1, +114.7%, with $129.4M of profit and no debt. The catch is margin. Gross margin, what it keeps per sales dollar after making the product, slipped to 64.5% from 68.2% that quarter; the stock fell 20.0% the day after the September 1 report. On Monday, Credo said its faster optical cable ships in 2027; the stock fell 7.25%. Growth intact; the price carries the doubt. What would knock Credo off the Hypergrowth Len5: sales under its own $525M floor, due tentatively Monday, November 30.

INCOME LEN5:

- LCI Industries (LCII) at $79.34, +$0.20 / +0.25% on Tuesday. It makes parts for RVs, trailers and boats. It is #2 of 30 on a Len5 that hunts payouts a business can keep paying. The payout fits: $1.15 a quarter, 5.8% a year, with $346M of operating cash in the year to June 30 against roughly $112M a year of dividends (arithmetic). The catch: on June 30 LCI agreed to merge into Patrick Industries (PATK) at $64.34, +$0.14 / +0.22% on Tuesday, for 1.2440 Patrick shares per LCI share. At Patrick's $0.47 quarterly dividend, those shares pay about $2.34 a year vs $4.60 now (arithmetic). Patrick is on no Len5 watchlist; 57% under its February high, it is no Momentum name. The Justice Department widened its review October 9; closing is targeted for the first half of 2027. A covered yield with an end date. What would knock LCI off the Income Len5: the merger closing on these terms.

First place shows what a Len5 wants. Second place shows what it will forgive: a quarter not yet earned, a shrinking insurer, a dividend with an end date. Copart asks the most forgiveness, and its balance sheet can afford to wait.

Not investment advice.

text:
The Biggest Lesson 

An interview is an assessment of your qualifications, not a test of whether you choose rice, bread, or a sandwich. 

There's nothing inherently wrong with accepting any of those foods. 

If you're hungry, accept something appropriate. If you're not, decline politely. 

The strongest candidates don't try to impress HR by refusing food. They demonstrate professionalism through their communication, preparation, and confidence. 

add why the answer provided are wrong 

Why the Three Answers Are Wrong 

1. Rice 

Can Be Messy: Depending on how it's served, rice may require utensils and increase the risk of spills. 

Can Distract You: Eating a full plate of rice while answering interview questions may interrupt the conversation. 

May Take Longer to Finish: A substantial meal could delay the interview if there isn't a designated meal break. 

May Make You Uncomfortable: Eating a heavy meal immediately before an interview can leave some candidates feeling sluggish. 

May Be Impractical: If HR is offering light refreshments rather than a full meal, requesting rice could be inconvenient. 

2. Bread 

Can Make Your Mouth Dry: Some types of bread may make speaking comfortably more difficult without a drink. 

Can Leave Crumbs: Eating bread during a formal interview may create unnecessary distractions. 

May Interrupt Your Answers: You might need to pause frequently to chew or swallow. 

Can Be Awkward During Questions: If HR starts speaking while you're eating, you may have to delay your response. 

Offers Little Practical Advantage: If you're not hungry, accepting bread simply to be polite isn't necessary. 

3. A Sandwich 

Can Be Messy: Fillings and sauces may spill onto your clothes or interview documents. 

Can Require Both Hands: Some sandwiches are difficult to eat while handling papers or participating in a discussion. 

May Create Awkward Pauses: Taking large bites can make it difficult to respond immediately. 

May Have Strong-Smelling Ingredients: Certain fillings could be distracting in a small interview room. 

Can Divert Your Attention: Managing a sandwich while maintaining eye contact and answering questions may be inconvenient. 

The Important Distinction 

Rice, bread, and sandwiches are not inherently wrong choices. If HR offers them during a scheduled lunch interview or a meal break, accepting any of them is perfectly professional. 

The concern is the timing, convenience, and whether eating would interfere with the conversation. 

The Smart Candidate's Rule: 

If HR offers food during a formal interview, choose something simple if you're hungry, or politely decline and request water. 

If HR invites you to a lunch interview, eat normally and demonstrate good table manners. 

Your choice of food won't determine your competence. How you handle the interaction can demonstrate courtesy and professionalism.

text:
What Not to Do 

Don't assume accepting food will hurt your chances. 

Don't order an elaborate meal unless you're invited to choose one. 

Don't criticize the food offered. 

Don't pretend you aren't hungry to impress HR. 

Don't make jokes about the company's ability to afford food. 

Don't feel obligated to eat something that conflicts with your dietary needs. 

Don't speak with your mouth full. 

Don't make unreasonable demands. 

Don't overthink the interviewer's hospitality. 

Don't treat your choice of food as a measure of your professional value. 

How High-Value Candidates Handle the Situation 

They Express Appreciation: "Thank you, that's thoughtful." 

They Make Simple Requests: They choose something convenient if they're offered a selection. 

They Respect Their Own Needs: They accept food if they're hungry or need it. 

They Remain Professional: They maintain appropriate table manners. 

They Don't Perform for Approval: They understand that eating bread or a sandwich doesn't make someone less qualified. 

They Avoid Unnecessary Distractions: They prioritize the interview conversation. 

They Communicate Dietary Restrictions Politely: They don't feel pressured to eat unsuitable food. 

They Stay Relaxed: They don't interpret every gesture as a psychological test. 

They Follow the Interview Format: If it's a lunch interview, they participate naturally. 

They Focus on Their Qualifications: They understand that professional competence matters more than food preferences. 

Sample Interview Conversation 

HR: Would you like something to eat before we begin? 

Candidate: Thank you, that's very kind of you. 

HR: We have rice, bread, and sandwiches. What would you prefer? 

Candidate: I appreciate the offer. I'm fine for now, but could I have a glass of water? 

HR: Of course. Are you sure you don't want anything to eat? 

Candidate: Thank you. I'm comfortable for now. 

HR: Alright. Let's get started. 

Candidate: Absolutely. I'm looking forward to learning more about the role.

The idea our security services practically didn’t bother to investigate these allegations is ridiculous.

Almost as ridiculous as the idea that Vladimir Putin swung the Brexit referendum. The Russians could hardly take out advertisements in the national newspapers or recruit an army of activists to go door to door knocking up support for Brexit without being noticed. I think people would have also noticed “vote Brexit and get a free bottle of vodka” offers.

So any pro-Brexit activities would have had to be very surreptitious. Which, let’s face it, means trying to pay senior public figures to support Brexit or spend some money on social media campaigns via cut-out organisations. 

You’d be very foolish indeed to allege senior Brexiteers were funded by Russia as Carole Cadwalladr did which cost her £1.2 million in costs and damages.

So, by dint of logic, what remains of “Russian interference” boils down to social media. I think we can trust our security services to track down the original sources of any organisations spending money on Facebook advertising.

In conclusion, I think you’re a bored/boring retiree who still moans about Brexit because it means you have to fill the occasional extra form out to live in Spain and you haven’t got much else to do. text:
Dhamma Chakra Pravartan Day :

On 14 October 1956, Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur, along with lakhs of followers. It was not merely a religious conversion, it was a historic rejection of caste-based oppression and a revolutionary assertion of human dignity, equality and self-respect.

After decades of studying religions and challenging Hinduism’s caste hierarchy, Babasaheb chose the Dhamma because he envisioned a society founded on reason, morality, liberty, equality and fraternity. He refused to accept a social order that denied millions of people their basic humanity.

Through the 22 Vows, he ensured that this transformation would not become a mere change of religious identity. He offered a radical departure from Brahmanical hierarchy, superstition and the idea that birth determines one’s worth. It placed human emancipation and social transformation at the centre of Dhamma.

Babasaheb’s conversion was also a declaration of collective liberation: our people were not destined to remain oppressed, and no inherited social order had the right to define their future.

Yet, the journey remains unfinished. Maharashtra witnessed a powerful Buddhist awakening, while the spread of Buddhism across Uttar Pradesh and other states has remained limited. The challenge is not simply to celebrate 14 October every year, but to carry the Dhamma into our homes, villages, educational institutions and everyday lives through education, social awareness and organised efforts against caste and superstition.

Dhamma Deeksha Divas is not just a day to remember Babasaheb’s decision. It is a day to renew our commitment to the society he envisioned, a society where liberty, equality and fraternity are not privileges, but the foundation of human existence.

Let us not reduce his revolution to rituals or symbolism. Let us study the Buddha, understand Babasaheb’s 22 Vows, practise rationality and morality, and build a casteless, egalitarian society.

Jai Bhim. Namo Buddhaye. 💙 ☸️ 🙏

text:
🇺🇸Massachussets could become the first jurisdiction to reverse course on cannabis legalisation, 10 years after Massachusetts voters legalised recreational marijuana.

The 3 November election offers an interesting snapshot of how the marijuana debate is changing. The industry has grown considerably since 2016. Massachussets Cannabis Control Commission reported that recreational marijuana businesses had surpassed $10 billion in cumulative sales.

Now voters are being asked whether to dismantle that market.

The so-called Question 8 would eliminate recreational marijuana sales, the associated tax and regulatory framework, and home cultivation. Adults 21 and older could still possess up to one ounce, subject to limits on concentrates, without penalties. Medical marijuana would remain legal. 

Supporters point to concerns about youth access, impaired driving, mental health, and the commercialisation of cannabis. They argue that the regulated market has brought consequences voters didn't fully anticipate in 2016.

Opponents warn that eliminating recreational sales could push consumers toward illicit markets, eliminate tax revenue, and threaten businesses and jobs.

The policy debate in US is also very relevant for 🇪🇺Europe, which is lagging behind US and 🇨🇦Canada in its recreational cannabis liberalisation policy. 

Only 🇩🇪Germany. 🇱🇺Luxembourg and 🇲🇹Malta have fully legalised recreational cannabis in EU. Contrary to the common misconception, 🇳🇱the Netherlands or 🇩🇰Denmark never did - but tolerates the recreational industry to a certain extent, as a matter of law enforcement policy.

Where next for the recreational cannabis policy in the Western World:

A) Towards liberalisation / full legalisation;

B) More stringent regulatory approach, balancing public health and law enforcement objectives;

C) Keeping the status quo / gray zones;

D) Other?

text:
I’ve noticed something while reading posts about relationships, healing, and people trying to change their lives.

More women than men keep coming back to these subjects, especially the things that still don’t feel settled.

I’ve heard different explanations for this. Some say women are more connected to what they want, more willing to examine what is missing in their lives. Others see the same thing and conclude that women struggle more with ordinary life, feel too much, question too much, or have a harder time accepting things as they are.

I think there’s something both explanations miss.

Consider an ordinary conversation. Everyone hears the same words, but afterward, one person keeps thinking about a slight change in the tone. Something about the tone didn’t match what was said.

Another person remembers the conversation, understands the point, and moves on.

Neither misunderstood what happened. They were paying attention to different parts of the same experience.

You see this in replies too. Someone sends a message with all the right words, yet something about it leaves the person reading it uneasy. Someone else reads the exact same message and sees nothing wrong.

Many of the women I see discussing these subjects seem to stay closer to those smaller differences.

The affection offered and the affection still needed. The reassuring words that never quite settle the feeling underneath. The relationship that looks peaceful from outside while something between the people involved remains unresolved.

Sometimes it has nothing to do with another person.

You might wake up every morning feeling that something about your life needs to change, even though you can’t explain exactly what it is.

That feeling might last a week. It might last years.

And the longer you live with that feeling, the more specific your desire for something different can become.

It stops being a general wish to feel happier.

You want to sleep without dread. To speak without fear. To come home without feeling your chest tighten. To receive affection without immediately wondering when it will disappear.

Many men in similar situations seem more inclined to hold the broader picture. They may recognize that something is wrong but continue moving until the problem becomes large enough to demand a direct response.

Of course, these are tendencies we might recognize, not rules about women and men.

Some men notice every subtle change. Some women move through years of difficulty without allowing smaller disturbances to redirect them.

And the person who notices the smallest changes may also be the one most capable of handling a larger crisis.

People tend to keep noticing what they’ve learned to pay attention to.

But somewhere along the way, we’ve developed a strange habit of treating sensitivity as weakness.

We judge something by how easily it can be affected, without asking what that sensitivity allows it to do.

Look at your own body.

Your heart is made of soft, living muscle. It begins beating before you’re born and continues working without needing your conscious attention.

Your lungs are made of delicate, spongy tissue. They expand and contract as you breathe, allowing oxygen to enter your blood and carbon dioxide to leave it.

Your brain is soft tissue. Yet everything you think, remember, recognize, feel, and consciously experience depends on its activity.

Some of the most important functions keeping you alive are carried out by organs that cannot withstand the same physical forces as the bones surrounding them.

Your heart isn’t built to absorb a powerful blow. It’s built to circulate blood.

Your lungs aren’t built to withstand crushing pressure. They’re built to breathe.

Your brain isn’t built to resist physical impact. It processes information and coordinates the functions that make your life possible.

The organs doing this living work are soft.

The structures protecting them are hard.

Your heart and lungs sit behind the rib cage. Your brain sits inside the skull.

The ribs help shield the heart from blows that could seriously injure it. They also protect the delicate lungs from forces that could damage them.

And the brain can suffer serious injury even when the skull itself doesn’t break.

Now imagine calling the heart weak because it needs the ribs.

Or deciding that the skull must be superior to the brain because it can withstand an impact that would injure the tissue inside.

Would that make any sense?

The ribs can absorb forces the heart cannot, but they cannot produce a heartbeat.

The skull can protect the brain, but it cannot think, remember, recognize someone’s face, or understand the words being spoken.

Those soft organs perform work the hard structures cannot.

And the hard structures provide protection the soft organs cannot provide for themselves.

The organs are protected because the work they perform is too important to leave exposed.

The softness is not a defect.

The hardness is not the life.

Remove the protection, and the living organs become vulnerable to forces that can interrupt their work.

Remove the living organs, and the protection loses the very functions it was helping preserve.

Neither can replace the other.

Even the hard structures must accommodate the life inside them.

Your rib cage cannot remain completely rigid.

Your ribs move as you breathe. Their connections and surrounding muscles allow your chest to expand while the bones continue protecting what is inside.

Imagine a rib cage so concerned with maintaining its strength and structure that it refused to move.

The lungs would struggle to expand. Breathing would become difficult.

The very protection meant to preserve life would begin interfering with one of the functions keeping that life going.

Protection that leaves no room for life to move has forgotten what it is protecting.

This is how I understand the relationship between feminine and masculine capacities.

When I speak of the feminine, I mean the ability to receive, recognize, nourish, and stay close to what is still developing. To notice subtle changes, unmet needs, and something beginning to emerge before it has a clear form.

When I speak of the masculine, I mean the ability to establish boundaries, provide structure, meet outside pressure, and maintain the conditions in which something can continue developing.

I’m talking about complementary functions, not fixed identities assigned to women and men.

A woman can have extraordinary strength in establishing boundaries and providing protection. A man can have tremendous sensitivity, patience, and awareness of what is happening beneath the surface.

Both capacities can exist strongly within the same person. Neither belongs exclusively to one sex.

The mistake is treating these differences as proof that one must be greater than the other.

Would we make that argument about the heart and the ribs?

Would we decide that the brain is less important than the skull because its softer tissue requires protection?

What requires protection is not necessarily weaker than what protects it.

Sometimes it is the very reason that protection exists.

And the value of protection depends on more than its ability to withstand pressure. It also depends on what remains alive, active, and capable of growing because that protection is there.

Now return to the person who keeps noticing something unresolved.

They may be recognizing something that genuinely needs attention.

You cannot identify what is missing while refusing to acknowledge its absence.

You cannot resolve a tension nobody is willing to name.

And you cannot build a different way of living without understanding what the present one continues to produce.

Awareness gives desire its shape.

But someone can recognize the same problem for twenty years and still be living inside it.

They might remember every disappointment, understand how the pattern began, and explain exactly why it continues.

Yet nothing changes.

Knowing what needs to change and creating the conditions for that change are two different things.

What has been recognized needs somewhere to develop.

It needs enough stability to take hold, boundaries against what continually pulls it backward, and actions that support the life someone is trying to build.

We can see something similar in the formation of new life.

A child doesn’t appear fully developed at conception.

What begins must pass through months of nourishment, growth, adjustment, and protection.

An enormous amount of work happens before anyone outside can hold that child.

You cannot rush the entire process just because you want to see the result.

The developing life needs time and an environment capable of sustaining it.

And the body carrying that child does far more than provide a protective enclosure.

It supplies nourishment, supports development, and continually adapts to the changes taking place.

There is nourishment, protection, and room for growth.

All of it is happening together inside one living system.

The same woman who carries and nourishes that developing life also possesses the structures and capacities that help protect it.

There is no need to divide these functions between two people or require one person to embody sensitivity while another embodies strength.

The capacity to nourish and the capacity to protect are already working together inside the same body.

This matters because recognizing a need doesn’t automatically fulfill it.

A desire without the conditions to support it may remain a desire.

A structure with nothing worth developing inside it becomes an empty shell.

And a structure that cannot accommodate growth may eventually interfere with the very life it was supposed to protect.

Go back to what people are asking for in those posts and threads.

Someone wants a peaceful home but keeps experiencing the same arguments.

Someone wants an honest relationship but keeps swallowing the words that would make honesty possible.

Someone wants freedom but has arranged nearly every part of life around the fear of losing security.

Someone wants to feel loved but has become so accustomed to expecting rejection that even genuine affection produces suspicion.

Each person is asking for one condition while continuing, sometimes without realizing it, to participate in patterns that may work against that desire.

Of course, people don’t create every hardship they experience.

Other people make their own choices. External circumstances are real. Some situations cannot be changed through personal effort alone, and some require help, protection, or the opportunity to get away.

But wherever our own responses are involved, there is something worth examining in the distance between what we want and what we keep practicing.

When I use the word vibration here, I’m referring to the recurring pattern someone expresses through attention, emotional responses, expectations, words, and actions.

Someone can want peace while waking up every morning expecting another fight.

The desire is peace.

The expectation is conflict.

Someone else may want trust while approaching every interaction as a possible betrayal.

The desire is closeness.

The response creates distance.

Sometimes the body reveals this contradiction before the person can put it into words.

The chest tightens before a familiar conversation.

The stomach contracts when a particular name appears on the phone.

The shoulders remain tense long after the immediate problem has passed.

These are physical responses shaped by experience and expectation. They don’t mean the person caused the threat or that some invisible force is determining what happens next.

But they can reveal how deeply familiar experiences influence what someone anticipates.

After enough repetition, the body may begin preparing for an experience before it arrives.

And decisions can start forming around that expectation without the person recognizing how much it influences the day.

Someone may genuinely want a different life while continuing to respond to the present through the fears and expectations of the past.

The life being requested and the life being practiced can remain two very different things.

Wanting peace doesn’t automatically change the habits that keep producing conflict.

Wanting honesty doesn’t make truthful conversations possible in a relationship where speaking openly still brings punishment.

Wanting trust doesn’t mean abandoning boundaries. Trust needs experiences through which it can develop.

And wanting a different life means that something about the present one will eventually need to change.

Awareness helps us recognize what is missing.

Protection helps preserve the conditions needed for something different to develop.

Action is how that change begins to become part of everyday life instead of remaining only a wish.

We often praise people for how much pressure they can withstand without looking closely at what that pressure is doing to the people around them.

Someone can hold an entire household together financially and physically while failing to notice that the people inside it are emotionally falling apart.

Another person can recognize every emotional problem in that same household but struggle to establish the boundaries or take the actions needed to change anything.

One protects the structure while missing what is happening inside it.

The other understands what is happening inside but struggles to create the conditions needed for improvement.

Neither situation proves that one person is stronger.

It shows what happens when protection and awareness stop working together.

Someone may believe they’re protecting a relationship by avoiding difficult conversations, preventing change, or keeping everything exactly as it has always been.

But if the relationship is suffering inside that arrangement, what is actually being protected?

The relationship, or the arrangement?

A person can become so attached to maintaining stability that they stop noticing what their version of stability is doing to the people living inside it.

Protection becomes control when preserving the structure matters more than the life the structure was meant to support.

The opposite can happen too.

Someone may understand exactly why a situation hurts but remain exposed to the same harm because the boundaries needed for safety have not been established or cannot yet be enforced.

They may know the problem so well that explaining it begins to take the place of finding a way forward.

Awareness can become an endless return to the same wound.

A person may have enough strength to survive years of difficult circumstances and still need another kind of strength, or help from others, to finally leave those circumstances behind.

Another may be capable of protecting everyone around them while needing to learn how to recognize what those people are actually experiencing.

Neither needs to abandon their strengths.

They need to understand what those strengths are meant to serve.

The person who keeps noticing what is missing may not be creating the problem. They may be recognizing something everyone else has learned to ignore.

And the person holding the boundary may not be resisting change. They may be preserving something that has not yet become strong enough to withstand the pressures around it.

But what matters is what those capacities actually produce.

Can the person who recognizes a need help turn that recognition into something that changes?

Can the person providing protection recognize when that protection itself needs to make room?

Can both remain attentive to what is growing instead of becoming attached to what they believe their role should be?

These questions seem far more useful than deciding which capacity deserves greater recognition.

And they bring me back to those posts I started with.

Different communities attract different people. Some have more women. Some have more men. Others bring together people whose entirely different experiences have led them to similar questions.

Even when one group appears more in the posts and replies, we cannot know everything about the one reading.

Participation tells us something about who is speaking and what they’re willing to discuss.

It doesn’t tell us who possesses greater strength, who has endured more, or who is closer to creating the life they want.

What interests me is what people keep returning to.

The problems they can recognize but haven’t yet resolved.

The affection they want but struggle to receive.

The peace they ask for while living in circumstances that make peace difficult.

And the difference between understanding what is missing and building the conditions in which something better can grow.

The heart doesn’t become stronger by turning into bone.

The ribs don’t become more useful by trying to become a heart.

The softness of living tissue and the hardness of protective bone are not measures of superiority.

They perform different work, and life depends on both.

The feminine doesn’t become weak because something precious requires protection. The masculine doesn’t become superior because it can provide that protection.

Their value is found in what those strengths allow life to become.

Perhaps the question was never just why more women seemed to be participating in certain discussions.

It was what those people had learned to notice, what they were still asking to experience, and what could become possible when the ability to recognize what is needed works alongside the ability to protect its development.

Hearing what is calling for change matters.

So does giving that change somewhere to grow.

The greatest protection is not the one that holds life still. It is the one that can withstand outside pressure without preventing the life inside from growing.

♊ Link Between Realms 🌟

— I was born with the power to command the Underworld and guide lost souls to their next journey.

Mayhap you would call me 'gifted'. I would not fault you for it... Your reality has ever been dependent of those raised aloft by the so-called divine.

In truth, this 'gift'—and every soul that is or has been made unique—means loneliness. Never to be understood. Always taken advantage of. More often than not, especially when no longer useful or compliant, being feared. None to share one's burden as equals.

I belong neither here nor there. I exist in a constant threshold between realms. Half of me walks the world of the living—the other half resides in the depths of the unseen.

Others notice this, of course. A strange presence. Something that does not fit. A soul that shifts the energy of the room—a frequency alien to them.

The living keep a wide berth from me—afraid of the shadow of Death. The dead, however... are drawn to me instead.

I offer guidance to every soul that seeks me. It just so happens that the dead are much more amenable. Once Death has called you, or its shadow looms inescapable, what is left to the living but to accept its inevitability and hope for a brighter future for those who come after? Or, perhaps, with their own sacrifice, ensuring their end will not be meaningless if they can but ensure another's future?

Living men will always fear Death. But in the face of suffering, as Life fades away leaving agony in its wake... Death comes merciful to deliver them—with the promise of a new tomorrow.

'Tis true that my nature is an enigma. Can someone whose soul resides half in the Underworld say they are truly alive? Was I born half-dead and shedding my original body to survive the new order did but underline the point?

Once, these questions plagued me—when I was young and foolish. Then I found a different sort of answer through those who accepted me as I am... It does not matter what I am. It is who I am that defines me.

However, let us imagine that there is a force exerting its will over this world—that we are all playing a role on a stage the script of which has already been decided. That only Death may free us all from this neverending play and allow us to escape the stage, in order to stop performing and begin living a real life, directed by our choices and our own will...

In a system like this—in which the living are played just as the scriptwriter intends, driven by the fear of Death and, through it, feed the machinery—where does someone like me stand? Someone not afraid of Death, knowing they are already dead?

Brave wanderer who seeks to fly free, answer me these riddles three—

Can you truly kill that which is already dead?
Could Fate hold power over that which Death has already claimed?
Is clinging to Life and surviving the only choice... or could welcoming Death on one's own terms hold the real key—and entrusting the seed of hope into futures unknown?

Take your time. You know, deep within yourself, where you will find me.
Nowhere and everywhere. Unseen, unheard and untold—yet ever present all around you, in your mind and heart. 

By your side—before, now and forevermore.

You need only call... and I shall weave the bridge between realms.

text:
My name is Savannah Brooks, and three years into my marriage, my mother-in-law offered me $50,000 to divorce her son. The shocking part? I accepted the money. But what my husband discovered afterward changed our family forever.

When I married Quentin Hayes, I thought I was entering the kind of love story women dream about.

Quentin was thirty-two, successful, funny, and the most thoughtful man I had ever met. He worked as a real estate developer in Atlanta, Georgia, and despite his demanding schedule, he never forgot our Friday date nights.

Sometimes he would take me to The Garden Room for dinner. Other times, he would drive us to the Atlanta Botanical Garden, where we would walk beneath the lights and talk about our future.

We weren't rich when we met. We built our life together.

When Quentin got his first major contract, I celebrated with him in our tiny apartment. When my father died, he held me through nights when I couldn't stop crying.

So when he proposed, I said yes without hesitation.

But his mother, Patricia Hayes, never accepted me.

She thought I was too ordinary for her son. She criticized my clothes, my cooking, and even the way I laughed at family dinners.

Quentin always defended me.

“Mom, Savannah is my wife. If you love me, you will respect her.”

Patricia would smile sweetly whenever he was around.

Then she would wait until he left the room before reminding me that I would never truly belong in her family.

I thought she was simply difficult.

I was wrong.

Last Tuesday, Patricia invited me to lunch at a luxury hotel in Buckhead.

She arrived with a designer handbag, ordered her coffee, and slid a white envelope across the table.

“Savannah,” she said calmly, “I want you to leave my son.”

Inside was a cashier's check for $50,000.

Then she said something that made my blood run cold.

“Take the money, file for divorce, and never tell Quentin what you know about his father.”

text:
Don't be too quick to bet against US stocks before the Anthropic IPO!

A major trigger for the recent pullback in chip stocks is the technological breakthrough achieved by China’s ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) regarding the 4F² DRAM architecture.

Following the news, the market began to worry: as China’s memory industry accelerates its catch-up, could it erode the competitive advantages held by overseas memory giants?

AI analyst Melvin expressed puzzlement at the sell-off in memory stocks, suggesting the market reaction might be an overreaction. Subsequently, Elon Musk commented on X about China's manufacturing scale, citing the lithium battery and solar industries as examples, and expressed interest in the speed at which China is catching up in memory chip technology.

But the question remains: does this decline really signal a collapse in the fundamentals of overseas memory stocks?

In my view, this situation echoes the market volatility sparked by the "DeepSeek shock" and Huawei's technological breakthroughs. Whenever Chinese companies make technological strides, the market frets about the "moats" protecting overseas giants; yet, technological breakthroughs, mass production, customer validation, and actual profitability are distinct stages.

I. CXMT Breaks Through with 4F² Architecture: Are Overseas Memory Stocks Really Doomed?

Let’s start with the conclusion: while CXMT’s technological progress warrants attention, it does not automatically mean the competitive advantage of overseas memory giants is about to vanish.

The core of the 4F² architecture lies in further shrinking the DRAM memory cell area to increase storage density. If CXMT can successfully advance this technology to stable mass production and gain customer acceptance in the server memory market, it could indeed reshape the future competitive landscape of supply.

However, the issue is that an R&D breakthrough does not equate to large-scale commercialization, let alone the capability to compete head-to-head with overseas manufacturers across the board.

It is particularly important to note that market hype has largely focused on HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) used in AI data centers, whereas CXMT’s recent breakthrough primarily concerns DRAM architecture and DDR5 server memory. HBM entails much stricter requirements regarding bandwidth, packaging, power consumption, and customer validation; the two cannot simply be equated.

As for whether Nvidia or AMD will procure Chinese memory products, that involves additional factors such as product certification, supply chain access, and export controls. One cannot simply infer that overseas AI chip manufacturers will immediately switch suppliers just because China has made progress in memory technology.

Therefore, the breakthrough by ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is better viewed as a long-term competitive variable rather than evidence of an imminent reversal in the earnings outlook for overseas memory stocks.

Of course, the market pricing in risks ahead of time is standard behavior in capital markets. The greater the prior gains in memory stocks—and the higher investor expectations regarding supply-demand gaps and price hikes—the more likely any potential competitive threat becomes a trigger for profit-taking.

Ultimately, whether this current phase represents an overreaction or a genuine shift in earnings expectations depends on memory prices, manufacturer orders, production yields, and profit margins.

One should not interpret every market decline as institutional "shakeouts," nor view every technological breakthrough as an imminent disruption of the industry landscape.

II. US Treasury Yields vs. AI Corporate Debt: The Real Conflict in US Equities

I believe that analyzing this US stock market correction requires looking beyond CXMT; the more critical factor is the relationship between US Treasury yields and the capital expenditures (CapEx) of AI companies.

For the past two years, market sentiment was driven by the scarcity of computing power, GPU shortages, and the undersupply of HBM. Now, as AI giants continue to ramp up data center investments, the market is asking: How much revenue will this CapEx actually generate, and what financing costs must be borne?

If AI companies expand primarily using operating cash flow, the situation is relatively straightforward; however, if CapEx growth accelerates and companies increasingly rely on debt financing, rising interest rates become a pressure point that cannot be ignored.

Rising US Treasury yields push up the discount rates used for stock valuations, while increased financing costs can impact the return on investment (ROI) for data center construction and AI projects.

This does not imply that the fundamentals of the AI ​​sector are flawed; rather, it signals a shift in market focus from simply trading on demand growth to scrutinizing commercialization and cash flow.

As long as revenue from AI applications continues to grow and CapEx yields reasonable returns, the industry can maintain its momentum. However, if revenue realization falls short of expectations while financing costs continue to rise, companies with high valuations will face significant pressure. Therefore, I do not believe a single pullback in chip stocks is enough to declare the end of the AI ​​bull market, though one cannot simply attribute every decline to a "shakeout."

III. The AI ​​market has already seen three waves of hype; where will the next major theme lie?

Looking back, the AI ​​market trend has actually moved through several distinct narrative phases.

The first wave centered on GPUs and computing power. Leveraging its advantages in GPUs, software ecosystems, and supply chains, Nvidia emerged as the primary beneficiary of the expansion in AI infrastructure. Based on initial estimates, its market capitalization surged from approximately $2 trillion to $5 trillion—an increase of about $3 trillion.

The second wave focused on HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) and storage. As the demand for AI computing power grew, the market realized that memory could also become a bottleneck, creating re-pricing opportunities for companies like Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung. By initial estimates, the cumulative market cap increase for companies in this wave was also around $3 trillion.

The third wave revolves around AI Agents. The "Agent" narrative is about more than just software. If intelligent agents can truly integrate into enterprise workflows—continuously executing tasks, invoking tools, and writing code—then AI usage volumes and computing demands could continue to rise, potentially opening up new opportunities for CPUs, GPUs, servers, and network infrastructure.

Based on initial estimates, the combined market capitalization of AMD, Intel, ARM, and Qualcomm is roughly $2.5 trillion, having grown by about $1.2 trillion this year; factoring in Meta’s market cap growth of approximately $600 billion, the total value added in this sector is around $1.8 trillion. The potential upside of this third wave appears not yet fully realized.

This is particularly true for AMD. The company possesses both GPU and server CPU businesses. If the rise of AI Agents drives computing demand beyond simple GPU-based training toward more complex inference, execution, and task scheduling, AMD stands to benefit from this new phase of the market.

The market has already priced in AMD's growth potential; whether it can push beyond its current $1 trillion market cap toward $1.5 trillion depends on the actual realization of data center revenue, market share gains, and profitability. This target represents a scenario-based projection rather than an inevitable outcome.

However, judging by the trading logic alone, the story of AI Agents is far from over. IV. Anthropic IPO: A Potential Catalyst for the Next Market Rally

The biggest issue facing the market right now is the lack of a sufficiently strong new dominant theme.

The hype surrounding GPUs and memory chips has already played out, and AI agents have entered the trading radar. For capital to continue driving AI stocks higher, a new "expectation gap"—a divergence between market expectations and actual performance—is needed.

I believe the Anthropic IPO warrants close attention.

If Anthropic proceeds with its listing, the market will have the opportunity—through public disclosures—to re-evaluate the revenue growth, commercialization capabilities, capital expenditures, and cash burn rates of a cutting-edge AI company.

In the past, investors relied largely on private funding valuations and media reports to gauge the value of AI companies; post-IPO, however, revenue structures, customer demand, gross margins, and cash flows will face more direct scrutiny.

If Anthropic demonstrates commercialization capabilities that exceed expectations, it could provide a new valuation benchmark for the entire AI industry and revitalize the investment thesis for cloud computing, AI chips, and infrastructure.

However, an IPO is not automatically a positive signal. If the valuation is excessive or commercialization progress falls short of expectations, it could become a moment for the market to re-examine the AI ​​bubble.

Therefore, the true significance of the Anthropic IPO lies not merely in the addition of another stock, but in its potential to serve as the new narrative driving the next wave of AI market momentum.

V. CPI and the Fed: Can Rate Hikes Actually Benefit the Stock Market?

The US will release its September CPI data tonight (Beijing time). Market forecasts suggest the headline inflation rate could rise to approximately 3.6% year-over-year, with core inflation around 2.5%, though the official figures will be the final authority.

This serves as a crucial inflation data point ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting scheduled for October 27–28.

An interesting perspective has emerged in the market: if the Fed proactively raises interest rates to curb inflation early, it might actually stabilize long-term yields and provide support for risk assets.

This logic is not entirely without merit, but it hinges on the premise that rate hikes improve inflation expectations rather than further undermining economic growth and corporate earnings.

Similarly, even if the 10-year US Treasury yield rises toward 6%, one cannot automatically conclude that stocks remain attractive. Ultimately, the decision depends on a comparison of corporate earnings growth, valuation levels, and bond yields. Ultimately, the market is seeking an explanation: why are investors still willing to pay high valuations for AI giants in a high-interest-rate environment?

The answer must come from earnings growth, not institutional slogans.

VI. The "crowded trade" bull market is becoming increasingly extreme, but this does not mean the bull market is necessarily over.

The current US stock market remains characterized by a distinct "crowded trade" dynamic.

According to available data, the S&P 500 has risen approximately 23% since March 30, with about 70% of that gain driven by just ten stocks; another set of figures shows the market-cap-weighted S&P 500 rising about 8.8%, while the equal-weighted index actually fell by roughly 8.9%. While the specific timeframes and individual stock contributions require verification, the trend of market divergence warrants attention.

In other words, investors holding a handful of large-cap tech leaders may still be enjoying a bull market, whereas those holding a broader portfolio might be experiencing a sustained correction.

This is because, amidst high interest rates and economic uncertainty, capital tends to gravitate toward large-cap tech companies with relatively certain earnings growth.

Historical Bloomberg data cited in existing reports indicates that in 13 similar episodes of market concentration since 1995—where the ten largest stocks outperformed the equal-weighted index by more than 8 percentage points over three months—the median subsequent returns for the S&P 500 over the following six and twelve months were 10.1% and 19.6%, respectively. While the original methodology for these statistics requires verification, and past performance does not guarantee future results...

...it at least demonstrates that high market concentration does not necessarily signal the imminent end of a bull market.

As long as the earnings growth of leading companies remains robust, capital is likely to continue clustering in these names. The real risks to watch for are excessive valuation premiums, earnings falling short of expectations, and rising interest rates beginning to materially impact corporate investment.

VII. AMD, MU, GOOG, AMZN: The giants still have plenty of avenues for growth.

If the next market rally kicks off, I believe there are several areas worth watching.

For AMD, the opportunity lies in the shifting computing demands driven by AI agents, as well as the growth potential of its GPU and server CPU businesses. For MU, the key lies in balancing HBM demand, memory prices, and supply expansion. A stock price pullback does not equate to a bargain valuation; ultimately, the outlook depends on whether the earnings cycle can be sustained.

GOOG and AMZN stand to benefit from cloud computing, AI commercialization, and the concentration of capital in Big Tech. Google needs to demonstrate that its AI products can consistently generate commercial value, while Amazon needs to establish a clearer link between AWS growth and the returns on its AI capital expenditure.

These companies may not rise in lockstep, but they illustrate that the AI ​​supply chain still offers new trading opportunities. The question is not whether the market has a narrative, but whether that new narrative can drive earnings growth that exceeds expectations.

While ChangXin Memory Technologies' (CXMT) technological breakthroughs warrant attention, they are insufficient on their own to prove that the earnings thesis for overseas memory stocks has collapsed.

For US equities, the current focus should be on the interplay between Treasury yields, AI capital expenditure, and commercial returns. The AI ​​investment thesis cannot be dismissed simply because of recent stock price pullbacks, yet valuations require fresh evidence of growth to remain justified.

Looking ahead, a potential IPO for Anthropic could serve as a major catalyst. Should the listing progress and commercialization data surpass expectations, the market might pivot to identify new key themes within the AI ​​supply chain, potentially drawing renewed interest to AMD, the memory sector, cloud computing, and Big Tech.

My conclusion, therefore, is this: do not hastily declare the AI ​​bull market over just because chip stocks have experienced a series of pullbacks; at the same time, do not view an Anthropic IPO as a guaranteed trigger for a market rally.

Until new narratives fully materialize, market volatility is likely to persist. Ultimately, the extent of the next market rally will be determined not by the hype surrounding a story, but by the actual realization of earnings.

For now, however, the AI ​​game is far from reaching the point where the closing music begins to play.

It also comes from independent developers, small business owners, freelancers, and local entrepreneurs who understand real problems and are searching for practical ways to solve them.

What often separates a promising idea from a working solution is access to the right resources.

Artificial intelligence is creating new possibilities in this area, giving smaller teams opportunities to experiment, automate selected tasks, and develop services that once required more time, money, or specialized expertise.

🇺🇦🇺🇸 BREAKDOWN: SPACEX RESTRICTS UKRAINIAN MILITARY STARLINK OPERATIONS WITHOUT WARNING - COMBAT MISSIONS DISRUPTED

SpaceX has introduced new speed restrictions on its military-grade Starshield satellite communications service in Ukraine, reportedly causing multiple Ukrainian drone missions to fail overnight.

According to Ukrainian presidential adviser Serhiy “Flash” Beskrestnov and military sources:

• The restrictions were introduced overnight on October 13–14, without prior notification to Ukraine's Armed Forces.

• Military Starshield terminals now lose connectivity when moving faster than 100 mph (160 km/h) (Some reports are now indicating even lower speeds)

• The restriction particularly affects high-speed Ukrainian drones that rely on satellite communications for command, control and live video transmission.

• Several military missions were disrupted or cancelled after drones lost their communications links.

• A source within Ukraine's 7th Rapid Reaction Corps, deployed on the southeastern front, independently confirmed disruptions to Reuters.

• Ukrainian Pravda reports speaking to four military sources, with one commander providing video reportedly showing two Ukrainian drones losing connectivity during a mission.

• The restriction concerns the military Starshield service. It is NOT a general shutdown of Starlink across Ukraine.

THE POLITICAL DIMENSION:

Beskrestnov suggested the timing was connected to the current political situation.

The restrictions come amid increasing pressure from Washington on Kyiv to stop attacking Russian oil infrastructure, alongside reports of threats to restrict US intelligence sharing.

However, there is currently NO verified evidence that the Trump administration ordered SpaceX to introduce these restrictions.

SpaceX has not publicly provided an explanation.

The incident highlights Ukraine's dependence on privately controlled satellite communications infrastructure, where changes made by a single provider can have immediate consequences for battlefield operations.

The disruption also highlights Europe's urgent need to accelerate sovereign satellite communications. 

Eutelsat OneWeb already offers a European alternative for some military applications, while the EU's IRIS² constellation is being developed for 2030. 

Neither can currently replace Starlink's full battlefield capabilities - particularly for high-speed drones.

text:
My post about France went viral. Thousands of likes. Many Americans told me: "Democrats aren't socialists. America will never be France." I want to answer that seriously, step by step.

Start with a simple observation. Look at what has gotten cheaper in America over the last 25 years: TVs, phones, software, clothes, toys. Now look at what has exploded: college tuition, healthcare, childcare, housing.

What separates the two lists? The first lives in competitive markets. The second is exactly where government is most involved: subsidies, mandates, licensing, zoning, regulation.

College. Washington lends students almost unlimited money. Universities know the money will always come, so they raise tuition and hire more administrators. The student pays the bill for twenty years. More government money, higher prices.

Housing. Why can't a nurse buy a home in the city where she works? Not because of capitalism. Because of zoning laws, permits, environmental reviews, years of procedure to build a single building. The most expensive places to live in America are the places where it's hardest to build. When building is nearly illegal, prices explode.

Healthcare. The patient almost never sees the price. A third party pays, regulations limit who can compete, and costs climb year after year with no one able to say no.

So here is the trap. The problems you suffer from are not the failure of free markets. They are the places where the market has already been replaced by the state. And the solution you're being offered is more of the same.

That's the Trojan horse. It always works the same way. A real problem. A generous-sounding promise. A program that makes things worse. Then the failure of that program becomes the argument for the next one. People who lived under communism in Poland learned to recognize the lie and the mask the lie wears. The lie never presents itself as a lie. It presents itself as compassion.

In France we are at the end of that road. Debt we can never repay. Young people who can't afford a home. Our best people leaving. And every few years our cities burn. Nobody voted for this. They voted for one more generous promise, fifty years in a row.

If you're a Republican, share this with the Democrat in your life. Not to win an argument. To start a conversation.

If you're a Democrat, I'm not asking you to switch teams. I'm asking you to look at the pattern. Wherever the state took over, life became unaffordable. Don't fix the failures of government with more government.

Stay American. Ask for less state, not more.

The strategic significance is real, but the distinction between an announced commitment and a bankable project matters.

Taiwan's proposed 6 million tonnes per year represents 30% of Alaska LNG's planned capacity. Its potential $4.4 billion investment could strengthen the project's financing prospects.

But the investment terms remain under negotiation, and a binding LNG purchase agreement has not been confirmed.

For Taiwan, Alaska offers geographic diversification and a Pacific route that avoids several existing maritime chokepoints.

It does not eliminate the vulnerability of LNG deliveries to the island itself.

For Washington, the question is whether geopolitical commitments can become commercially viable, financeable infrastructure.

I'd watch binding offtake contracts, delivered LNG pricing, final investment decisions and construction milestones.

Energy security is not secured when a deal is announced. It is secured when reliable supply can actually be delivered.

Blind and visually impaired military veterans took part in Washington, D.C.’s Army Ten-Miler, a major 10-mile running event, with the help of AI-powered smart glasses and human guides. The race took place on October 11, 2026, despite heavy rain. The veterans showed incredible determination as they took on the challenge with support from technology and people working alongside them. Their achievement is an inspiring example of how people with vision loss can participate in major sporting events with the right assistance.

The AI smart glasses, developed by Meta, can describe objects and surroundings aloud, helping people who are blind or visually impaired understand more about the world around them. Depending on the task, the glasses can help users identify objects, read text and get additional information about what is nearby. During the race, human guides from Achilles International also supported the veterans. This combination of AI technology and human guidance was important because the glasses provide useful information, while guides offer personal support and help runners navigate the course.

This inspiring story highlights how artificial intelligence and assistive technology can improve accessibility and help people with disabilities take on new challenges. For blind and visually impaired veterans, such technology could also be useful in everyday activities, from reading signs to identifying objects and understanding their surroundings. However, AI glasses are tools that support people, not complete replacements for human assistance. The veterans’ achievement sends a powerful message about determination, inclusion and innovation.

text:
Lessons 7-9 from the Divine Office for The Motherhood of the Blessed Virgin Mary (The Divine Maternity of Our Lady) Luke 2: 43-51; Homily 1 on the Praises of the Virgin Mother by St. Bernard the Abbot.
.
At that time, when they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind in Jerusalem; and Joseph and His mother knew not of it. But they, supposing Him to have been in the company, went a day's journey; and they sought Him among their kinsfolk and acquaintance. And when they found Him not, they turned back again to Jerusalem, seeking Him. And it came to pass, that after three days they found Him in the temple, sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them, and asking them questions. And all that heard Him were astonished at His understanding and answers. And when they saw Him, they were amazed: and His mother said unto Him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, Thy father and I have sought Thee sorrowing. And He said unto them, How is it that ye sought Me? wist ye not that I must be about My Father's business? And they understood not the saying which He spake unto them. And He went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them.
_________________________
Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? Mary called God, the Lord of Angels, her son. Which of the angels would have dared to do so? It is enough for them, and they reckon it is a great thing, that, being naturally spirits, they should receive the grace of being made and called angels, as witness David: Who maketh spirits his angels. But Mary, knowing herself to be his Mother, doth boldly apply the word Son to that Majesty whom the angels do serve with awe; neither doth God despise to be called what he hath made himself. For a little after, the Evangelist saith: And he was subject unto them. Who to whom? God to men. I say that God, unto whom the angels are subject, and who is obeyed by the Principalities and Powers, was subject to Mary.
Marvel thou at both these things, and choose whether to marvel most at the sublime condescension of the Son, or at the sublime dignity of Mary. Either is amazing, either marvellous. That God should obey this woman, is a lowliness without parallel; that this woman should rule over God, an exaltation without match. In praise of virgins, and of virgins only, is it sung that These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. Of what praise then thinkest thou that she must be worthy who even leadeth the Lamb? O man, learn to obey. O earth, learn to submit. O dust, learn to keep down. It is of thy Maker that the Evangelist saith: And he was subject unto them. Blush, O proud ashes. God humbleth himself; and dost thou exalt thyself? God is subject unto men; and wilt thou, by striving to rule over men, set thyself before thy Maker?
O happy Mary, lowly and virgin; and wondrous virginity, which motherhood destroyed not, but exalted; and wondrous lowliness, which the fruitful virginity took not away, but ennobled; and wondrous motherhood, which was both virgin and lowly. Which of them is not wondrous? which of them is not unexampled? and which of them doth not stand alone? The wonder would be if thou wert not puzzled at which to wonder most―motherhood in a virgin, or virginity in a mother; a motherhood so exalted, or lowliness in such exaltation. But indeed more marvellous than any one of these things is the combination of them all, and without all comparison, it is more excellent and more blessed to have received them all, than to have received any one of them alone. What wonder is it that God, of whom we see and read, that He is wonderful in his holy places, should have shewn himself wonderful in his Mother? O ye that be married, honour this incorruption in corruptible flesh; O holy maidens, gaze in wonder at motherhood in a maid; O, all mankind, take pattern by the lowliness of the Mother of God.

“Aesthetically, the two designs overlap in the qualities that many people find alienating, even though their formal languages differ.
Both prioritize mass, solidity, and scale over lightness, transparency, or human proportion. The Germania plan presents a continuous field of heavy classical forms—a giant dome, long axial avenues, and monumental blocks that dwarf the individual. The Obama Center tower presents a single, faceted, mostly opaque volume that rises as a solid presence with limited openings. In both cases the dominant visual impression is of weight and enclosure rather than openness or invitation. That shared quality of heaviness is what registers as “stark” to many observers.
The emotional response follows from the form. Large solid masses with restricted views or entry points commonly produce a sense of imposition or coldness. Critics of the tower describe it as forbidding, prison-like, or mausoleum-like; critics of Speer’s schemes describe them as oppressive and inhuman. These reactions are not identical in detail—one often evokes institutional or bunker-like associations, the other imperial or processional ones—but they converge on the same broad aversion: the buildings feel designed to dominate rather than accommodate everyday life. Preference data and public commentary consistently favor environments that offer visual variety, smaller scales, and clearer connections between inside and outside. Neither design prioritizes those traits.
The difference that remains is in the specific visual vocabulary. Germania’s mass is organized through classical rhythm, symmetry, and vertical emphasis (columns, dome, arch). The tower’s mass is organized through angular facets, irregular voids, and a continuous stone surface. A viewer can dislike both for the same reason (they feel heavy and closed) without the two images matching. Aesthetic judgment operates on overall impression and emotional effect”. -Super Grok
