text:
Revelations alleged flydubai co-pilot was 'influenced' by Melbourne extremism
Shock links between imam at taxpayer funded Islamic centre and convicted terrorist
Bombshell new revelations expose the alarming ties between the Melbourne Islamic centre linked to the 9/11-style flight hijacker and its leader’s previous support for Osama bin Laden.

Oscar Godsell and Peta Credlin
The Melbourne imam behind the Islamic centre linked to the alleged flydubai hijacker, which has been given hundreds of thousands in taxpayer dollars, has ties to one of Australia's worst terrorists.

Islamic Information and Services Network of Australasia (IISNA), an entity connected to MyCentre, has been embroiled in the FlyDubai terror plot amid allegations copilot Hamam al-Hammami was radicalised while living in Melbourne.

The leader of IISNA, Sheikh Samir Mohtadi – also known as Abu Hamza – previously gave evidence in the terrorism trial involving Abdu Nacer Benbrika, who was convicted of intentionally being the leader of a terrorist organisation.

In 2008, it was reported Mr Mohtadi knew Benbrika for 15 years, having once been close friends and learning “a lot” about Islam from him.

Under cross-examination at the Benbrika trial, Mr Mohtadi said he agreed Osama bin Laden had been regarded as a good man by many Muslims including himself.

He also acknowledged that he watched videos of beheadings.

Mr Mohtadi has broken his silence about the international terrorism probe in a social media video, saying he was a victim of "false allegations".

"Those who are righteous, they’ve always been attacked, abused, accused, killed, imprisoned … and this is the way it is,” he said in a video.

"Regardless how much you explain yourself to people, they’re fixated with their ideas and you can’t change them. So the best thing sometimes is not to say anything.
Allah did not tell the prophet to defend himself, to go and defend yourself. No, no, no.
Despite links to the known terrorist, MyCentre, which lists Mr Mohtadi as a leader, has been given hundreds of thousands of dollars in taxpayer grants.

This includes $68,000 in federal grants for multiculturalism funding from the Albanese government.

https://t.co/rYaUbMhTew can also reveal IISNA received $393,000 in funding from the Victorian government for the construction of a Centre for Muslim Women’s Well-being.

The Albanese government has acknowledged there remain “reasonable questions” about the funding arrangements.

The grants were given despite Mr Mohtadi’s public links to the convicted terrorist leader.
“Doesn’t matter what you say or what you do … they’re going to continue on accusing you, abusing you, making false accusations.”
Scrutiny of the government’s grants to MyCentre has also brought attention back to Mr Mohtadi’s history of public statements about Israel, Zionism and the Australian government.

In sermons and social media posts previously reported by The Australian, he described Zionists as “scavengers” and “bloodsuckers”.

“We don’t believe in a state called Israel … every righteous human being believes there is Palestine and there is no Israel,” he said.

“I’ve always said and I’ve always believed that these Zionists are not normal … They are bloodsucking human beings … They’re scavengers. They are not humans, I swear by Allah.”

“Inshallah, they all go back to Russia, Ukraine, America and Britain … and that Palestine is pure from these filthy terrorist Zionists.”

He then called on Allah to grant him one final wish: “Oh Allah … give me the ability to pray in Masjid al-Aqsa and to free Palestine from the terrorist Zionists”.

AFP investigates Flydubai pilot’s Australian links

Meanwhile, the Australian Federal Police has begun examining any domestic links between Mr Al-Hammami and the plot to crash a plane into an Israeli airport.

UAE prosecutors have alleged Mr al-Hammami became acquainted with individuals associated with MyCentre while studying in Melbourne in 2017.

Attorney-General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi said Mr al-Hammami had provided a detailed confession following his arrest over the alleged September 30, 2026, mid-air attack.

The UAE authorities allege the pilot’s radicalisation began while he was studying in Melbourne in 2017, when he was exposed to extremist literature and propaganda.

“The findings indicated that signs of his drift towards extremism and terrorism first emerged in 2017, while he was studying in Australia,” Mr al-Shamsi said.

“He was influenced by Takfiri ideology through reading extremist literature and following online content glorifying terrorist organisations and suicide attacks.”

https://t.co/rYaUbMhTew does not suggest any connection between Mr Al-Hammami and Mr Mohtadi, or that Mr Al-Hammami was radicalised at My Centre, only that the UAE Attorney-General said the pilot confessed to becoming acquainted with individuals connected to the centre at the time he was allegedly radicalised.

Sheikh Samir Mohtadi has overseen the expansion of an Islamic community organisation in Melbourne.

Mr Mohtadi has been identified on MyCentre’s website as its community leader and imam.

The organisation says it is working to build Australia’s largest Islamic centre, with plans to expand its facilities in Melbourne’s northern suburbs.

The centre’s website traces its origins to the Islamic Information and Services Network of Australasia (IISNA), founded by Mr Mohtadi.

The organisation now offers religious education, school programs, sporting facilities, counselling and other community services.

The controversy has raised questions about taxpayer funding received by MyCentre, which operates through Multicultural Youth Centre Ltd, a registered charity.
GrantConnect records show MyCentre received an initial grant of $36,960 on March 19, 2024, which was published on GrantConnect on June 11 that year.

A subsequent variation, published on December 11, 2025, increased the grant by $31,176.20, giving it a new end date of December 19, 2028.

Home Affairs has said multicultural grants are administered under the Commonwealth Grants Rules and Principles 2024 and the government’s grants framework.

The department said allegations about recipients are tested, responses considered and applications assessed against grant objectives and conditions.

Asked about the language-school grant, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said he did not directly manage that part of the program.

“I'll be able to find something out on that. I don't directly manage that part of the program, but it's a reasonable question,” he said.
“We need to make sure that we are making it harder for them to operate in every single way. So that's the principle I'd apply to it.”

The Victorian government also gave $393,000 to Multicultural Youth Centre, to support the construction of a Centre for Muslim Women’s Well-being.

In response to Questions on Notice, the then Allan Labor government said in 2025 that it was “pleased” to have supported the project.

Government under pressure to review grants

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has demanded a review of government grants to multicultural organisations in response to the MyCentre findings.

“The government obviously didn't even conduct simple Google search, let alone ASIO security checks, before handing over taxpayer-funded grants,” she said.

“Labor has handed money to groups
that are trying to divide Australia and may be facilitating extremism because they can't be bothered to do a google search.”
“It is really important that we use every lever we have to be able to make sure that we are denying oxygen to people who want to do us harm.
According to an analysis of GrantConnect data provided to https://t.co/rYaUbMhTew by One Nation, Labor has thrown nearly $400 million at multicultural projects.

The analysis puts the total value of grants categorised as “multiculturalism” at $385.9 million across 2022–23 to 2025–26.

That was compared to just $327.8 million which went to “community safety” projects over the same period.

Of the funding going to multicultural projects, $340.3 million, or 88 per cent, was given to electorates held by Labor at the time of the grants.

That was compared with just $10.9 million, or three per cent, to Coalition-held seats, one per cent to Greens electorates and eight per cent to other divisions.

Also included in the analysis was a breakdown of multiculturalism funding going to organisations linked to various religious groups.

Among the religiously linked grants, Muslim organisations accounted for about $86.7 million, or 30 per cent of the religious total.

That was followed by Jewish organisations at $77.5 million, Christian organisations at $71 million and Hindu organisations at $31.1 million.

The analysis compares those figures with 2021 Census religion data, calculating that Muslim-linked organisations received 9.5 times their share of the population.

Yes, the distribution of the land was not fair according to the population distribution at the time. Maybe they were counting on the repatriation of Jews living abroad, maybe there were other factors. I wasn’t in the room, so I don’t know the reasons and I don’t care.

The point is that the percentage of land was just an excuse, not the real cause of the conflict. The Arab League refused to accept the existence of a separate Jewish state and wanted a single state with Jews under a “protected minority status.”

Their refusal wasn’t just words, and it wasn’t taken to the negotiating table to discuss borders. The day after Resolution 181 passed, Arab paramilitaries attacked Jewish neighborhoods, and a year later, hours after Israel was founded, five countries declared war on it.

So don’t talk to me about unequal land distribution. The issue was never the borders, it was the very existence of a Jewish state.

And before you shift the discussion to Gaza and the West Bank: The Palestinians have been offered the chance to establish a state many times. They themselves rejected it, not Israel.

In the founding charter of the PLO in 1964, three years before the Second Arab–Israeli War, it explicitly states that the organization’s goal is not sovereignty over Gaza and the West Bank, which had been liberated by Egypt and Jordan, but the liberation of the lands of Palestine from Israel. text:
Thousands of Alaskans spent an October day in Wasilla forming winding queues for shuttles and a distant view of the stage, their patience tested by hours of prayers, anthems and speeches from the usual suspects. The scene mixed food trucks with fervent displays of loyalty, all awaiting a figure whose entrance involved music, dance moves and the familiar promise of political redemption. It was a marathon of anticipation that felt both ordinary and oddly heightened for a region accustomed to distant federal attention.

Trump held forth for ninety minutes on resource pipelines, Arctic strategy and the perils of opponents who might throttle development, while labeling Democrats with a pointed nickname and dismissing certain social policies as absurdly mainstream. He pressed voters toward specific candidates for Senate, Congress and governor, arguing only one path offered a realistic win, and called for an end to ranked-choice voting on the ballot. The delivery blended foreign policy boasts with local urgings, delivered to a crowd heavy with Mat-Su politicians and statewide hopefuls.

Such gatherings reveal how endorsements can steer turnout in a state where natural assets remain central to debates, yet the real test lies in whether the energy translates beyond the sports center walls. The mix of adulation and pointed warnings left little doubt about preferred outcomes, even as the day underscored the blend of spectacle and strategy that keeps these events humming.

text:
Palace says no help expected from VP Sara on El Niño response
By Darryl John Esguerra

MANILA – Malacañang on Wednesday said it does not expect Vice President Sara Duterte to help the government address the impact of El Niño, citing her previous statement that she would not share her proposed solution to lowering rice prices because she did not want to help President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.

During a press briefing, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro was asked whether Duterte had reached out to offer ideas on mitigating El Niño’s effects and whether the Palace was open to her suggestions.

“From that statement na ayaw niyang tumulong sa Pangulo, ano mae-expect natin sa Bise Presidente sa pagtulong sa isinasagawa ng Pangulo, sa mga interventions ng gobyerno? Wala tayong lalong maasahan sa Bise Presidente (Given her statement that she does not want to help the President, what can we expect from the Vice President in helping with the President’s initiatives and the government’s interventions? We can expect even less from the Vice President),” Castro said.

Castro recalled Duterte’s earlier remarks on the administration’s promise to sell rice at PHP20 per kilo.

Duterte had said the target was not feasible but claimed she knew how to achieve it, adding that she would not share her proposed solution because she did not want to help the administration.

Castro challenged Duterte to show whether Davao City had been selling rice at PHP20 per kilo outside the administration’s Kadiwa program.

“Hindi lamang po information dissemination ang ginagawa ng administration. Hindi lang sa information dissemination tumitigil ang Pangulo. May aksyon, may pagtulong, may mga ginagawang pamamaraan (The administration is not limited to information dissemination. The President does not stop at information dissemination. There is action, assistance and measures being undertaken),” Castro said.

The government has been preparing interventions to mitigate the anticipated effects of El Niño, including measures to protect water and food supplies and support vulnerable sectors. (PNA)

text:
The Trump administration (especially in its second term starting January 2025) has advanced multiple policies prioritizing biological sex over gender identity in federal policy, with particular focus on minors, women’s sports, the military, and official documents. These actions are often described by supporters as restoring biological reality, protecting women/girls, and restricting low-evidence medical interventions on children; critics view them as restrictions on transgender rights. Outcomes include policy shifts, hospital program suspensions, and favorable court rulings, though many face ongoing litigation.

Core federal policy on sex

On January 20, 2025 (Inauguration Day), Executive Order 14168 (“Defending Women From Gender Ideology Extremism and Restoring Biological Truth to the Federal Government”) established that the U.S. government recognizes only two immutable sexes—male and female—defined by reproductive biology at conception. It directed agencies to use “sex” rather than “gender,” remove materials promoting “gender ideology,” end related federal funding, limit forms to male/female, and base official documents (including passports) on biological sex rather than self-identification. It rescinded several Biden-era orders and dissolved the White House Gender Policy Council. Agencies implemented this across forms, websites, employee groups, and programs.

Youth medical interventions (“chemical and surgical mutilation”)

Executive Order 14187 (January 28, 2025, “Protecting Children from Chemical and Surgical Mutilation”) directed an end to federal funding, sponsorship, or promotion of puberty blockers, cross-sex hormones, and surgeries intended to alter sex characteristics in those under 19. It tasked HHS with reviewing the evidence and taking steps (including via Medicare, Medicaid, grants, and research funding) to restrict the practices.

HHS released a major evidence review concluding that the benefits of these interventions for minors are uncertain/low-quality, with risks of irreversible effects (infertility, sexual dysfunction, bone density issues, etc.), aligning with findings from the UK’s Cass Review and shifts in several European countries. Subsequent CMS rules ended federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for such procedures on minors (effective around mid-October 2026, with limited tapering for existing hormone therapy). HHS also proposed barring hospitals from performing them as a condition of Medicare/Medicaid participation and issued declarations that they do not meet professional standards.

In response, dozens of hospitals and health systems (White House claims 30–40+; reporting confirms multiple major ones including Kaiser Permanente, various Children’s Hospitals, NYU Langone, UPMC, Cleveland Clinic, Mount Sinai, and others) suspended or ended pediatric programs. The Justice Department reached settlements with at least six major systems in which they agreed to stop the treatments for minors, pay fines, and in some cases offer care related to side effects or detransition.

Women’s sports and Title IX
A February 5, 2025 executive order directed enforcement of Title IX to reserve women’s sports and related facilities for biological females and to investigate non-compliant entities. Athletic organizations including the NCAA and U.S. Olympic bodies adjusted policies.

On June 30, 2026, the Supreme Court upheld state laws (Idaho and West Virginia) allowing exclusion of biological males from female school sports teams. The Court was unanimous that the bans do not violate Title IX and held 6-3 that they do not violate the Equal Protection Clause, stating that states may maintain separate women’s/girls’ sports based on biological sex to ensure fairness and safety. This supports similar laws in roughly two dozen other states. Trump publicly called it a major win.

text:
Cinematic aerial drone film, 30 seconds, of the Vijayanagara capital Hampi at its peak in the early 1500s. Use the uploaded reference images as the base for the architecture, granite boulder landscape, and temple layouts. Rebuild every structure as complete and newly built, with no ruins: fresh carved granite, painted stucco on the gopurams, silk banners, brass lamps and flower decorations everywhere. The city is crowded and busy with people of the Vijayanagara Empire.

Style: photorealistic, epic historical film, golden-hour sunlight, warm saffron and gold tones, soft haze over the Tungabhadra River, smooth gimbal-stabilized drone movement, 24fps, shallow atmospheric depth, rich textures, 4K detail.

People and costume: men in white and ochre dhotis with angavastram shawls, turbans, and tall kullayi caps for nobles. Women in bright Kanchipuram-style silk saris in red, green, and gold, with jasmine strands in their braids, gold temple jewelry, nose rings, and bangles. Priests with sacred thread and vibhuti marks. Merchants in fine cotton and silk.

Flowers throughout: marigold and jasmine garlands strung across streets and temple doorways, lotus offerings, rangoli kolam patterns at entrances, rose and marigold petals falling through the air, flower sellers with heaped baskets.

SCENE-BY-SCENE (30 seconds)
Scene 1 (0–4s), The river and the city reveal @[Image 1](image_1) (Tungabhadra / boulder landscape)
The drone rises slowly over the Tungabhadra River at sunrise. Round coracle boats carry pilgrims with flower baskets across the water. The camera tilts up to reveal the vast golden boulder hills and the sprawling city beyond, smoke from temple lamps drifting upward.

Scene 2 (4–8s), Virupaksha Temple worship @[Image 3](image_3): ( Virupaksha gopuram and courtyard)
The drone glides toward the towering painted gopuram of Virupaksha Temple, hung with marigold garlands. It descends into the courtyard, where hundreds of devotees offer flowers and coconuts, priests wave brass aarti lamps, bells ring, and petals scatter in the air.

Scene 3 (8–13s), Hampi Bazaar, gems and gold @[Image 7](image_7) (: Hampi Bazaar / pillared street mandapas)
The camera tracks low down the long colonnaded bazaar street. Merchants under the stone mandapas display open heaps of rubies, emeralds, diamonds and pearls on silk cloths, measuring gems on brass scales. Goldsmiths craft necklaces at small anvils. Traders from Persia and Portugal in foreign dress bargain with local merchants. The street is packed with shoppers, flower sellers, spice and silk stalls, and cotton awnings in saffron and red.

Scene 4 (13–18s), Royal elephants (@[Image 6](image_6): Elephant Stables)
The drone sweeps past the domed Elephant Stables as a line of royal war elephants walks out. They are decorated with gold-embroidered caparisons, brass bells, painted foreheads, and silver howdahs, with mahouts seated on their necks. Children throw flower petals as they pass.

Scene 5 (18–23s), Soldiers and cavalry (@[Image 4](image_4): Mahanavami Dibba / royal enclosure)
A wide aerial view of the royal enclosure and the great stone Mahanavami platform. Columns of Vijayanagara soldiers march in formation with spears, curved swords and round shields, wearing red and white tunics. Cavalry on Arabian horses with ornate saddles and plumes trot in disciplined rows. The king watches from the decorated platform under a white royal parasol.

text:
Part 2 of the Second Task Arc. The previous part can be found below.

Tales Before The Second Task - Research and Relaxation -

The Library of Hogwarts sprawled as far as the eye could see, hundreds upon hundreds of rows of halls made up by thousands of shelves and a hundredfold that of books in each one. Within it, students of all ages could be seen frolicking about, some with stacks of parchment as wide and tall as they were, most there for an assignment or other whilst others were clearly there for the sake of curiosity and a yearning for knowledge. 

Harry'd seldom been the second. Necessity had been a companion of his when it came to reading: He simply did not enjoy doing so for leisure. For him, relaxation entailed Quidditch, speaking with his friends, or generally getting to know those around him. He was fond of pranks and magical toys and dueling and the defense of magical objects, moreso the application of them rather than the theory behind them. 

So seeing him in the Library was a rare sight, and seeing him without Granger or Weasley? Even rarer indeed. Today then was the rarest of sights, for Harry came into the Library neither alone nor with his friends. Instead, he'd come in with a certain girl of platinum hair and silver eyes, silver eyes which flitted to and fro anxiously, hoping none would catch them. 

Draceana Malfoy had insisted she'd come help him, a few days now after the both of them had snuck out into the Prefects' bathroom. He'd spent the days mulling about the song they'd heard, and though he'd asked Hermione and Ronnie about it, the two of them hadn't really managed to help him with the preparations of the task. Though they'd spent ages looking and asking about, they'd found nothing. So finally he sought to look for it himself. 

The prospect of 'himself', however, soon became moot. It wasn't a week or so into his research that Malfoy herself had come to him, pulling him away in the midst of the halls whilst they roamed from one class to the next. 

"Any progress?" She'd ask, curt and to the point, and when he'd shrugged she'd frowned ever so deeply. "This isn't a game, Potter."

"I'm well aware, Dracy." He'd started using that nickname more and more, as of late. It always made her pause. "But I've no leads. And even Hermione wasn't able to help me, in the Library."

Draceana's face had soured greatly. "Please. As if Miss Know-It-All would've found it, anyways." He rolled his eyes against her comment. Even though their relationship had shifted in the way it had, she still couldn't help but jab at his friends from time to time. At least now he could more easily shut her up. He was about to move to do so when her hand pressed against his collar, and with a cutting gaze did his aspirations cease.

"Not now, Potter. This is important. Far more important. We're going to the Library." She gave him a knowing look, her hands squeezing upon his chest, fingers trailing up to take hold of his scarf. 

"Must we? Like I said, I already went with Hermione." He asked, with a groan. He'd rather go around the entire grounds asking every ghost and portrait before stepping another foot in the Library. 

"We must and we shall. Clearly you and that..." The girl bit at her tongue, cleared her throat, and continued. "Friend of yours missed something. Meet me after supper. I'm free today, as it were." 

Harry gave a resigned nod, and Malfoy pulled him down by that scarf then, pressing her lips against his for a short but heated little moment before shoving him back. "Now get out of my sight. I can only stand your glasses knocking against the bridge of my nose for so long."

She was blushing whilst smirking. So was he, as he rolled his eyes and pushed past her and into the hall once more.

The rest of the day had been uneventful, other than that moment in the Great Hall where Seamus had said something that'd made Veronica laugh right as she was taking a barbaric bite out of a chicken-leg, which caused her to choke and wheeze in the middle of the table. He and Hermione had had to slap her on the back rather hard before she coughed up the meal, and she'd been all pouty for a good two minutes after before Seamus'd gotten another rise from them all. 

After dinner everyone parted ways and he found himself face to face with Malfoy at the appointed time, the girl tapping at her foot impatiently whilst she leant against a pillar right outside the Library, in the hall. 

"You're late." She'd huffed, giving him a rather nasty glare.

"I'm ten minutes early!" 

"Which is twenty minutes late. One ought to be punctual when scheduling a date."

He lifted a brow, a half-smile on his face. "A date? Is that what this is?"

Malfoy shrugged, flipping her hair to one side with a swish of her hand. "It's a study-date, yes. Please, Potter, do you think me so shy as to balk at the prospect? Now come. The sooner we start, the more candlelight we can burn. And the better I can prove that the Granger girl needs those thick bottle-bottoms more than you do."

Harry'd let out the softest of laughs and followed the girl to the Library anon. Thus had they arrived, and thus had the rarest sight of all been granted to those who cared to look, of which only a couple were there. 

They'd spent the first half hour or so searching around for anything to do with the Black Lake, mermen, and ways of breathing underwater. The same parameters that Harry had spent hours on with Hermione a week or so back, even conscripting Ronnie anytime the girl wasn't busy.  The next hour after that was spent poring over the gathered texts. Several spells came to mind, but all of them were either just a bit too difficult to consistently incant in the space of what were now only a scant few weeks to learn them. The ones that weren't were too short in nature, all of them listing but a few minutes of respite amidst murk before needing reincantation, or worse still needed lengthy repeats which might spell certain doom if he wasn't ready or able to do them. 

"What about this one?" Harry'd said, pressing open the page of a book that hadn't quite been worn down by time and thousands of fingers just yet. "Scuba-Spells. You think anyone here would be able to teach me?"

Draceana rolled her eyes at the sight, gently bapping the boy in the forehead with her knuckle. "No, you scar-headed fool. Not unless we know someone who's been here from the Red Sea, and I doubt they'll be able to condense a few months' worth of course-teaching in days!" She'd sighed, looking down at the tome she'd pried open, full of potions and brews. 

"There isn't a single potion for it. Not a one! With how many magical creatures of water there are, you'd have thought the Wizarding World would be prescient enough to study more on the matters of living under waters!" She huffed, rubbing at her temples. "There's no mention of any charms for it, either. None that fit our criteria." 

There was another sigh there, a shake of her head. "There's the bubblehead charm, maybe. But it's too complicated, and more than that it'd impair your sense of sound and sight."

"Why would that matter?" Harry interrupted her, to which Draceana shushed him, pressing her finger against his lip. 

"What if you need to see in there, you idiot? No, there's nothing. Nothing!" She was incensed now, huffy all the way. Harry looked besides themselves, checking for anyone, before pressing a hand to her cheek. She stopped, staring at him.

"...Harry?"

She'd said his name.

"It'll be alright. We'll get to the root of it, I'm sure." His voice was sweet. Low. Soft. For a moment, Draceana pondered: Was she the first to ever hear this tone, from him? Jealousy might've threatened her then, but she was too lost in his eyes. 

Then, something clicked, and she parted from him, a devilish little smirk upon her lips. 

"Wait here."

And off she ran, with steps that were sure and confident, and a certain billow to her hair and her robes which made her look utterly gorgeous to him in the dim candlelight. 

She came back a few minutes after, holding a herbology book in her hands. Harry frowned at it. "What's plants gonna help us with, here?" He asked, incredulous. 

"What's the main component for most potions and potables, Potter?"

He blinked. "But you said there weren't any..."

"No, of course not! But we can approximate by searching for the source. The... 'root', of the problem, didn't you say?" She was grinning now, and it reminded him of Professor Lupin's fanged grimace, that night in which he'd transformed before them. 

She opened the book then, sat down beside him, and pressed herself close. Then, the two of them worked, poring over its pages and indexes, searching for anything that might work.

It was another hour before they'd found it. By then, the hour of night had come, and the halls had grown quiet. Within them, Draceana continued to work, whilst a certain green-eyed-boy laid his head against her shoulder, her scarf wrapped around the both of them, and his eyes peacefully closed.

He'd fallen asleep. The nerve of him! And she'd let him, of course. Weak enough to slumber as he was, she'd seen no reason not to. Besides, it allowed her to get a look at his features without those thick-rimmed spectacles, to study him for further weakness.

To memorize the way his lips opened ever so slightly as he began to dream. To memorize the pace of his breath, or the way his eyes closed. To memorize his smell, so close to her. His warmth.

But she'd finally found it. There, hidden amidst the almanac. Gillyweed. A common magical component whose name she never quite took particular interest in until tonight, and which seemed dreadfully obvious in retrospect. No wonder that mudblooded Granger had missed it, likely too focused on everything complex and naught simple. 

She'd found it. She just had to wake him up, now. To tell him, and that'd be that. They'd part ways, head to their Common Rooms, and tomorrow would be just as ever.

But he looked so peaceful, there. So handsome. Had he always been this handsome? She'd always thought he was cute, deep down. A gem in the rough, tarnished as he might've been by the company he kept. But now? Now he seemed utterly gorgeous to her, with his thin lips and his messy hair and his oddly long lashes, and his sharp nose and those slightly puffy cheeks still indicative of the growing of a young boy into a young man. 

So defenseless, too. What would she had given to have this opportunity, years prior? She would've done him such great mischief then! Hexed his shoelaces together, drawn a big "Stinky!" on his forehead, or maybe even simply left a slug upon his chest. 

A few years prior, he probably wouldn't be caught dead showing this side of himself to her.

"You idiot..." She muttered, running her hands across his bangs so, so carefully. "...don't you know I'm the evil Queen Serpent of Slytherin, Potter...? Acting so defenseless near me..."

She pulled herself down, the pace of her breath quickening, her heart following suit. He was so close. She had to crane her neck awkwardly, but she didn't care. So close. 

"...I've waited so long for you to be mine." She muttered. And it was true. Her friend. Her lackey. Her toy. Her pet. The first day she'd seen him, amidst the Tailor shop, she'd found herself utterly struck by him. His eyes, his scar, the legend that she'd heard time and time again, beneath him. It was why she'd offered her hand to him, that day. Offered him a place amongst her. 

His rejection had stung. More than that, it'd enraged her. How dare he, she'd thought. How dare he besmirch her gifts.

How dare he make her work so hard for this.

How dare he make her obsess for so long, stalking him across the grounds, following his every step.

How dare he force her to notice more and more about him. How dare he take so long to ask her out.

How dare he make her... enjoy him, so much.

And now that they'd kissed. Now that their feelings had been laid bare --not spoken, never spoken, for if they were spoken the spell would break--, she had ridiculed herself time and time again for him. She'd kept pulling him out of sight every chance she could, every day if she could, though often that wasn't the case. He was always orbited by someone, be it the Weasley and Granger girls or the odious twins or any number of followers and admirers and friends and Housemates. 

But he was alone here and there, often enough that she could skirt away and pull him with. Often enough that she could steal his lips under the guise of torturing him, even though in reality she just wanted to obsess over their texture just as she had every other part of him for years on end.

He was so defenseless.

Her lips were so near to his, again. Her breath hot against his face, mirrored in her own.

Draceana Malfoy kissed her Sleeping Beauty. She kissed him slowly, careful not to wake him. Felt his lips, slightly dry, against her own. Felt the knock of his nose on her cheek, the warmth of his cheeks upon her own. He stirred, and she pulled back, wrapping a careful set of arms around him and burying herself into his hair. He smelled like treacle tart, like wood and fresh soaps. He felt like home, to her, so much so that for a moment she thought she might cry, holding him tight as she could without waking him.

She'd missed her home terribly, the first few weeks at Hogwarts. Home to her was right, where she'd been raised and where she'd had her status and her self understood. It meant everything to her, and Potter... he felt like it, to her! Like home, the home she sometimes yearned for, the home she sometimes found herself missing so much she could cry over it! 

Draceana took a deep breath, chewing at her lip and rubbing her fingers against his arm. She kissed at his forehead, at his temple. She did it for no reason at all, because he wasn't awake to tease her and because they were truly alone in the library this late at eve. But Madam Irma would soon come, and the spell would be shattered. But it wasn't quite time for that yet-- curfew hadn't quite started, and she'd already handled the convincing of that witch Madam Pince that the two of them were doing very important studies for Professor Snape's class-- so she had some level of leeway.

Surely... it'd be fine, right? In a few minutes she'd wake him, and tell him about the weed, and they'd figure out how to procure it, to keep him safe in the Task ahead. But for now...

For now, Draceana kissed him again, as careful as she could, and held him against herself. For now, Draceana let herself relax, closing her eyes and telling herself that she'd just be a moment. That she just wanted to rest and properly drink it all in.

Later, Madam Irma would find the two of them wrapped up in each other, scarf carefully tied between their necks, and would wake the two of them with a sharp snap of her featherduster against her hands and a whisper-thin hiss from her lips. The two of them would start, and they'd be scolded severely for undue fraternization in the library, and for a smudge on one of the books which Harry would later swear she'd made up just for the sake of punishing them. They would leave the Library fifteen minutes after that, red in the face and teary in the eyes from the embarrassment and the frustration.

As they walked through the halls after on the way to their Common Rooms, Draceana would let out a deep sigh, hands still shaky from the fright.

"I found it." She'd comment, looking towards Harry with a sheepish, mortified smile. 

"You... You found it? Really?!"

"Yes. I did. Gillyweed. It helps you grow gills-- works for an hour, too. Perfect for what you'll need."

"Blimey... How did me and Hermione miss that?"

She smiled, then, forgetting her embarrassment and grabbing him by the shoulder and pushing up to kiss him on the cheek, thankful for their similar heights and even more thankful to her mother for her inherited tall stature. 

"Do not come back broken, Harry." She whispered against his ear, sending shivers down his spine.

"You wouldn't do quite so good as my favorite toy if you were to come back broken."

She was clutching him tight, at the lapel. Her lips were curled into that villainous smirk, but her eyes... her eyes were pleading. Honest.

Harry smiled at the girl, pressing a hand to her own, squeezing there tight.

"I promise."

To her. To Hermione. To Veronica. To all of those who believe in him.

To all of those who helped him.

To Draceana, who smiled and pet him on the head in a way that made him huff at her and pulled back to a jolly step, skipping her way right down the halls with a lightness he'd seldom seen in her. One that was dignified and regal as ever, of course, but which had a noticeably subtle bounce on each step. 

Yet, something still troubled him, even as she walked away.

The song. 

And while you're searching, ponder this.
We've taken what you'll sorely miss.
An hour long you'll have to look, 
To recover what we took.

text:
THE CONNECTION BETWEEN MAN AND THE ELEMENTAL WORLD

The elements—Earth, Water, Air, and Fire—are not mere physical substances but primordial forces, each bearing its own intelligence and hierarchy of beings. Paracelsus named them the gnomes of Earth, the undines of Water, the sylphs of Air, and the salamanders of Fire. These are not fairy-tale creatures but the living intelligences of the elemental planes, the formative powers that shape the mineral, vegetable, and animal kingdoms. They operate according to the laws of their own spheres, largely unconscious of higher purposes, yet they respond to the directed will and imagination of the human being who has begun to awaken.

Man’s connection to this world is rooted in his own constitution. The physical body is woven of the densest condensations of the four elements. The etheric or vital body is the living web of elemental forces that animates it. In every breath the sylphic currents move; in the circulation of blood the undine rhythms flow; in the heat of metabolism the salamandric fire burns; and in the solidity of bone and tissue the gnomes maintain form. When consciousness remains identified solely with the personal ego, these forces operate automatically, often in conflict or excess. When consciousness begins to rise into the higher self, man becomes capable of entering into conscious relationship with them.

This relationship is not one of domination but of reciprocal service and recognition. The elemental beings require the light of human consciousness to evolve beyond their instinctive cycles; man requires their cooperation to restore the harmony of his own nature and of the Earth itself. In the alchemical tradition this is expressed as the purification and recombination of the elements within the vessel of the soul. Earth is fixed and made transparent; Water is purified of emotional turbidity; Air is clarified into true thought; Fire is tempered into spiritual will. The result is the birth of the quintessence—the fifth element—within the human being, the point at which the elemental world is redeemed and raised.

Mystically, this connection is enacted through the imagination. Not fantasy, but the disciplined, living imagination that is the true organ of spiritual perception. When the mind is stilled and the heart opened, the elemental realms become visible not as external objects but as inner landscapes and presences. A stone reveals the slow, patient intelligence of Earth; a flame shows the aspiring, transforming nature of Fire; the movement of wind carries the thought-forms of Air; the depth of water reflects the soul’s own fluidity. In ritual, in meditation, and in conscious living, the human being offers the elements the gift of self-awareness, and in return receives their strength, wisdom, and vitality purified of lower impulses.

There is also a shadow side. When man denies or exploits the elemental world without recognition, the forces become distorted. Earth hardens into greed and rigidity; Water stagnates into emotional poison; Air scatters into illusion and falsehood; Fire rages into destructive passion. The modern world, in its dissociation from nature and from the subtle planes, has largely severed this conscious link, resulting in both ecological crisis and inner fragmentation. Restoration begins not with external technique alone but with the inner act of recognition: seeing the elemental world as ensouled, and oneself as its responsible steward and co-creator.

Ultimately, the connection between man and the elemental world is a path of mutual evolution. As the individual learns to hold the four elements in balance within himself, he becomes a living temple in which the elemental beings may receive the light of spirit. In this way the ancient maxim is fulfilled: “As above, so below; as within, so without.” Man is the bridge. Through him the elemental world is lifted toward the divine, and through the elemental world the divine descends into living form.

text: Collectors whithout game are not new, but as I I predicted, the ridiculous army of anti-Sony detractors—which formed in the wake of the backlash against the all-digital approach—is out in force with laughable arguments. After all, the practice of selling collector's editions without the game itself included (often referred to as "Collector's Boxes" or "merchandise packs") has become a genuine logistical and commercial trend among publishers. It allows them to distribute a single box worldwide without worrying about platforms (PS5, Xbox, PC) or game languages ​​and region locking. Recent Releases (2024–2026)  • God of War: Laufey – Collector’s Set (2026): Recently unveiled by Sony at a price of €150, this set contains an impressive light-up figure of Faye, a 51-card Oracle deck, and a mini artbook—but no game. • Grand Theft Auto VI – Vice City Edition (2026): Rockstar Games offered a very expensive collector’s version (around $400) featuring sunglasses, a cap, and a figure of the "Macca" mascot, while completely excluding the base game. • Life is Strange: Double Exposure – Collector’s Edition (2024): A Square Enix Store exclusive containing physical items (such as the vinyl soundtrack and an artbook), explicitly sold with the disclaimer "does not contain the game."  Classics and Early Examples  Red Dead Redemption 2 – Collector’s Box (2018): One of the most famous cases. Rockstar marketed a lockable metal crate containing a weapons catalog, playing cards, a puzzle, and a coin, but the game had to be purchased separately. Diablo IV – Limited Collector’s Box (2023): Blizzard sold a massive box set including an electric candle ("Candle of Creation"), a mousepad, a cloth map of Sanctuary, and an artbook for around €100—without a single digital key to play the game. Battlefield 1 – Collector’s Edition (2016): EA offered a premium version featuring a statue of the main character, a deck of cards, and a carrier pigeon transport tube. A specific version of this collector’s set was sold without the game, allowing PC and console players alike to purchase it. Sonic Frontiers – Collector's Edition (Lézard) / Mass Effect Catalyst: Sega and other publishers have occasionally offered alternative versions of their major collector's editions—often through specific retailers or directly on their own websites—that ship only with the statue and the lithographs.

text:
It's been four months since I started going to the gym and my life has changed drastically.⁣

Let me explain how.⁣

My life before the gym was, wake up, pray, work, come online post content, sell, reply DMs and emails, watch movies, complete any task or project I have and do offline routines.⁣

But ever since I started going to the gym, I look forward to stepping outside my house in the morning and evenings.⁣

I build my body, I correct bad postures, I sweat.⁣

My body moves every day on purpose.⁣

Not going to buy some things I may need on some days and call it "I'm moving my body."⁣

This one is intentional. Consistently.⁣

Now, my body is beginning to shape out real good, I have built endurance and strength. Something I wouldn't build from my room.⁣

I get to have conversations with people physically, laugh and engage in physical activities. Doing this alone has disrupted the habits my brain was used to before. Now there's a physical routine to look forward to.⁣

There are people who look forward to seeing me in the gym.⁣

If I don't show up, they reach out.⁣

If I come around, they ask questions while giving me a hug.⁣

I was once the 2nd runner on the leaderboard. Haa. A whole me. I never knew I could be that consistent.⁣

Last year I told God I want my people to find me, physically or online. I love community. I love people.⁣

As much as I love doing things on my own, I also love being part of communities that help people grow.⁣

Na there dem see me.⁣

So far so good I influenced 3 of my neighbors to sign up for the gym.⁣

Just with my lifestyle.⁣

They saw me go to the gym every day.⁣

They cheered me and saw how consistent I was, how fit I was getting every single day and signed up.⁣

My coach said he has something for me at the end of the year for influencing 3 of my neighbors. 😂⁣

I didn't even talk to my neighbors, they saw me show up every day and they got in.⁣

Community.⁣

Building strength.⁣

Positive influence.⁣

That's a breath of fresh air from someone who works from home.⁣

And to be honest, what gave me access to the gym was two things. Good income and a personal decision to start taking my general health seriously.⁣

Na person wey don chop dey enter gym to build muscles.⁣

That gym membership, that consistency, that coach, none of it was free.⁣

It was funded by a skill.⁣

A skill I learnt and turned into something people pay me for.⁣

Content marketing. Copywriting. Knowing how to help businesses sell.⁣

That's what's been paying for my mornings and evenings at the gym.⁣

That's what's been paying for the small luxuries I used to only dream about.⁣

People sleep on learning a skill because they think it's "just content" or "just writing."⁣

But that same skill has quietly funded my gym membership, my bills, my peace of mind, and my ability to say no to clients who don't respect my time.⁣

If you have a skill right now, whatever it is, and you haven't figured out how to turn it into consistent income, you're sitting on something that could fund your own version of the gym.⁣

Your own version of showing up for yourself physically, financially, mentally.⁣

I help people take the skill they already have and turn it into a real, paying offer.⁣

Book a 1:1 skill clarity session and I'll teach you how to use the skill you learnt to land paying clients, people paying for your knowledge.⁣

text:
3.2.1 African Trypanosome – Trypanosoma brucei – African Sleeping Sickness

ID: Trypanosoma brucei 
Cold War spy, expert in deep infiltration into enemy territory. Changes identity every 7–10 days. 
Black trench coat, fedora hat, dark sunglasses.  
Professional Skills: Genetic deception, Disruption of host recognition systems, 
Master of immune hypnosis and silent evasion 
Favorite Book: The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat
(he himself once mistook his surface coat – and swapped it for another VSG) 
Favorite Song: 
The Spy Who Loved Me 
Favorite Movie:
The Man with the Golden Gun 
Life Motto:
"Catch me if you can"
 
   Epidemiology
Trypanosoma brucei is transmitted between hosts by the female tsetse fly. This impressive vector can transport the parasite across vast distances, spanning entire regions of the African continent. If the sandfly - the humble vector of leishmaniasis from the previous chapter - resembles a sputtering motorcycle courier running low on fuel, then the tsetse fly is more like a jumbo jet with in-flight refueling powerful, persistent, and going the distance.
Naturally, the disease is geographically restricted to Africa-specifically sub-Saharan Africa-because that's the only place where tsetse flies live. Since these flies don’t venture beyond the continent, any cases reported elsewhere in the world are limited to travelers. Historically, there have been up to 50 such cases per year, mostly among pilgrims; in recent years, the numbers have dwindled further, with only the occasional unlucky businessperson or overly curious safari tourist making the list.
And in Israel? One case, just one, of a traveler returning from Tanzania has made it into the medical literature. So yes, even we get a footnote.
Less than 1% of tsetse flies in Africa are actually infected with viable trypanosomes-and thank goodness for that. If the rate were any higher, the continent might have been depopulated long ago. Remarkably, the fly itself secretes a cocktail of substances that actively kill many of the parasites it ingests during a blood meal from humans or animals. As admirers of both epidemiology and humanity, we must tip our hats to this unexpected rivalry between two villains: the tsetse fly and the trypanosome. May their mutual sabotage continue.
The illness itself (don’t worry, full details are coming soon) begins with a nasty mix of fever and general malaise during the early stage, when the parasite first enters the body. This is followed by a much more sinister second stage, in which the parasite crosses into the brain and triggers a “sleeping sickness” that ultimately ends in death. In short: not recommended for anyone with a pulse.
There are several subspecies within the broad group of African trypanosomes (T. brucei), including some that mainly infect animals. In humans, however, two subspecies are especially important to differentiate, as the disease they cause differs markedly in its course-particularly in terms of speed of progression, response to treatment, and overall prognosis. 
________________________________________
1. Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
• This is the dominant strain in West Africa.
• Transmitted by the tsetse fly Glossina palpalis, typically found near rivers and other water sources-the fly’s natural habitat.
• It is an anthroponotic disease, meaning transmission occurs primarily between humans, with animals playing only a minor role.
• Historically, tens of thousands of cases were reported each year. In recent years, however, the number has dropped significantly fewer than a thousand cases were reported in 2022 (approximately 750).
• Clinically, the disease caused by T.b. gambiense follows a more prolonged course compared to its eastern counterpart. It’s important not to be misled by the slower progression: untreated, the disease still carries a near 100% mortality rate. The parasite gradually migrates from the blood and lymphatic system to the central nervous system, a process that can take several months or even years.
• Owing to this more gradual progression, treatment typically involves medications that are safer and have fewer side effects than those used for the more aggressive eastern form.
________________________________________
2. Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense
• This is the dominant strain in East Africa.
• Transmitted by the tsetse fly Glossina morsitans, which thrives in dry savanna regions.
• A zoonotic disease: transmission occurs primarily among wild and domestic animals, with humans only occasionally and accidentally caught in the crossfire.
• Much less common than the West African strain-currently, fewer than 100 cases are reported per year. (Thank God!)
• Clinically, this form is far more aggressive. Left untreated, it’s almost universally fatal. The parasite invades the bloodstream and lymphatic system, then rapidly crosses into the brain, usually within weeks.
• Because of this fulminant progression, treatment typically requires highly toxic medications, including arsenic-based compounds (yes, actual poison). Fortunately, safer, and more effective options have been developed in recent years. 
________________________________________
  A Brief but Useful History Lesson
At the dawn of the 20th century, African sleeping sickness was widespread across Central and West Africa, particularly in the Congo region. Annual cases exceeded 50,000, causing devastating health and social consequences.
The Congo offers a telling case study for understanding the disease’s historical trajectory. During the late 19th and early 20th centuries, Congo was under Belgian colonial rule, effectively treated as the personal property of King Leopold II. The colonial regime was notorious for its brutal exploitation of the local population, marked by forced labor, slavery, and severe repression, including violence against those who resisted.
Amid this oppression, one notable positive legacy was the Belgians’ early recognition of vector-borne diseases-ailments transmitted by insects such as tsetse flies and mosquitoes. To protect their officers and soldiers, they implemented systematic vector control measures targeting these insects. Although motivated primarily by self-interest, these campaigns significantly curtailed the spread of sleeping sickness and other diseases like malaria, leading to a substantial decline in cases.
In 1960, known as the year of “Black Africa,” Congo, like many African nations, gained independence. Unfortunately, the following decades saw a sharp reversal. Successive governments, often unstable and preoccupied with internal conflicts, largely neglected healthcare and vector control, diverting scarce resources toward military spending. This neglect precipitated a resurgence of sleeping sickness, with tens of thousands of new cases annually.
Since the turn of the millennium, however, renewed efforts have been made to strengthen public health infrastructure and revive vector control initiatives. International support and improved local campaigns have steadily driven down disease incidence to historically low levels, marking a hopeful chapter in the fight against this deadly illness.
 ________________________________________
  Morphology, Pathology, and Life Cycle
The African Trypanosoma parasite has two main morphological forms (a fancy way of saying two "shapes"), both equipped with a flagellum for movement, a nucleus for basic life decisions, and a kinetoplast - a unique structure made of mitochondrial DNA. But don’t get too emotionally invested: after Leishmania and Trypanosoma, this whole kinetoplast business will fade into the parasitological sunset.
One key point: unlike Leishmania, Trypanosoma brucei has no intracellular form - it never hides inside host cells.

1. Trypomastigote (pictured)
• This is the morphological form present in the human host and responsible for clinical disease. It is detected throughout all stages of infection: initially in the bloodstream and lymphatic system, and later in the cerebrospinal fluid following invasion of the central nervous system.
• A flagellated protozoan measuring approximately 15–20 microns in length - roughly equivalent to the combined length of two adjacent red blood cells.
• Trypomastigotes are found in the blood and lymphatic system-the latter serving as a parallel drainage system for the circulatory system. They appear in two distinct morphological variants: a long, slender form and a shorter, stouter form, commonly referred to as the “short stumpy” form. This morphological distinction has functional relevance in the parasite’s life cycle, as will be discussed in the following section.
________________________________________
2. Epimastigote
• This is the developmental form found within the insect vector, the tsetse fly (Glossina species).
• It possesses a single flagellum and measures approximately 15 microns in length.
• The kinetoplast is located anterior to the nucleus, a distinguishing feature of this stage.
• This form arises in the fly’s midgut and plays a key role in the transition toward the infectious metacyclic stage.
________________________________________
In the bloodstream forms of Trypanosoma brucei (i.e., the trypomastigote stage), the parasite is exposed to host immune defenses and must sustain rapid motility and replication. 
To meet its high energy demands, it relies primarily on glycolysis, utilizing abundant glucose available in the host's bloodstream. This metabolic process occurs within a specialized organelle known as the glycosome. As a result, mitochondrial activity is minimal during this stage, and the kinetoplast - a structure containing mitochondrial DNA - plays a reduced functional role. Correspondingly, it is positioned posterior to the nucleus, distant from the flagellum.
In contrast, during the epimastigote or procyclic stage within the tsetse fly vector, the parasite enters a metabolically less demanding environment. Glucose is scarce in the fly's midgut, so the parasite shifts to an aerobic metabolism based on oxidative phosphorylation via the Krebs cycle, using amino acids as its primary energy source. In this context, mitochondrion becomes functionally active, and the kinetoplast assumes a central role in energy production. Accordingly, it repositions anterior to the nucleus, closer to the base of the flagellum. 
Simplified summary (for those still enrolled in a questionable diploma program somewhere in Eastern Europe):
In the human host, the parasite runs on sugar (glycolysis). In the tsetse fly, it burns proteins (via the Krebs cycle). In other words - life adapts to what's on the menu. ________________________________________
  Pathogenesis (annoying, but leads to understanding the clinical picture)
In the patient’s bloodstream, Trypanosoma exists as two trypomastigote forms: the long slender and the short stumpy. Both swim using a flagellum and generate energy primarily through glycolysis. They express Variable Surface Glycoprotein (VSG) on their surface, a critical factor for immune evasion.
A key difference between these forms is that the long slender trypomastigote-let’s call it the “model in heels”-is the replicative stage, dividing by binary fission: 1 becomes 2, then 4, then 8. It’s all about reproduction. The short stumpy form, by contrast, does not divide-perhaps due to some parasite narcissism, refusing to reproduce when not at its best. However, this stumpy form is essential for transmission, as it is the form taken up by the tsetse fly during a blood meal, allowing the parasite’s life cycle to continue.
Why is VSG expression so important? Because VSG is the primary target of the host’s antibody response. As an extracellular parasite, Trypanosoma is vulnerable to antibody-mediated recognition, leading to clearance by the spleen-the body’s parasite graveyard. However, the parasite is cunning. Monitoring parasite levels in the blood from infection onward reveals a fascinating cyclical pattern.
The parasitemia curve shows recurring waves. Initially, parasite numbers rise rapidly as long slender trypomastigotes multiply. Within hours to days, this surge plateaus as some slender forms differentiate into non-dividing stumpy forms-essential for survival in the tsetse fly vector. Following the plateau, parasite levels sharply decline due to immune clearance, only to surge again and start a new wave. This cycle of rise, plateau, and fall repeats every few days, defining the characteristic oscillations of African trypanosomiasis.
Why does parasite count decline? Because the host’s immune system eventually mounts an effective antibody response. It takes several days, but once antibodies specific to the current VSG variant are produced, they efficiently target and clear the parasites by directing them to the spleen.

What causes parasite levels to rise again? The answer is antigenic variation-the parasite’s clever switch in VSG structure. Although its genome is relatively small, it contains roughly a thousand VSG genes, each encoding a slightly different surface glycoprotein-imagine a wardrobe with a thousand different hats.
The parasite’s big trick is to continuously and randomly switch which VSG gene it expresses by moving a new gene into the active expression site near the genome’s telomere. When antibody levels rise and threaten parasite survival, this switch produces a new parasite population displaying a different VSG variant, unseen by existing antibodies. The immune system then requires days to develop new antibodies.
This ongoing cycle of immune recognition, parasite clearance, and VSG switching drives the characteristic waves of parasitemia. It is an evolutionary arms race: the winner is whoever adapts faster, either the host producing effective antibodies or the parasite changing its disguise. The parasites that survive are those that have perfected frequent VSG switching.
Clinically, these parasitemia waves correspond directly to fever cycles. When parasite levels peak, the inflammatory response triggers a high fever; when parasite numbers drop, the fever subsides. Similar patterns occur in bacteremia, viremia, and fungemia, explaining why blood samples taken during fever spikes are most likely to detect the pathogen.
  Pathogenesis (there was something promised about sleep, wasn’t there?)
In the first stage of African trypanosomiasis, the parasite circulates in the bloodstream and lymphatic system, hence the hemolymphatic stage. The lymphatic system is a drainage network alongside blood vessels, housing immune cells in lymph nodes. When infection occurs, these nodes swell as the immune response activates.
This early stage lasts weeks to months, varying by parasite strain. The West African Trypanosoma brucei gambiense causes a slow, chronic illness, while the East African T. b. rhodesiense leads to a rapid, aggressive disease. Clinically, it features intermittent fever spikes, lymphadenopathy, general malaise, nonspecific rash, and subtle signs that rarely suggest the diagnosis directly.
The most critical moment in the disease occurs when the parasite crosses the blood-brain barrier (BBB), a highly selective border often likened to the Berlin Wall or a geopolitical no-man’s land. This crossing marks the start of the cerebral stage, where the parasite invades the central nervous system and causes encephalitis. Without effective treatment, this stage is invariably fatal.
After crossing the blood-brain barrier, the parasite causes progressive brain inflammation that severely disrupts neurological function. This leads to the classic “sleeping sickness,” marked by severe disturbances of the sleep-wake cycle, behavioral changes, confusion, and eventually coma. Over time, our understanding of these neurological symptoms has evolved from simple explanations to complex neuroimmunology mechanisms.
From early pathologists’ descriptions, we learn that parasite-induced brain inflammation caused a striking and unique feature: numerous inflammatory cells - various leukocytes - were seen surrounding blood vessels in the brain like a sleeve, effectively “strangling” them. This vivid image is simple, easy to grasp, and highly illustrative, yet it reveals the limited understanding of the underlying processes at that time.
Today, we know the process is far more complex. In response to the parasite’s presence in the brain, inflammation affects both the meninges and the brain tissue itself. This is driven by a cascade of signaling molecules - interleukins and leukotrienes - essentially the devil’s names for fever-inducing, immune-activating chemicals, including TNF-alpha, interleukins 1 and 10, and interferon gamma.
It’s all very academic, and anyone daring enough to dive deep into this molecular chaos deserves respect - and maybe a kind escort out of here.

But what’s truly worth remembering about this fierce inflammation that disrupts the brain’s tranquility and inflicts lasting trauma?
At the heart of this storm is a molecule we’ve already met VSG, the Variable Surface Glycoprotein, the parasite’s ever-changing antigen that helps it evade the immune system’s attacks. This cursed glycoprotein drives several immune manipulations, including:
• Antigenic variation-constant camouflage through surface switching
• Inhibition of the complement system, a key arm of immunity responsible for clearing invaders
• Stimulation of inflammatory mediator production, which amplifies the damaging inflammatory response.
• Induction of autoantibodies-antibodies that mistakenly attack the body’s own tissues in response to VSG.
________________________________________
The Character of VSG
Five Things You Wanted to Ask It - But Didn’t, Because You're Not in the Habit of Chatting with Microscopic Sociopaths
(Title abridged for your convenience)
1. Success has many fathers; failure is an orphan.
The molecule has around a thousand genes encoding it.
2. It has attention deficit disorder.
The parasite's restlessness, expressed in a sudden switch of the protein displayed on its surface, prevents the development of an effective vaccine against it. No one has the ability-or financial incentive-to vaccinate against a thousand variants for one disease.
3. Not a desk-job soldier and not a combat one. More like a generic sucker who shows up once a week.
In scientific terms (yeah, right), this refers to a cyclic pattern of rise and fall in parasite levels, occurring approximately every seven days.
4. A true sociopath.
Almost the entire surface of the parasite is covered with VSG.
This is a domineering molecule that refuses to share space.
5. A protein suffering from manic depression.
This protein is not content with frequent structural changes to deceive the enemy-it also suppresses desired inflammatory activity (complement activation) and simultaneously stimulates generalized inflammation (over-secretion of inflammatory mediators), which serves its purpose by causing damage.
________________________________________
  Clinical Features: What I Really Want Is to Sleep
In the days following a tsetse fly bite, a lesion develops at the site where the parasite enters the body. Its official, utterly insufferable name:
chancre – to be pronounced shahn-ker, with pursed lips and a heavy French accent (preferably while squinting dramatically).
The lesion appears 2–3 days after the bite, red, swollen, and tender to touch (or as you might call it – painful). It will disappear after about three weeks.
But don’t worry, that’s just the beginning.
________________________________________
A few days later, short fever spikes (lasting 1–3 days) begin, marking the first phase of the disease – the hemolymphatic stage.
Alongside the fever comes swollen lymph nodes, especially in the posterior cervical triangle – you know, the spot where guys give each other hearty slaps on the neck.
This swelling became known by the historical and hysterical name:
Winterbottom’s sign
The sign was first described by British physician Dr. Thomas Winterbottom, who earned himself a name and a notoriety to match (think eternal fame, just darker).
Dr. Winterbottom noted that enslaved Africans with neck swelling often slipped into sleep and died within weeks, and he used this observation to warn slave traders that these individuals were "defective goods."
Historical context aside, medical slave screening is indefensible in any century or language.
________________________________________
Other nonspecific symptoms of the early stage include:
• Headaches
• A rash (the so-called trypanid rash)
• Muscle and joint pain
• A general sense of "something's off", but turned up to 11.
________________________________________
In the second stage – which kicks in within weeks (T. b. rhodesiense) or months to years (T. b. gambiense) – the real deterioration begins:
• Loss of appetite, sometimes progressing to full-blown anorexia
• Apathy
• Confusion
• Behavioral changes, including episodes of psychosis (think: your fourth-grade teacher when she discovered the whoopee cushion incident)
Later symptoms include:
• Tremors (of the limbs and tongue)
• Neurological decline
• Disrupted sleep cycles – young children dozing off on school benches, adults nodding off anywhere and everywhere for extended periods.
Eventually, seizures may occur (more common in the eastern form of the disease), followed by coma and general deterioration, such as respiratory infections and other complications from complete neglect of the body.
As the sleep disturbances deepen, patients may fall into constant sleep, then a profound coma, and ultimately death, unless aggressive and timely treatment is provided.
The World Health Organization defines stage two of African sleeping sickness as severe when white blood cell count in the cerebrospinal fluid exceeds 100 cells/μL.
They list numerous neurological signs that raise suspicion for advanced disease and the need for targeted therapy, including:
• Confusion
• Bizarre behavior
• Slurred or muddled speech
• Heightened anxiety
• Motor weakness (e.g., dropping a cup)
• Wide-based gait (ataxia)
• Uncontrolled limb movements
• Seizures
________________________________________
  Diagnosis
(Mirror, mirror on the wall – where’s the vile parasite, may his candle flicker and fall?)
In general, it’s always best to identify the parasite directly by observing it in the relevant body compartment. In the case of Trypanosoma brucei, there are three primary sites to sample where trypomastigotes may be seen under the microscope:
1. Blood (both thick and thin smears)
2. Lymph nodes
3. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
Since there are usually only a few parasites per compartment, the diagnosis is easily missed (in scientific language, this means that the sensitivity of microscopic detection is low).
Hence, several techniques are used to increase the number of detectable parasites per unit of volume.
These include injecting the suspected material (like blood) into an experimental animal, allowing the parasite to multiply inside it, making it easier to detect. Another method is examining the buffy coat layer of blood, where parasite concentration is higher.
What is the buffy coat, you ask? Great question.
When blood is separated by density, you get:
• Red blood cells at the bottom
• Plasma at the top
• And in between, the buffy coat – a thin layer containing white blood cells and platelets, where trypomastigotes are often more concentrated.
Finally, there's amplification by electric charge, a historical method (but well beyond what you need to pass this course).
________________________________________
Beyond direct microscopic observation, molecular detection (PCR) can be used to identify the parasite’s genetic material. The advantage here is a near-perfect sensitivity and specificity – close to 100%.
But there's a key limitation: PCR is a closed-ended question – it gives you a yes/no answer only for what you explicitly asked.
Unlike microscopy, it won’t show you something unexpected or suggest alternative diagnoses.
________________________________________
Indirect detection methods include serological tests for detecting antibodies against the parasite in both blood and CSF.
One worth pausing on is the rapid serological screening test known as:
Card Agglutination Test for Trypanosomiasis (CATT)
In this test, a paper card is used with parasites (or parasite antigens) fixed in ten small circles. You place a drop of the suspect’s blood into each circle. If that person has antibodies against the parasite, they’ll bind to the antigens, and visible clumping (agglutination) occurs – an effect you can see with the naked eye.
This test is:
• Cheap
• Rapid
• And enables screening of large populations quickly.
However, its drawback is a somewhat limited sensitivity in the field, meaning infected individuals might be missed due to false negatives.
