🇸🇴🇸🇩| The UAE’s Proxy Army: Building Somalia’s RSF Under Israeli Supervision

October 14, 2026 | Mogadishu

The United Arab Emirates has transferred troops from Somaliland and Puntland to its own territory for advanced military training conducted by Israeli officers. The troops are being trained in drone warfare and counter-drone defense systems, the exact capabilities that turned Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces into a genocidal machine.

This is not a training program. It is the construction of a proxy army.

The RSF Parallel

Somalia’s Federal Government has accused the UAE of establishing and supporting armed forces that could be used in a manner similar to the Rapid Support Forces in Sudan. The accusation is not speculative. It is a warning based on a pattern that has already destroyed one African nation.

The RSF began as a paramilitary force built, armed, and financed by the UAE. It was deployed in Darfur, then in Yemen, then against Sudan’s own army. It committed genocide. It displaced millions. It turned Sudan into a graveyard. The UAE has denied arming the RSF. The UN has documented the supply lines. The UAE’s fingerprints are on the weapons.

Now the same model is being replicated in Somalia. Troops are being pulled from Somaliland and Puntland—the two regions where the UAE has established military bases, ports, and intelligence infrastructure and trained by Israeli officers on Emirati soil. The objective is not to strengthen Somalia’s national army. It is to build a force that answers to Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv, not to Mogadishu.

The Architecture of Control

The training is not an isolated initiative. It is the final component of a military architecture that the UAE has spent years assembling across the Horn of Africa.

Berbera Airport in Somaliland has been transformed into a military base with underground bunkers, aircraft hangars, troop shelters, and command-and-control facilities. Satellite imagery from October 2025 to March 2026 shows at least 18 deep holes dug into the sandy soil, with containers placed inside before being covered with earth concealed storage for ammunition, weapons, or fuel. The project is being carried out under a 2017 defense agreement with Somaliland, but Le Monde reported that it is ultimately intended to serve U.S. and Israeli interests.

At Bosaso Airport in Puntland, the UAE deployed an Israeli-made EL/M-2084 radar in March 2025 the same multi-mission radar used in Israel’s Iron Dome system. Israeli military delegations have visited Hargeisa and Berbera. Somaliland intelligence officers have secretly traveled to Tel Aviv for training. Israel has acknowledged working discreetly with Somaliland for years.

The UAE and Israel operate an intelligence-sharing platform known as Crystal Ball, designed to “design, deploy and enable regional intelligence enhancement”. The bases at Bosaso and Berbera are nodes in this network, monitoring the Gulf of Aden, the Red Sea, and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.

The Puppet’s Role

The UAE is not an independent actor. It is a subcontractor. It provides the money, the bases, and the diplomatic cover. Israel provides the technology, the training, and the strategic direction. The United States provides the political protection.

The RSF was not the UAE’s creation alone. It was built with Israeli intelligence support, Emirati financing, and American tolerance. The same coalition is now building a force in Somalia. The troops being trained in the UAE today will be the RSF of the Horn of Africa tomorrow, a paramilitary force loyal to Abu Dhabi, equipped by Tel Aviv, and deployed against any Somali government that refuses to accept foreign tutelage.

The Somali Government’s Response

Somalia’s Federal Government has already severed all agreements with the UAE, annulling deals spanning port operations, security cooperation, and defense. The Council of Ministers cited “reliable reports and evidence indicating practices linked to the United Arab Emirates that undermine the sovereignty of the Somali Republic, its national unity and political independence”.

Defense Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi confirmed before the Upper House that aircraft had flown from Bosaso to Sudan the first official acknowledgment that Puntland’s airport was being used as a transit point for weapons shipments to the RSF.

Mogadishu has banned UAE military flights. The UAE has been removing its military equipment from Bosaso. But the damage is already done. The troops are already in the UAE. The training is already underway. The proxy army is already being built.

The Silence of the International Community

The United Nations has documented the UAE’s role in supplying the RSF. The UN mission found grounds to believe that a network involving individuals and entities in the UAE, Chad, Libya, and Somalia supplied the RSF with weapons and equipment. A U.S. senator has expressed concern over a UAE-linked training hub in Ethiopia for what he called “genocidal RSF thugs”.

And yet the training continues. The bases expand. The proxy army grows.

The international community does not intervene because the UAE is an ally of the United States. Israel is an ally of the United States. The RSF’s genocide in Sudan was tolerated because the UAE was on the right side of Washington’s regional alignments. The same calculation applies to Somalia. The destruction of a nation is acceptable if it serves the interests of the empire.

The Choice for Somalia

Somalia is being offered the same choice that Sudan was offered: submit to the UAE-Israeli axis, or face the consequences.

Submit, and the UAE will build your ports, train your troops, and fill your government with men who answer to Abu Dhabi. Refuse, and the proxy army being trained today will be deployed tomorrow not to defend Somalia, but to dismantle it.

The Somali people have already rejected this choice. The government in Mogadishu has severed the agreements. The Defense Minister has named the crime. The people understand what is being built in their country.

But the UAE does not need Mogadishu’s permission. It has Berbera. It has Bosaso. It has the bases, the radar, the intelligence network, and the Israeli officers. It has the proxy force in training. It has everything it needs to turn Somalia into the next Sudan.

Long live Somalia. Long live the resistance against foreign domination. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

text:
Everything that happened in the markets yesterday, Oct 13.

Bank earnings kicked off. Apple expanded into the smart home. NVIDIA pushed deeper into Europe. Oracle’s AI ambitions ran into an energy bottleneck. Netflix secured another major sports deal.

And underneath all of it, investors are wrestling with the same question:

How much growth is already priced in?

Here’s the full breakdown:

1. THE INDEXES BARELY MOVED. INDIVIDUAL STOCKS HAD A VERY DIFFERENT DAY.

The S&P 500 closed at 7,805.45, down 0.02%.

The Nasdaq finished at 27,204.38, down 0.15%.

The Dow dropped 180.45 points to 51,670.10, down 0.35%.

Those numbers make the session look uneventful.

But bank earnings, semiconductor competition, product announcements, and regulatory news gave investors plenty to digest.

A flat index can hide substantial changes in what investors are willing to own.

That was the more interesting story yesterday.

2. GOLDMAN SACHS DELIVERED A HUGE QUARTER.

$GS reported $18.68 BILLION in revenue and $17.01 in earnings per share.

Net earnings reached $5.29 billion, and annualized return on equity came in at 18.7%.

It was Goldman’s second-highest quarterly revenue performance ever.

The investment takeaway: a complicated market can still produce a very profitable operating environment for a firm helping clients trade, finance transactions, and manage risk.

But strong business performance and an attractive stock price are separate questions.

Investors still have to decide how much of that strength was anticipated, and whether the next few quarters can sustain it.

3. THE BANK REPORTS SHOWED A CONSUMER WHO IS STILL SPENDING.

$JPM, $C, $WFC, and $GS all reported higher profits than a year earlier, although results versus expectations were mixed.

JPMorgan delivered a rare earnings miss. Wells Fargo’s earnings beat came alongside a revenue shortfall.

The broader message from the banks was that consumers continue to spend and service their debts, while businesses keep investing.

That matters because bank results offer a direct window into the economy through payments, deposits, lending, and credit losses.

The question heading into 2027 is how long that resilience can hold if borrowing costs remain elevated.

A household can absorb higher costs for a while. Sustaining that spending requires income, employment, and access to credit to keep supporting it.

4. TECH POSITIONING IS GETTING CROWDED.

Bank of America’s October fund manager survey showed investors’ technology overweight reaching its highest level since August 2020.

That tells you the AI trade has substantial institutional participation.

It also creates a higher bar for good news.

When investors already have large positions, another positive announcement may have less buying power behind it than people expect.

A disappointing announcement can have the opposite effect: plenty of holders suddenly reassessing the same position.

Crowding alone does not tell you when a rally ends. It tells you why the reaction to an earnings miss can become unusually sharp.

5. THE “6% TREASURY YIELD” DISCUSSION NEEDS CONTEXT.

A reported finding from BofA’s survey was that 37% of respondents would rotate from stocks into bonds if the 10-year Treasury yield reached 6%.

That is a positioning survey, not a guaranteed market trigger.

But it captures a real valuation problem.

As Treasury yields rise, equities have to compete with a higher return available from government debt.

That competition becomes especially relevant for stocks whose valuations depend on profits expected many years into the future.

The key issue is how quickly yields move, why they move, and whether corporate earnings can keep improving alongside them.

6. PAUL TUDOR JONES IS WARNING ABOUT 2027.

Jones compared the current environment with 1999 and argued that next year could be difficult for equities.

His concern includes the split between companies benefiting from AI and those being left behind, along with the prospect of more equity issuance to finance the boom.

That supply argument deserves attention.

Investors often focus on demand for stocks. IPOs, secondary offerings, and insider unlocks increase the amount of stock that demand has to absorb.

Still, a veteran investor’s warning is a forecast.

The useful question is whether earnings growth, financing conditions, and investor demand support today’s prices, and what happens if one of those weakens.

7. APPLE MADE A BIGGER MOVE INTO THE HOME.

$AAPL introduced HomeView, a new smart home device with a 7-inch display, personalized content, FaceTime, home controls, and Siri AI.

Apple also refreshed its HomePod mini and Apple TV lineup.

The strategic opportunity is straightforward: give customers another reason to interact with Apple throughout the day.

A shared home device could extend the ecosystem into routines involving entertainment, communication, and household management.

The investment test will come after the launch.

Do people use it regularly? Does it make existing Apple products more useful? Does it create meaningful demand beyond early enthusiasts?

Those answers will matter more than launch-day excitement.

8. ORACLE’S AI BUILDOUT HAS A PHYSICAL BOTTLENECK.

$ORCL urged regulators to expedite approval of the Green Chile natural gas pipeline supporting Project Jupiter in New Mexico.

The pipeline is intended to supply roughly 400 million cubic feet of gas per day to the project’s power infrastructure. Its operating timeline has reportedly slipped into February 2027.

This is one of the clearest reminders of what AI infrastructure actually requires.

Compute capacity depends on electricity, fuel, equipment, construction, and permits.

A company can secure customers and order hardware while still facing delays in delivering usable capacity.

For investors, the questions are becoming more concrete: when can a site operate, what will it cost, and when can spending start producing revenue?

9. NVIDIA IS EXPANDING ITS EUROPEAN AI FOOTPRINT.

Jensen Huang said $NVDA planned to announce another $2 billion in European investments over the following week.

The company also announced investments in French AI businesses, including Doctolib, Genesis AI, Pigment, and Entalpic.

The strategic logic extends beyond selling chips.

Supporting developers and businesses can help expand the number of applications using NVIDIA’s technology.

That could strengthen future demand across healthcare, enterprise software, and industrial uses.

The investment question is how effectively those relationships translate into durable adoption and profitable demand.

10. SEMICONDUCTOR COMPETITION REMAINS A LIVE RISK.

Memory-chip competition was another important part of the session, with reports about Chinese producer CXMT’s progress drawing attention.

For $MU and the wider semiconductor industry, growing demand is only one part of the equation.

Investors also need to assess manufacturing progress, competing supply, pricing, and the durability of technical advantages.

An industry can grow rapidly while individual companies face pressure on margins or market share.

That is why “AI demand is strong” cannot answer every question about every semiconductor stock.

11. OPENAI’S SECURITY INCIDENT PUT AI INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY IN FOCUS.

OpenAI said it discovered an unauthorized recording device in an office, terminated the employee involved, and referred the matter to the FBI.

The company said it had found no evidence of improper access to or exfiltration of model weights, source code, or customer data.

The broader business implication is that protecting valuable AI technology includes physical security and internal controls.

As these companies expand their workforces, partnerships, and infrastructure, operational discipline becomes part of protecting their competitive position.

12. BANK OF AMERICA FACED A MAJOR ENFORCEMENT ACTION.

FinCEN assessed a $1.2 billion penalty against $BAC over anti-money-laundering failures.

The announcement also described an $11.6 million OFAC settlement and a concurrent $750 million OCC penalty.

Those amounts should not simply be added together without checking how the resolutions interact.

For investors, the immediate questions concern the financial treatment, required remediation, and future compliance costs.

A bank’s earnings power also depends on how effectively it controls operational and regulatory risk.

13. NETFLIX CONTINUED ITS EXPANSION INTO LIVE SPORTS.

$NFLX secured rights to stream all 104 matches of the 2030 FIFA Men’s World Cup in Spain and Andorra.

The agreement also provides for selected free-to-air coverage in Spain.

This gives Netflix a major event in a host country and another opportunity to build appointment viewing.

For the business, live sports could support engagement, advertising, and subscriber acquisition.

But the economics matter.

Investors will eventually need to weigh the cost of the rights against the revenue and retention they generate.

A prestigious event becomes a valuable investment when the numbers work.

14. ADP ADDED ANOTHER LABOR-MARKET DATA POINT.

ADP’s weekly NER Pulse reported average private-sector job additions of 24,750 per week over the four weeks ending September 26.

This is a preliminary four-week average. It should be interpreted alongside other employment data.

For markets, the balance remains delicate.

Hiring needs to support household spending, while wage and price pressures need to ease enough to improve the inflation outlook.

One reading cannot settle that debate. The direction across several reports will carry more weight.

15. THE BIGGER QUESTION IS WHETHER GROWTH CAN BROADEN.

AI continues to dominate market attention, but the health of the wider market matters too.

Investors should watch whether earnings improve across more industries, whether more stocks participate in advances, and whether businesses outside the AI boom can maintain margins.

Broader participation would give the market more sources of support.

Persistent concentration would leave index performance more dependent on a smaller group delivering exceptional results.

There is plenty happening beneath a nearly flat index.

text:
October 24, 2008. Dr. Sean George is on the way home from his medical clinic in West Australia when the unthinkable happens.

He starts to experience chest pains and other signs of a heart attack even though he's only 39-years-old.

Though he doubts its a heart attack, despite all warnings to the contrary, he surrenders the wheel to the intern riding with him, and they head for another clinic run by his friend Dr. Rao. Rao's team takes an electrocardiogram and confirms it is indeed a heart attack.

Not even a second later, George goes into cardiac arrest. Seizing and writhing on the medical bed.

The team jumps into action pumping and shocking his chest. They administer 4,000 chest compression and shock him 13 times within a 55-minute period and are unable to get George back.

By this time, George's wife, Sherry Jacob, arrives with staff from nearby Kalgoorlie Hospital, where she herself works as a medical professional. Everyone knows the situation is beyond hopeless. Brain cells start to die after 3-minutes without oxygen and the organ is completely dead after 20.

George is gone.

Rao and the others persuade Sherry that needs to go in and say goodbye because there's nothing more that can be done. Instead, Sherry takes her husband's hand and say a prayer to God, begging him to give her and their 10-year-old boy more time with George.

George's heart instantly restarts. Stunning Sherry and the clinic staff.

They get him on a life flight to the hospital asap. The flight gets delayed due to a horrendous hailstorm, but they put him in a medically induced coma for three days soon as he arrives, against all odds. None of them expect him to wake, but the fact that his heart restarted at all with no further medical assistance offers a sliver of hope to Sherry.

On day 3, George wakes perfectly coherent. No signs of brain death whatsoever. He even has full memory of the events leading up to his cardiac arrest and is able to review his own medical charts without assistance. 2 weeks, he's discharged. 3 months, he's back to working full time.

Craig Keener recounts George's story in his book Miracles Today. But such documentation is unnecessary.

Dr. Sean George has retold his own story time and again and released his medical records to the public at his website.

Below is a video of his testimonial shared on YouTube from his own mouth.

Diogo Dalot has been disappointing lately, and his performance against Atlético Madrid was another reminder that he needs to step up.

Honestly, he looks mentally distracted on the pitch. The sharpness, concentration and confidence we expect from him have been missing.

Against Atlético, he was caught sleeping for the opening goal when Baena exploited the space behind him with a simple ball over the top. 

That is basic defensive awareness, and at this level, you cannot afford to switch off in the opening minute.

He also lost track of Julián Álvarez when the striker found space and struck the post. 

Then, on the second goal, Lookman got behind him to finish the rebound after Lammens saved David’s initial effort.

Three situations. Three reminders of the same problem: Dalot must be more alert, track runners properly and defend his zone with greater urgency.

He was also far too limited going forward. His delivery and final-third contribution offered little, and he failed to provide the attacking quality needed to punish Atlético.

Where is the Dalot who plays with confidence, makes intelligent overlapping runs, presses aggressively and contributes in both boxes?

I don’t care about reputations or past performances. 

You play for Manchester United, and you must deliver consistently.

Dalot needs to wake up, regain his concentration and fight for his place. 

We cannot keep accepting performances like this.

text:
Good morning, friends. As the first light of October 14, 2026, gently wakes the world at this early hour, I invite you to pause with me and receive a simple, powerful word for the day ahead. Our verse in the Fear Not series comes from Genesis 43:23: "Be at ease... you have no need to fear."

These words were spoken to men carrying heavy burdens. Joseph's brothers had traveled far, their hearts filled with worry about the past mistakes they had made and the uncertain future that lay before them. In that tense moment, a reassuring voice cut through their anxiety and invited them to relax, to trust that provision and peace were already in motion.

We wake up to our own versions of that tension every day. Perhaps you are carrying concerns about rising costs, job stability, or the health of someone you love. Maybe the steady stream of headlines about global events leaves you wondering how things will unfold for your family or community. These real pressures can make fear feel like an unwelcome companion as we start our routines.

Yet the ancient invitation still rings true: be at ease. The same God who turned a story of betrayal and famine into one of reunion and abundance is present in your circumstances right now. He sees the bills, the difficult conversations, the quiet doubts, and the larger uncertainties that occupy our thoughts. Nothing surprises Him, and nothing is beyond His care.

This morning, take a slow breath and let the promise settle. You do not have to face the day braced for the worst. Small acts of trust—offering a kind word, pausing for gratitude, or simply choosing to move forward—can loosen fear's hold. As communities continue to navigate challenges together, we can be sources of calm for one another, reflecting the peace this verse offers.

Whatever lies ahead today, remember you are held. Walk gently, stay hopeful, and know that ease is possible even amid the unknown.

text:
Dhammapada - Yamakavagga.
The Story of Matthakundali

In the ancient city of Savatthi, there lived a Brahmin named Adinnapubbaka. His name literally meant "He who never gave anything to anyone." He was immensely wealthy, yet his stinginess was the stuff of legends. He never bought gifts, never gave alms, and never spent a single coin unless absolutely forced to. 

When his only son was born, Adinnapubbaka wanted to give him a golden ornament. However, he refused to hire a goldsmith, fearing the artisan would overcharge him or steal a few grains of gold. Instead, the Brahmin took a piece of raw gold and beat it into a crude, circular shape himself. Because of the rough, ring-like ornament the boy wore around his neck, he became known to everyone as Matthakundali (He of the Burnished Ear-Rings).

When Matthakundali turned sixteen, he suddenly struck down with a severe attack of jaundice. Seeing the boy growing weaker by the day, his mother grew frantic. “Brahmin,” she pleaded, “our son is dying. We must send for a physician!”

Adinnapubbaka scowled. “Wife, if I send for a professional physician, I will have to pay him a fee in rice and coins. You care nothing about the loss of my substance! I shall manage this without wasting our wealth.”

The Brahmin hurried to the village square, approaching various doctors under the guise of casual conversation. He would ask, “Tell me, friend, what do you usually prescribe for a generic ailment like jaundice?” The physicians, assuming he was asking out of intellectual curiosity, mentioned the bark of certain trees and various wild herbs. Adinnapubbaka memorized their answers, went into the woods to gather the ingredients himself, and forced his dying son to drink the amateur concoctions. Predictably, the boy’s condition grew exponentially worse.

Realizing the boy was on the brink of death, the Brahmin grew anxious—not for his son's life, but for his own reputation. He thought, “If people come to visit my dying son inside the house, they will see the vast treasures and wealth I keep hidden here.” Without a shred of mercy, Adinnapubbaka carried his agonizingly weak son out of the house and laid him down on the hard floor of the outside veranda, leaving him there to die exposed to the elements.

On that very morning, the Buddha arose early and surveyed the world with his eye of infinite compassion. He saw the pure heart of young Matthakundali shining through his physical suffering. The Buddha perceived that if he visited the boy, Matthakundali would generate a moment of profound faith, die with a pure mind, and be reborn in the heavenly realms. Furthermore, this miracle would shatter the stone-cold stinginess of the father and lead thousands to spiritual awakening.

The Buddha, accompanied by his attendant Venerable Ananda, walked into the city of Savatthi on his daily alms round. He approached the Brahmin’s house and stood at the edge of the veranda. Because Matthakundali was facing the inner wall, the Buddha projected a magnificent ray of golden light that illuminated the wall in front of the dying boy. 

Startled by the celestial glow, Matthakundali painfully turned his head. There, standing in majestic serenity, was the Buddha. Matthakundali was too weak to move. He could not raise his hands in a traditional gesture of respect, nor could he offer standard words of praise. He looked into the compassionate eyes of the Buddha and thought, “My own father, out of greed, has denied me medicine and cast me out to die. But the Great Teacher, the Supreme Buddha, has come to my veranda just to see me.” With his last remaining strength, Matthakundali projected a wave of absolute, pure devotion and faith toward the Buddha. The Buddha, knowing the seed of faith had been firmly planted, turned and walked away. A moment later, Matthakundali closed his eyes and peacefully passed away.

Because he died with a mind entirely purified by faith, the transition was instantaneous. As if awakening from a deep sleep, Matthakundali woke up in the Tavatimsa (the Realm of the Thirty-Three Gods). He found himself reborn as a Devaputta (a celestial being) living in a magnificent golden mansion spanning thirty leagues, surrounded by a retinue of a thousand heavenly maidens (Apsaras). 

Meanwhile, back on Earth, Adinnapubbaka discovered his son’s lifeless body. The reality of his loss finally broke through his greed. He cremated the boy, but the grief consumed him. Every single day, the old Brahmin would go to the cemetery, throw himself onto the earth near the funeral pyre, and weep uncontrollably, crying, “Where are you, my only son? Where have you gone?”

Up in the heavenly realm, the reborn Matthakundali looked down and saw his father weeping at the burning ground. He remembered how his father had cruelly denied him medicine to save a few coins. Yet, looking at the old man's absolute misery, compassion filled the deity's heart. He thought, “My father is destroying himself with blind grief. I must go down and change his attitude.”

Matthakundali disguised his heavenly form, taking the exact human appearance of his former self. He descended to Earth and sat down on the ground just a short distance from where his father was weeping. The youth covered his face with his hands and began to cry out in deep, exaggerated agony.

Adinnapubbaka stopped his own weeping and looked over. He was stunned to see a young man who looked exactly like his late son. He approached the youth and asked, “Young man, I weep because I have lost my only son. But why do you wring your hands and cry so bitterly?”

The disguised youth looked up and said, “Old man, I have built a beautiful, magnificent chariot made of solid gold. But I am weeping because I cannot find a suitable pair of wheels for it. Without wheels, my chariot is useless!”

The wealthy Brahmin, desperate to find a substitute for his lost son and wanting to do a good deed, replied eagerly, “Do not cry, sweet youth! Tell me what kind of wheels you need. If they are made of silver, gold, brass, or iron, tell me! I am a very wealthy man. I will buy or manufacture the perfect set of wheels for your chariot!”

The youth looked the Brahmin straight in the eye and said, “Sir, standard wheels will not do. The sun and the moon are perfectly round and beautiful. I want the sun and the moon to be the wheels for my golden chariot!”

Adinnapubbaka stared at him in utter disbelief. He shook his head and said, “Young man, you are a fool! You are crying for something that is impossible to possess. The sun and the moon are millions of miles away in the heavens. No mortal can ever catch them to make chariot wheels. You are going to die of grief for an impossible dream!”

The youth suddenly stood up, his face breaking into a calm, knowing smile. He looked at the Brahmin and said, “Old man, you call me a fool? The sun and the moon are real. We can see them rise, we can see them set, and their paths are visible to all. I am crying for something that actually exists. But you... you stand over a pile of cold ash, weeping for a son who is dead and completely gone from this world. Between the two of us, who is the bigger fool?”

The words struck the Brahmin like a lightning bolt. The fog of his blind grief instantly evaporated, replaced by a profound realization of the impermanence of life. He wiped his tears and looked at the boy with deep respect. “Who are you?” the Brahmin asked softly. “Are you a human, a spirit, or a god?”

The youth shifted, revealing a glimpse of his celestial radiance. “I am your son, Matthakundali. Because I reposed a single moment of absolute faith in the Buddha on my deathbed, I was reborn in the Realm of the Thirty-Three Gods, inheriting a golden mansion and unimaginable splendor.”

Adinnapubbaka was stunned. “A single moment of faith in the Teacher brought you such glory?” 

“Yes, Father,” the deity replied. “Abandon your grief, give up your stinginess, take refuge in the Triple Gem, and practice generosity.” With those parting words, the Devaputta vanished, returning to the heavens.

Transformed by the encounter, Adinnapubbaka hurried back to the city. He approached the Buddha and invited the Master and the entire community of monks to his home for a grand, lavish feast—an act that shocked the entire city of Savatthi. 

During the feast, a lingering doubt troubled the Brahmin’s mind. He approached the Buddha and asked, “Venerable Blessed One, is it truly possible for a person to be reborn in the heavenly realms simply by offering a mental tribute of faith, without giving alms, keeping the precepts, or listening to the Dhamma?”

The Buddha smiled and replied, “Brahmin, why do you ask me? Did your own son Matthakundali not come down from the heavens just this morning to tell you it is true?” The Buddha then used his psychic powers to make Matthakundali’s golden mansion and celestial form visible to the entire assembly. 

Turning to the gathered crowd, the Buddha delivered the absolute truth of the mind: “Monks and laypeople, the mind is the architect of everything. If a person speaks or acts with a pure, faithful mind, happiness and heavenly rebirth follow them as naturally and inevitably as a shadow that never leaves its source.”

It was on this occasion that the Buddha uttered the famous second verse of the Dhammapada:

"Mind precedes all mental states.
Mind is their chief; they are mind-made.
If one speaks or acts with a pure mind,
Happiness follows him,
Like a shadow that never leaves."

At the end of the discourse Matthakundali and his father Adinnapubbaka attained Sotapatti Magga and Sotapatti Phala. Adinnapubbaka also donated almost all his wealth to the cause of the Buddha's Teaching.

Nottingham Forest’s Defence 🔴

Keep the Space Between the Lines Compact 🔴

vs Coventry

Half-Space + Line Break 🔵

vs 1-5-2-3 / 1-5-4-1 — Escaping the High Press 🔵

- Escape the HIGH PRESS using the HALF-SPACE + LINE BREAK.
- Draw them out, then attack behind them.

① Place the #8 / #10 / False Winger in the Middle-Zone Half-Space

- Second-line #8 / #10 drops toward the ball to demand the pass from a deeper position.
- Draw the ball-side CB (RCB / LCB) out.
- Combine with short passes, but even if the player is not used, his movement gives the back-line passer the option of supplying a long ball to the winger.
- The double pivot reacts to the second-line movement but stays deeper, drawing out the opposition double pivot.
- Maintain a 3-4-player central numerical superiority through the BOX MIDFIELD.
- Use a front five to create numerical equality against the back five.
- Prefer inverted-foot players who are comfortable as FALSE 9 / 10 / WINGER.
- This makes it easier to receive toward the inside, providing more options than taking the first touch toward the outside.
- Left MF: Bruno G. / Rice; including FALSE WINGERS, Eze / Tzolis.
- Right MF: Ødegaard / Merino.

② Winger or #9 Makes the Line Break to Attack the WB / CB 1v1

- In ①, the ball-side CB has already been drawn out, making it difficult for him to support the WB.
- Arsenal no longer have Martinelli, a winger who specialised in repeated LINE BREAKS, so rather than simply asking both wingers to constantly run behind, an asymmetrical structure is the priority and the ideal.
- On the right, Saka or Madueke becomes the SPACE LINE BREAKER.
- On the left, Tzolis or Eze holds the width and looks to receive to feet more often than on the right.
  (LINE BREAK when the timing is right.)
- On the left, the priority is for the #9 — Gyökeres or Havertz — to drift across and make the LINE BREAK.

④ Resulting Shape: 1-4-2-2-2 / 1-3-1-4-2

- 1GK.
- Three to four players in the back line (including DLP).
- At pivot level: inverting SB / FALSE 10 included.

- Up front:
  - left side = #9 / 10 (Gyökeres / Havertz)
  - right side = winger (Saka / Madueke).
- Against a 1-5-4-1 / 1-5-2-3, 1-3-1-5-1 becomes the main option.
- Against a back-four base, alternate between 1-4-2-4 / 1-3-2-4-1.

Cross-Field Pass / Switch Pass / Long Ball / KO Ball 🔵

  - move the ball from side to side with short passes
  - keep the distances between players compact
  - shorten passing distances to reduce turnovers / mistakes in deep areas.
- Including the GK, use shapes such as 1-4-2-4 or 1-3-2-5 to create numerical superiority against Forest’s 3-2 pentagonal HIGH PRESS across the last line + third line.

  - one more direct medium-to-long pass toward an SB / winger / #9 on the flank
  - target a higher area
  - avoid the opposition CB
  - contest against the WB instead, increasing the probability of winning the aerial duel / 2ND-ball duel.

False Winger + Countermovement 🔵

- Draw out the opponent’s WB or ball-side CB.

- Ideally, use an asymmetrical structure.

- Against a 1-5-2-3 HIGH PRESS, when the GK creates the +1, the SB can become free.

Pocket 🔵

- Ideally, shots should go to the bottom-right from the taker’s perspective.
- Position two to three players in the POCKET between the CB-MF lines, creating a +1 against Nottingham Forest’s double pivot.

Pocket vs 1-5-4-1 🔵

- One of the limited spaces available to the attacking team is the POCKET between the CB and MF lines.

1) To maintain numerical superiority wide, the pivot or CB sometimes has to move across to support the flank.
This can temporarily leave the defensive structure resembling a SINGLE-PIVOT shape.

2) The double pivot has a large area to cover around the POCKET, making stamina management difficult.
During the HIGH PRESS, they SHADOW PRESS together with the front three. As DLPs or through PRESS-BACK actions, they also drop into the last line, creating a lot of vertical running.

3) The 3CB in the last line prioritise protecting the central penalty area and therefore tend to RETREAT.

Line Break 🔵

- Gyökeres or the SB repeatedly makes LINE BREAKS and looks to score behind the last line.
- LINE CONTROL is more difficult with a back five than with a back four.
- LINE BREAKS should target the HALF-SPACE.
- These actions are more likely to create a big chance / DOGSO and can also draw out the CB or pivot.
- LINE BREAKS pin the last line deep, creating more space and time between the CB-MF lines.

False 9 / 10 + Countermovement 🔵

- Depends on Havertz’s injury status.
- At the moment, if Havertz starts against Bayern, Gyökeres is the leading candidate to start here.
- Ødegaard or Merino operates as FALSE 10 and draws the opposition marker, creating a local +1.
- When the FALSE 9 / 10 vacates the #9 / #10 space, an SB / winger / MF inverts into it to preserve the structure.
- Pinning the marker makes it more difficult to defend the FALSE 9 / 10 with M2M.
- Keeping player distances compact makes COUNTER-PRESSING easier.

Maintain Four Lines 🔵

- Preserve fluidity + ideally leave two passing options high on the top line.
- A response to M2M HIGH PRESS.
- It becomes more difficult for the opponent to maintain compactness from the last line all the way to the forwards.
- Conversely, if Arsenal cannot maintain four lines, the opponent can defend M2M while remaining compact from the last line to the front.
- That allows high or middle-third regains, making it harder for Arsenal to progress into the attacking third.
Key: False 9 / 10 / Winger
- Ideally, two players drop to offer passing lanes while two players remain on the top line.
- 1-4-2-2-2
- Ideally leave two LINE-BREAKER profiles high.

Pattern 1

Havertz + Ødegaard both drop as FALSE 9 / 10 → Saka / Madueke remain high
- Havertz–Ødegaard on the second line.
- Madueke–Saka on the first line.
- Madueke is particularly suited to this role.

Pattern 2

Only one of the FALSE 9 / 10 drops + one winger inverts
- In the recent Leeds match, Havertz and Ødegaard maintained a vertical relationship and preserved a passing option on the top line.
- Eze / Tzolis are particularly suited to the FALSE WINGER role.
- Eze / Tzolis – Ødegaard on the second line.
- Havertz – Saka / Madueke on the top line.

Pattern 3

9 / 10 stay high + both wide players become FALSE WINGERS
- Eze / Tzolis – Saka on the second line.
- Havertz – Ødegaard on the top line.
- Pin the opposition SB / WB centrally.
- This makes it easier for the top-line players to attack the CB 1v1.
Other Adjustments
- Merino: FALSE 9 / 10.
- Rice: CARRY / #8 > #10.
- Dowman: FALSE WINGER / #10.
- Gyökeres: LINE BREAKER / FALSE 9.
- Adjust depending on player profile.

text:
A woman he used to belong to sent him a bill.
In February 1860, Sarah Logue wrote to Syracuse from Tennessee, demanding $1,000 for the man she still called her property. She had already sold his brother and sister to cover a debt of her own. Now she wanted him to cover hers.

The bill reached a brick house on East Genesee Street in Syracuse addressed to a name Jermain Wesley Loguen had not answered to in over two decades. Sarah Logue signed it "Jarm."

What she did not seem to know, or perhaps chose not to know, was exactly who Jarm had become in the twenty-six years since he last answered to that name.

He had been born enslaved near Nashville, Tennessee, on February 5, 1813, the son of an enslaved woman named Cherry and the white planter who owned her, David Logue. His own father held the deed to him.

In 1834, in his early twenties, he ran. He took a mare from the farm named Old Rock and rode until Tennessee turned into Kentucky and Kentucky turned into a country where the law could not reach him.

He crossed into Canada with nothing else, and no education. He could not read a word of the alphabet and could not write his own name.

That was the condition he arrived in at St. Catharines, Ontario, a runaway with a stolen horse and no letters at all, determined to get some.

From there he made his way into New York State, added an "n" to the surname he was born under to mark it as his own, and took "Wesley" as a middle name after the founder of the faith he had adopted. By 1837 he was studying at the Oneida Institute, a school in central New York run by the abolitionist Beriah Green and among the few in the country that would teach a Black man at all.

He settled in Syracuse in 1841 as a schoolteacher and a licensed preacher in the African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church. Within a decade, his house had become the busiest stop on the Underground Railroad in the state, and quite possibly the country.

He married Caroline Storum in 1840.

She had been born free near Jamestown, New York, into an educated, biracial abolitionist family, and she ran the depot as fully as he did.

He and his wife fitted the cellar of their house at 293 East Genesee Street with bunks and printed their own home address in the local paper, daring the law to come find it. Historians estimate that some 1,500 people passed through that basement on their way to Canada.

Loguen ran it almost as a public ledger. He printed notices in the Syracuse papers announcing which fugitives had passed through, and how many, daring the marshals to read the count for themselves.

People started calling him and Caroline the King and Queen of the Underground Railroad.

He paid for that house the same way he paid for everything else, by working for it twice over. Alongside his pulpit and his classroom, he bought and sold real estate in a city that was growing fast, one parcel at a time.

When Congress passed a tougher fugitive slave law in 1850, Loguen stood up at a rally in his own city and said what most men in his position kept to themselves. "It outlaws me, and I outlaw it," he told the crowd, and he meant every marshal sent to enforce it too.

He got the chance to prove it thirteen months later. On October 1, 1851, federal marshals arrested a cooper named William Henry, known around Syracuse as Jerry, and took him toward a hearing that would have ended in his return to slavery.

Church bells rang out a signal across the city. A crowd that grew to two or three thousand people gathered outside the building where Jerry was held, and by nightfall they had broken through the door, freed him from his irons, and started him toward Canada. Loguen had helped plan it from the beginning.

Nineteen indictments came out of that night. Loguen's name was on the list, and he fled north himself for the winter, wanted now by Tennessee and by the federal government both.

Of the nineteen, only one man, Enoch Reed, was ever convicted, and he died before his appeal could be heard. No one else spent a single day in prison for freeing Jerry.

By spring he was back in Syracuse, picking up exactly where he had left off.

He kept going after that. Loguen allied himself with the wealthy abolitionist Gerrit Smith and his Radical Abolition Party, and in the years that followed he helped recruit men for John Brown's raid on the federal armory at Harpers Ferry, work that could have hanged him just as surely as any fugitive slave warrant ever would.

In 1859 he put the whole story into print for the first time, an autobiography called The Rev. J. W. Loguen, as a Slave and as a Freeman. Several historians who have studied the letters believe Sarah Logue read it, or heard about it, and that is what put a runaway she had not thought about in years back on her mind.

That is the man the bill from Tennessee found in February 1860.

The census taker who came through Syracuse that same year recorded something Sarah Logue almost certainly never saw. Jermain Loguen's household was listed at $4,500 in real estate and $1,500 in personal property, enough to purchase his own freedom several times over, if he had ever wanted to buy it.

Sarah Logue, the woman demanding $1,000 from him, claimed no property in her own name at all.

The man she still called her miserable chattel now owned more than she did.

He sat down on March 28, 1860, and answered her letter line by line. He opened by thanking her for news of his mother, Cherry, still alive and still enslaved on the same land that had once held him.

"You are a woman," he wrote, "but, had you a woman's heart, you never could have insulted a brother by telling him you sold his only remaining brother and sister, because he put himself beyond your power to convert him into money."

He was not finished. He turned her own arithmetic back on her: if he sent money at all, it would be to buy back his brother and sister, not to save her land.

"Did you raise your own children for the market?" he asked her. "Did you raise them for the whipping-post?"

He noticed she had not mentioned her husband anywhere in her letter, and he had a guess why. "I infer, therefore, that he is dead," he wrote, "that he has gone to his great account, with all his sins against my poor family upon his head."

On the matter of the stolen mare, he offered no apology. "Have you got to learn that I had a better right to the old mare, as you call her, than Mannasseth Logue had to me? Is it a greater sin for me to steal his horse, than it was for him to rob my mother's cradle, and steal me?"

The thousand dollars she wanted, something close to forty thousand in today's money, was never really about the mare. Then he told her exactly what it was worth to him.

"Did you think to terrify me by presenting the alternative to give my money to you, or give my body to slavery?" he asked. "Then let me say to you, that I meet the proposition with unutterable scorn and contempt."

He signed nothing away.

His reply reached Boston within weeks and ran in The Liberator on April 27, 1860, under the heading "Mr. Loguen's Reply." Readers across the free states copied it into scrapbooks and read it aloud at meetings. Sarah Logue's letter survives today largely because his answer carried it along.

He never sent her a dollar. He never let a friend buy his freedom either, before that letter or after, calling it a compromise he would not make with what he called his God-given gift of freedom.

In 1868, the African Methodist Episcopal Zion Church made him a bishop, and put him in charge of its conferences across the Alleghenies and Kentucky. His daughter Amelia married Lewis Henry Douglass, the oldest son of Frederick Douglass, the following year. Another daughter, Sarah, would go on to graduate from Syracuse University's medical college in 1876, one of the first Black women in the country licensed to practice medicine, a milestone her father did not live to see.

He was preparing for a mission assignment on the Pacific Coast in 1872 when tuberculosis stopped him. He went to the mineral springs at Saratoga Springs, New York, hoping for a cure, and died there on September 20, 1872.

He is buried in Oakwood Cemetery in Syracuse, not far from the house on East Genesee Street that once held 1,500 strangers overnight, still owed a brother and a sister nobody ever paid him back for. He had already written down, in 1860, the only accounting he cared to settle.

"Before God and high heaven," he asked her, "is there a law for one man which is not a law for every other man?"

text:
At a laundromat in Kentucky at ten at night, an old man in a veteran cap stood before a fitted sheet like a man facing an army alone.

He folded it once. It became a knot. He shook it out again. His hands were trembling.

In my land, you do not watch an elder struggle with his banner. And you do not offer help aloud. You simply take your post.

I stepped to the other end of the table and took the two corners.

He did not flinch. He did not ask my name.

"On three," he said.

"Three," I said.

A fitted sheet has no straight lines. I have struck down camp in a monsoon with less trouble.

We stepped in. We flipped. We folded. We did not speak a word through four sheets and eight towels.

When the stack was finished, it stood straight as a castle wall.

The old man put his rough hand on top of the cotton. He looked at the empty space beside me.

"My wife took that side for forty-two years," he said softly. "This is the first week I had to do the laundry."

He wiped his nose with his sleeve.

I stood at attention and bowed deeply to my side of the table. You do not take another warrior's post without saluting their shadow.

He bought me a cold root beer from the machine. We sat on plastic chairs and watched the dryers spin until midnight.

I go every Thursday at ten now.

I guard the left corners.

text:
Early Life
Roku was born in the Fire Nation to a high-born family. As a child and young man, he was close friends with Sozin (the future Fire Lord). They trained together and shared a birthday. Roku was a skilled firebender from a young age.
When he was 16, the monks of the Southern Air Temple identified him as the Avatar (the reincarnation of Avatar Kyoshi). He left home to master the four elements, traveling the world and learning waterbending, earthbending, and airbending in addition to his native firebending. He also learned to control the Avatar State.
Avatar Duties and Relationship with Sozin
As Avatar, Roku worked to maintain balance and peace among the Four Nations during a time of growing technology and political tension. He was known as wise, merciful, and well-intentioned, though later admitted he could be indecisive.
His long friendship with Fire Lord Sozin became both a strength and a fatal weakness. Sozin proposed expanding the Fire Nation’s power and colonies to “share” its prosperity with the world—essentially a plan for conquest. Roku rejected this and warned Sozin against aggression. When Sozin later moved forward with invasion plans, Roku confronted him, defeated him in battle, and spared his life out of old friendship, telling him any further aggression would mean death.
Death
Years later, during a volcanic eruption on Roku’s home island (triggered in part by Sozin’s actions), Roku tried to stop the disaster. Sozin arrived and initially helped, but then betrayed Roku, leaving him to die in the toxic gas and lava. Roku’s death allowed Sozin to begin the Hundred Year War unopposed. Roku’s spirit carried deep guilt over failing to stop Sozin earlier.
Legacy and Connection to Aang

text:
Hidden GOP vote could ‘easily’ keep the Senate in Republican hands | Nick Givas, The Western Journal

CNN chief data analyst Harry Enten said Monday that Republicans have a substantial chance of maintaining their Senate majority if polling numbers are off by only a few points.

Enten pointed out that the polling industry has consistently favored Democrats in past elections and said it would not take much for the Republicans to hold on to vital toss-up seats.

“Let’s just say we have the 2026 Senate polls, but if the polls are underestimating the Republicans by 3.5 points, which you know is really possible, because we’ve seen it through the history, right? You go back to 2020, that’s basically what happened,” he declared.

“Even in 2024, in a number of the key states we saw it happen, including places like Texas.”

Enten then rattled off several other high-profile contests, some in ruby-red states, and said voters could easily defy pollsters and flip the blue wave narrative on its head.

“How about Michigan? How about up there in Maine, how about in Alaska, how about in Iowa, how about in Kansas — which has been getting a lot of press lately — all of these go red. All these go red, and the Republicans don’t just hold the United States Senate; they hold it easily with 52 seats to the Democrats’ 48 seats.”

Enten’s map didn’t even include potential GOP Senate wins in Ohio, North Carolina, New Hampshire, or Georgia, where Republicans have historically been competitive, if not outright dominant.

If polls are underestimating Republicans in the states that Enten mentioned, and they stay red, the GOP would only need to pick off two swing states to increase their current 53-47 majority.

The CNN analyst also highlighted how the early October generic congressional ballot has underestimated Republicans in 14 of 16 elections since 1994.

“What is going on here?” Enten asked. “And it’s happened by an average of, I believe, what is this — four points. The average is a four-point underestimation of Republicans since 1994.”

Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York also raised concerns on Tuesday about GOP fundraising advantages, according to a letter obtained by The Hill.

Schumer wrote that control of the upper chamber could come down to an “unprecedented tsunami of Republican money” that has the potential to level the playing field in the home stretch, with only weeks to go until Election Day.

“We have strong candidates, a clear message, and a political climate that offers real opportunities. But Republicans have one enormous advantage of their own. Money,” Schumer stated.

He also said President Donald Trump has the bandwidth to spend between $400 million and $500 million through his super PAC, MAGA Inc., and that big tech mogul Elon Musk has pumped nearly $300 million into the midterm races to help Republican candidates.

Schumer added that other “megadonors” have jumped into the fray and are funding Senate races at rates unlike anything “we’ve ever seen before.”

“That’s the enormous force bearing down on this election,” Schumer concluded. “And it’s a challenge none of us can afford to underestimate.”

text:
Podcast Summary | Call Her Daddy: Heather McMahan: Dog Shows, Neck Lifts & Airport Fits

Overview
Heather McMahan treats every professional and personal disaster as material, and the through-line is control: who has it, who takes it from you, and what it costs to get it back. A Ryder Cup hosting gig collapsed into a firing she frames as a double standard. A dog show booking happened days after a neck lift, drains and all. An ovarian torsion at 30,000 feet became the most painful experience of her life and a lesson about trusting instinct. Running underneath all of it is her stated frustration that women are damned if they do and damned if they don't, a thesis she has now built into a special, a possible political run, and a refusal to accept jobs without a clear job description.

Key Themes
- Getting fired from a Ryder Cup gig for repeating a crowd chant reveals a double standard: a male comic would likely have been celebrated, not stripped of credentials.
- Women in the industry avoid asking clarifying questions for fear of seeming difficult, which is exactly how McMahan ended up as a glorified court jester with no defined role.
- The phrase damned if you do, damned if you don't is the organizing idea behind By a Thread and her broader case for why women get blamed for everything.
- Working through a neck lift recovery for a dog show reveals a professional who will choose the job over the doctor's orders, then admit she didn't tell her surgeon.
- Marriage and friendship obligations around destination weddings and bachelorette trips have outrun what friends can reasonably be asked to spend, and the honest move is to say so.
- HomeGoods functions as a feminine safe space and a treasure hunt, which reframes discount shopping as agency rather than overconsumption.
- Financial literacy and pumping the brakes are framed as the antidote to wedding-industry and lifestyle pressure, especially since saving for a house took seven years.
- Trusting your own body and instinct outranks loyalty to a schedule, whether that means skipping a flight or refusing a job without a job description.
- McMahan's satire and her sincerity share a spine: she documents the mess rather than curating it.

Detailed Summary
Heather McMahan's third special, By a Thread, lands on Hulu, and the title doubles as a thesis. Her recurring argument is that women are damned if they do and damned if they don't, judged for doing too much or not enough. It is not an abstract observation. It is the frame she puts around a run of specific, documented mishaps that would end most careers and instead became material.

Start with the Ryder Cup. McMahan was hired to host a sponsor event the night before the main event and was on site at Bethpage Black on Long Island, dressed head to toe in Ralph Lauren, including men's 10.5 loafers. Her call time was 4:45 a.m., which she initially misread as an afternoon slot. She expected red-carpet-style interviews and commentary. What she found was no defined job description at all, a role she describes as a glorified court jester.

A producer told her she could curse after a coach took the microphone and said let's go with an expletive. She then led the same chant. When the crowd chanted an obscenity aimed at Rory McIlroy, she repeated it into the microphone. Roughly ten minutes later Team Europe asked for her credentials. A Team Europe representative confronted her in person, yelling that she could not say anything about European players. She wrote an apology letter to McIlroy through Team Europe and says she does not condone any of the behavior directed at him.

Her read on the aftermath is where the thesis sharpens. The crowd had been drinking since early morning. She was sober. She says she was later blamed for the behavior of men hours after the fact. A male comedian in the same spot, she argues, would have been celebrated. Headlines framed it as McIlroy versus McMahon, implying a feud she says did not exist. Her husband Jeff had warned her not to take the job, calling New York and Long Island sports fans feral, and she now uses the Masters, which she attends annually, as the contrast case for how a golf crowd is supposed to behave. The takeaway she states outright: she avoided asking clarifying questions because she feared being seen as difficult, and she will not take another job without knowing exactly what is expected.

The dog show is the opposite story told with the same lesson about overcommitment. McMahan hosted behind-the-scenes interviews with breeders, vets, and groomers at the American Kennel Club Best in Show in Orlando in December, not the live prize segment. The opportunity came through her manager after the company reached out, citing her as a dog fan. She was about a week out of a neck lift when the gig was offered. She describes the procedure as cutting behind the ears, pulling skin up, and some liposuction. She says nothing was done to her face and that she has only had Botox, no lip filler.

She had drains and dried blood down the back of her neck and wore a cashmere turtleneck to cover it. She did not tell her doctor she was taking the job, and she took a muscle relaxer during the show, which left her feeling off the cuff while working. She calls it a wild experience and says she enjoyed studying the people and characters there. The tension is plain: a professional who says she does not party before shows chose to work with open wounds rather than lose a booking.

Her dogs are a running bit that carries real weight. Macaroni Lemon Ferrari Daniels and Riotoni Cannoli Gandalfini Daniels share a surname pattern and are French bulldogs, Macaroni a girl, Riotoni a boy. Possible future names include Ravioli, Risotto, and Rizzy. She calls herself an overbearing dog mom and argues that this demonstrates she would be a great regular mom as well. Jeff's response, per her retelling, is to call her a sociopath. The exchange captures how she converts the question of whether she wants children into a joke that lands on her own terms.

Travel is its own system, built from experience. She wears a blazer, a rag and bone pajama jean, a tank top, and no bra. She holds Delta 360 and Diamond Medallion status and million-miler tags, and her grandfather was chief pilot for Delta for a long time. She flies with a BGA bag. She does not drink on planes except possibly a champagne or a glass of red wine internationally. Her staples are ginger ale, Coke Zero, electrolytes, and Delta 360 compression socks.

The gout story runs into the travel and body-trust themes. She says she got gout for the first time despite being on a GLP1 and was told she should not drink red wine. She describes gout as traditionally a king's disease associated with rich foods, liver, heavy foods, and wine, and understands it medically as a surplus of uric acid. During her first flare-up she had been meal prepping ground turkey, steamed rice, and broccoli. Someone messaged her that too much ground turkey can build up uric acid. In the weeks prior she had been in Italy eating nitrate meats and cheese.

Then the flight that became the worst pain of her life. In 2019, on a New York to London flight, McMahan experienced an ovarian torsion. She has PCOS and a history of ovarian cysts; the torsion flipped her ovary and required hospital evaluation. She initially mistook the pain for appendicitis or a kidney stone. She took Advil, then vomited in the galley after being given oxygen. A nurse on board assessed her and suggested an ectopic pregnancy, which McMahan disagreed with. Flight staff gave her medication to sedate her and she lay in the galley covered with a blanket.

The plane did not turn around. It landed at Heathrow, where she was taken off on a gurney. A hospital near Heathrow gave her nitrous oxide in the ambulance and examined her with an ultrasound to check ovarian blood supply. She was discharged with oxycodone and returned to Heathrow for luggage and customs. She had concealed the emergency from Jeff until she reached the hospital, which made him furious.

Four days after surgery, on Thanksgiving, she diagnosed Jeff with a kidney stone and told him to drink a beer. At the hospital, staff initially focused on her because she had drains and dried blood before treating his kidney stone. She was supposed to be recovering and instead nursed him for several days. She uses the story to argue her pain was more severe, and to make the broader point that she wants her medical self-diagnoses trusted.

The Pitbull material shows what happens when an obsessive bit runs long enough to become real. McMahan has performed as a Pitbull drag impersonator for over ten years, doing special effects makeup and impressions. The persona opened her first tour via video. Pitbull invited her to his Hyde Park concert, where they broke the Guinness World Record for most people in bald caps, and Guinness included her in the count and sent her a plaque. Kesha performed before Pitbull took the stage, and McMahan was hosting a YouTube live countdown of him receiving the record.

Walking through the crowd with a camera crew, fans mobbed her thinking she was Pitbull. She had to tell people she is a woman, and they only believed it up close. She credits her hair and makeup artist for the convincing look. She met Pitbull, whose real name is Armando, at Hyde Park, got a meet and greet, and says she now has his number. He texted her in an exaggerated, all-caps, many-exclamation-point style. Her stated dream is to collaborate with him, specifically in a music video or as his stunt double. Her favorite songs are Fireball and her true OG pick, Kulo, and she ties her Lil Jon fandom to her Atlanta background.

Moving out of her mother's house after six years is presented as a privacy decision. Her reasons: wanting to have sex in her kitchen, not being able to nap after doing sixteen shows in a weekend, and her mom questioning her rest with lines like, it's 3:00 in the afternoon. Jeff had been quietly preparing, telling her he had already put down payments and was in escrow on four properties for her to choose from.

Her mother, Robin, is an incredible contemporary painter whose house is described as a shrine to her own art. At that house McMahan did decorating work, and three days later her mom had repainted everything. Elsewhere, McMahan nearly got decapitated by an outdoor ceiling fan that detached while still rotating while she was having coffee, a moment she compared to Final Destination. Her mom's reaction was dismissive, saying she had come to loosen the screws.

She funds her lifestyle, including her pool, through casino shows and private gigs, and frames it as ten years of hard work. One private gig was for a group of about twenty-five very private people she could not find information on online. Her team vetted them, they turned out great, and now they have her personal phone number. She jokes she will come roast people or families at Christmas for money and notes that decorating curtains are expensive. She and her mother now live in LA and go to the HomeGoods in the valley, homegoodsing it up at all times.

The HomeGoods section carries the money conversation. It is framed as a joyful, feminine safe space and a hunt, where the thrill is finding discounted, sometimes imperfect pieces and making them your own: bowls, mixed metals, marble, discounted sheets, funky outdoor furniture like a frog-on-lily-pad table. Slightly chipped or broken items get bought because they are discounted and the flaws can be turned to face the wall. The snack section earns specific praise for dried pastas, Italian candies, and pistachio candies, chocolate, and pistachio cream.

Overconsumption and wedding expectations get tied directly to financial strain, with an explicit call for financial literacy and for people to pump the brakes. Destination weddings plus separate bachelorette trips are framed as too much to ask of friends. McMahan says she has been a bridesmaid many times and had mostly great experiences, though half those weddings ended in divorce. She married abroad and skipped a bachelorette because asking people to travel overseas for the wedding was already enough; friends threw a surprise pool party instead.

One anecdote lands hard: a group of friends confronted a bride the night before her wedding about disliking her fiance. She married him anyway and the marriage ended. Another friend planned a Puerto Rico wedding, and McMahan told her she could afford either the wedding or the bachelorette, not both. The friend understood. McMahan says she saved for seven years to buy a house and still feels guilty buying things for herself. She did only one wedding dress try-on, was not a Bridezilla, and in Italy was focused on guests having fun.

Her trend takes are decisive. She loves wedge flip flops, Birkenstocks, skinny cigarettes, toe rings, monogramming, going out tops, and Juicy Couture tracksuits, and rejects the idea of fifteen bridesmaids. On monogramming she has euro shams with her own initials, not her husband's, citing the Southern custom that the woman's initials go on the bed. She did not take her husband's name, partly because her father died and only had girls, and says kids will have Jeff's name. Bodysuits get jokingly blamed for poor circulation and gout, and she wants tops brought back.

On craft, McMahan describes writing comedy with a theater-kid approach: start with a beginning and end, a bookend, then work backward. She isolates herself in a basement about three weeks before touring with whiteboards and sticky notes, not sleeping for days and chain-smoking. She names Andrew, Ray, and Tina as the people who come on the road with her. She avoids yes men and actively solicits critical feedback after shows, including reactions from specific seats. She says she feels more confident than ever about this special, while noting her first special dealt with her dad's passing and was vulnerable.

Two closing lessons get stated plainly. If you are about to get on an airplane and do not feel good, trust your instinct and do not do it. If you do not know your job description, ask. The golf community still gets affection despite the Ryder Cup wreckage and the joking about pivoting to tennis.

Running for office is the wildest thread and possibly the most consistent one. McMahan frames a potential political run around the slogan McMahan can and she will, positioning herself as wanting to change the world for women. She says people high up and Illuminati adjacent have repeatedly asked when she will run for office in Georgia, and jokes she may have to cage fight Marjorie Taylor Greene. She describes filling baby registries for women, including women who have spoken openly about infertility and IVF. She was offended when a wealthy country-club acquaintance with a three-thousand-dollar bassinet on her registry asked for money.

The contradictions hold together rather than cancel out. The dog mom who says she would be a great regular mom. The sober professional fired for a chant she repeated on a producer's green light. The woman who skipped her own bachelorette because she could not ask friends to spend more. Damned if you do, damned if you don't, and still booking the next flight, the next special, and possibly the next campaign.

text:
Texas oilfield wastewater could help cool data centers without draining freshwater | Muskanbhatia, Interesting Engineering

Can waste water from the oil and energy industry quench the thirst of data centers? Researchers at The University of Texas in Austin are betting it can.

They suggest that established desalination technologies could allow data centers to use salty or contaminated water to meet their cooling needs, reducing their reliance on freshwater.

Although there are various ways to separate salt from water, researchers said reverse osmosis, which uses pressure to push water through a semipermeable membrane, is more energy-efficient. However, the technology has one drawback: it struggles to treat water saltier than seawater.

Heating water into vapor and then condensing it back into freshwater is another viable solution, but this method requires more energy.

Turning wastewater into coolant

According to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute, large data centers can consume up to 5 million gallons of water per day. The waste water generated by certain oil fields in Texas is over thousand fold higher than this amount.

Data centers can become more efficient in their water usage if they reduce stress on local water resources without drastically increasing costs or overall energy demand, according to a recently published study in Water Research.

“We’re not waiting for a futuristic technology to come along and solve this problem for us,” said Vaibhav Bahadur, who is a professor at the University’s Cockrell School of Engineering’s Walker Department of Mechanical Engineering and is one of the leaders of the research.

Bahudur noted that though the desalinations methods are available but they incur a cost. These costs, however, will be a small fraction of a data center’s total energy footprint when compared even with the most energy-intensive water treatment.

Texas oilfields offer alternatives

He proposed turning attention to the Permian Basin. This geological region in West Texas generates approximately 8 billion gallons of produced water per day during oil and gas extraction.

The researcher said this water could be put to better use instead of being transported elsewhere for disposal, where it could pose long-term risks.

“The Permian (Basin) puts out 1,200 Olympic-sized swimming pools per day, and right now this water is transported over long distances and injected underground. This is problematic in many ways including the risk of seismic activity,” Bahadur said. “We’re also running out of space to bury that water, by as early as 2030. We need to find a way to use it, and cleaning it up for data centers is a great way to do that.”

The research finding becomes significant given that only less than 4 percent of Earth’s water is freshwater, and only a fraction of it, just 0.5 percent, is accessible and safe for human consumption. Additionally, by 2028, water consumption by data centers is expected to reach approximately 33 billion gallons, filling nearly 50,000 Olympic-sized pools, according to Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.

I think Elon is also negotiating in public here, praising Micron while calling the others expensive, trying to put pressure on suppliers to offer Tesla and xAI better memory pricing. And of course, it has a geopolitical angle too.

He’s not wrong, though, but it’s also the strategy of a smaller player with less market share and capacity. If you look at pricing, Samsung and SK hynix have been increasing prices a little more aggressively, and Micron has to respond to that as the smaller player.

So they structure their long-term deals differently. Three-quarters of that contract revenue has a defined pricing framework, mostly with floors and ceilings that protect customers against further increases. This earns them some customer appreciation, but I think it’s overstated. They’re still putting up 86–87% gross margins, so don’t pretend Micron is the cheap and reasonable one.

Tesla has its AI5 production lined up with TSMC in Arizona and Samsung in Texas. So Elon’s angle is also pushing for more U.S. production and a focus on a U.S. player. That strengthens the case for his own Terafab project: cheaper memory, more domestic supply, and more control.

Let’s not pretend Micron is the nicest kid in class.

text:
"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."
