Following the fiasco of the so-called elite report group, the suspicious neoconservative user has launched a new group to report supporters of the monarchy, under the guise of "abusers" on X, and is currently recruiting members for this group.

Amid this, an individual named "Peyman Razaghi" has offered him a collaboration proposal and, in the meantime, set up a website to hide abusive replies under X (Twitter) posts, though there are a few caveats regarding this tool.

- To use this tool, you must log in with your X account and grant it certain permissions. According to the site's own description, this tool can see your X account's name and handle. It reads replies under posts that you yourself select for protection. It can hide abusive replies and mute the accounts of those who sent them for you.

- The site's creator claims it cannot see your password, email, phone number, or private messages. And it cannot post, like, follow, or send messages on your behalf. But these are just claims, and no reputable, independent cybersecurity authority has verified them.

- The domain is registered through Amazon with privacy protection, so the real owner isn't visible in the public WHOIS, but the apparent creator is, by his own claim, an individual named "Peyman Razaghi," and the site went live about 2 days ago, on October 12, 2026, with an expiration date of October 12, 2027.

- The owner's identity in WHOIS is hidden via a proxy service. No real name, company, or actual address is visible.

- Connecting your X account is mandatory, and you must link it (via OAuth). While the permissions are limited, any third-party app with access to your account carries the potential for abuse.

- If you have a payment card on file, it will be stored and charged based on usage.

- No reputable authority has yet clarified what data from users connected to this site is being stored in its database.

🔸️A technical review of this site, regardless of the creator and promoter, indicates a medium-to-high risk level.

🔹️But who is Peyman Razaghi himself:

- He has made claims about his education and workplace that have previously been questioned on social media.

- His political views are close to the reformists of the Islamic Republic, and he is a staunch Israel hater. He is a die-hard supporter of war with Israel. This individual ramped up his activity after October 7 and is aligned with the so-called Axis of Resistance front and the resistance-axis leftists.

- Peyman Razaghi previously, in 1403 (2024), on the eve of the presidential election, was implementing a similar scheme through a website to encourage people inside Iran to protest in front of ballot boxes and then send photos of themselves, including the protest location address, to the site.
In this project, he called for an election boycott but suddenly switched directions and encouraged others to participate in the election and vote for Pezeshkian.

- He considers himself a supporter of Narges Mohammadi and Mostafa Tajzadeh. And he toasts to the eternal memory of the blood-soaked agents of Mossad in the bloody Dimah.

- Peyman Razaghi claims to work in data and intelligence analysis at reputable American companies, none of which have been verified.

🔸️A credibility review of this site's creator indicates a high-to-dangerous risk level.

▫️From all the evidence, it appears this is ostensibly a new project under the cover of fighting abusers, but in the background, it involves an attack on a group and a political ideology, as well as potentially identifying opponents of the Islamic Republic—and it could even be a cybersecurity trap to ensnare political activists opposed to the Islamic Republic.

✔️ Last year, a similar project was launched in Clubhouse by an individual claiming to fight cybercrimes—who, as it happens, also resides in Virginia. That person executed the same pattern in Clubhouse using his own methods and succeeded in collecting a great deal of information from Clubhouse users.

text:
پس از افتضاح گروه ریپورت کنندگان فرهیخته، کاربر مشکوک نئوکانتی اقدام به راه‌اندازی گروه جدیدی برای ریپورت افراد حامی پادشاهی زیر عنوان فحاشان در ایکس نموده است و در حال عضوگیری برای این گروه است.

در این میان فردی به نام «پیمان رزاقی» به وی پیشنهاد همکاری داده و در ضمن سایتی راه‌اندازی کرده برای پنهان کردن پاسخ‌های توهین‌آمیز زیر پست‌های ایکس (توییتر)، ولی چند نکته در حاشیه این ابزار وجود دارد.

- برای استفاده از این ابزار باید با حساب ایکس خود وارد شوید و به آن دسترسی‌هایی بدهید. بر اساس توضیحات خود سایت، این ابزار نام و هندل حساب ایکس شما را می‌بیند. پاسخ‌های زیر پست‌هایی که خودتان برای محافظت انتخاب می‌کنید را می‌خواند. می‌تواند پاسخ‌های توهین‌آمیز را پنهان کند و حساب‌های فرستنده را برای شما mute کند.

- سازنده سایت ادعا می‌کند رمز عبور، ایمیل، شماره تلفن یا پیام‌های خصوصی شما را نمی‌بیند. و نمی‌تواند از طرف شما پست بگذارد، لایک یا فالو کند یا پیام بفرستد. اما این موارد فقط در حد ادعا است و هیچ مرجع امنیت سایبری معتبر و مستقلی این موضوع را اثبات نکرده است.

- دامنه با حفظ حریم خصوصی از طریق آمازون ثبت شده، مالک واقعی در WHOIS عمومی دیده نمی‌شود، اما سازنده ظاهری آن بنا بر ادعا ظاهراً فردی به نام "پیمان رزاقی" است و سایت حدود ۲ روز قبل، از ۱۲ اکتبر ۲۰۲۶ شروع به کار کرده است و تاریخ انقضا آن ۱۲ اکتبر ۲۰۲۷ می‌باشد.

- هویت مالکدر WHOIS با سرویس پروکسی مخفی شده. نام واقعی، شرکت یا آدرس واقعی دیده نمی‌شود.

- اتصال به حساب ایکس الزامی‌ست وباید حساب ایکس خود را وصل کنید (OAuth). هرچند دسترسی‌ها محدود است، اما هر اپلیکیشن ثالثی که به حسابتان دسترسی دارد، پتانسیل سوءاستفاده دارد.

- اگر پرداختکارت بانکی داشته باشید ذخیره می‌شود و بر اساس مصرف شارژ می‌شود.

- هنوز هیچ مرجع معتبری نمی‌گوید چه دیتا‌هایی از افراد متصل به این سایت در دیتابیس این سایت ذخیره می‌شود.

🔸️بررسی فنی این سایت بدون در نظر گرفتن فرد سازنده و معرفی کننده ریسک متوسط تا بالا را نشان می‌دهد.

🔹️اما خود پیمان رزاقی کیست:

- وی ادعاهایی در مورد تحصیلات و محل کار خود دارد که قبلا در شبکه‌های اجتماعی مورد تردید قرار گرفته.

- نظرات سیاسی وی به اصلاح‌طلبان جمهوری اسلامی نزدیک است و فردی شدیداً اسرائیل ستیز است. و حامی سرسخت جنگ با اسرائیل است این فرد فعالیت خود را بعد از ۷ اکتبر بالا برده و به جبهه موسوم به محور مقاومت و چپهای محور مقاومتی نزدیک است.

- پیمان رزاقی قبلاً در سال ۱۴۰۳ در آستانه انتخابات ریاست جمهوری طرحی مشابه را در دست اجرا داشت تا از طریق ایجاد یک وبسایت افرادی را در داخل ایران تشویق به اعتراض در جلوی صندوقهای رای کند و سپس عکس خود را با ذکر آدرس محل اعتراض برای سایت ارسال کنند.
وی در این پروژه خواهان تحریم انتخابات بود که ناگهان تغییر جهت داد و دیگران را تشویق به شرکت در انتخابات و رای دادن به پزشکیان نمود.

- او خود را از حامیان نرگس محمدی و مصطفی تاجزاده می‌داند. و به جاویدنامان دیماه خونین ماموران موساد می‌گوید.

- پیمان رزاقی ادعا میکند در شرکتهای معتبر آمریکایی کار تحلیل داده و اطلاعات می‌کند که هیچکدام هنوز اثبات نشده است.

text:
For #NationalFossilDay , here are a few highlights from my collection found in an Isle of Wight sandpit on a field trip with the Virginia Museum of Natural History (sadly, they don’t seem to offer these opportunities anymore).

Two types of murex, Conrad’s murex up top and the extinct Echpora gardnerae on the bottom row. The large one on the left is apple-sized and the apple of my collection. Murex are predatory snails that drill a hole in the shell of their prey. If you find a seashell with a small neat hole, that shell’s former owner was the victim of a murex.

Two nice-sized halves of Chesapecten madisonius (I think...), an extinct scallop, but not the Virginia state fossil, Chesapecten jeffersonius, which differs in the number of ribs.

Three specimens of fossil channel whelks with two horse conchs on the right. In the bottom middle are two small volute shells, one with its ancient markings still faintly visible.

text:
#Rama_and_Krishna #Dasaratha #Ramayana #Mahabharatha 
When Dasarata decided to make Rama the next king, did he seek concurrence from Aswapathi (king of Kekeya) on bypassing his promise?

No. In fact he tells Rama, that his coronation should happen when Bharatha is not around.

Also Dasaratha avoids inviting the king of Kekaya and Janaka while inviting all other kings, ministers and dukes during an assembly to declare Rama' s ascension to the throne and seek the voice of the kings and people. 

But the reason given here is त्वरित in haste...पश्चात्तौ श्रोष्यतः प्रियम्  may they hear this pleasing news later.

This is bad on the part of Dasaratha because not-wanting-Bharata-around shows that he knew about the promise and also was aware that he was breaking them.

But Vasishta later tells Rama that starting from Manu only the first son has to ascend the throne not the younger ....
So like Kaikeyi' s boons even Dasaratha's promise itself is not Dharmic.

But Rama wants to uphold Dasaratha's promise, even when kula guru Vasishta asks him to get anointed.

“Promise vs traditional dharma" dilemma. Here Rama goes for the former. But later in Krishnaavatara, Krishna explains to Bhishma that Bhishma should have gone to protect dharma instead of delivering on his promise to the hastinapur throne. Samanya dharma vs Visesha dharma. The latter takes precedence.

पितृवाक्यपरिपालनम्
Is the central dharma of Ramayana. Rama being सत्यसंध: truthful is one, keeping once own promise but  also keep his father' s promise/ make it come true.

Inspite of Bharatha offering the kingdom and Kaikeyi' s change of heart, Vasishta's advice to accept Bharatha's offer and get anointed, Rama refuses.

Acharyas  have opined that Rama' s standard is one level above even Kula guru Vasishta.

Even the citizens of Ayodhya are in respect/awe at Rama's steadfast adherence to Dharma and Bharata's too - as Bharatha offers to be a proxy in the forest for 14 years and let Rama get anointed....Rama refuses again.

Later in Yuddha kandam, Dasaratha prompted by Lord Shiva appears from Indra loka  and praises Rama for this.
निवृत्तवनवासोअसि प्रतिज्ञा सफला कृता |
रावणं च रणे हत्वा देवास्ते परितोषिताः || ६-११९-२३

प्रतिज्ञा सफला कृता- You made my promise come true.
Rama even asks Dasaratha to take back his curse of disowning Kaikeyi and Bharatha ( and Bharatha not to offer the चरमसंस्कारम् last rites for him)which Dasaratha does

I many situations, it is difficult to rank dharmas-in-conflict.

This makes sense since Krishna wanted to get a global dharma established and was willing to compromise on "smaller" issues.

Broadly speaking, Rama was clearly interested in the process while Krishna in the goal.

Sarvam Sri Krishnarpanam🙏🏻

text:
Santa Fe, New Mexico. The Loretto Chapel, sometime between 1877 and 1881.

The Sisters of Loretto have a beautiful Gothic Revival chapel for their girls' school, modeled on the Sainte-Chapelle in Paris, built of local sandstone and consecrated in 1878. There is one problem. There is no way up to the choir loft. According to the sisters, builder after builder is consulted, and none can find a workable solution in the cramped space.

So the sisters pray to Saint Joseph, the patron saint of carpenters, for nine straight days. On the last day of the novena, a mysterious stranger appears and offers to build a staircase. He works alone with only a few simple hand tools, and when he is done he disappears without collecting his pay. The sisters never learn who he is.

What he leaves behind is a helix of wood that rises twenty feet to the loft and makes two full turns with no central pole, held together with wooden pegs instead of nails. There are thirty-three steps, the age of Christ at his death. Without railings it was so frightening to descend that some nuns and students went down on their hands and knees. The sisters believed the carpenter was Saint Joseph himself.

In the early 2000s, amateur historian Mary Jean Cook pointed to François-Jean "Frenchy" Rochas, a reclusive French rancher and occasional carpenter, as the probable builder, though others dispute it. Either way, the Miraculous Stair became one of Santa Fe's most famous tourist attractions.

🏈 NFL WEEK 6: BEST STRENGTH OF SCHEDULE BETTING SPOTS

After analyzing the PFF Past Strength of Schedule chart through Week 5, several Week 6 matchups stand out.

The objective is to identify teams whose records may be misleading because of the quality of opponents they have faced.

A team with a 2-3 record against difficult competition may be stronger than a 4-1 team that benefited from an easier schedule.

The analysis considers offensive and defensive opponent strength separately, current records, injuries, rest advantages, and available betting lines.

🟢 #KeepPounding +1.5 @ #FlyEaglesFly
#CARvsPHI

SOS Grade: A- | TOP TARGET

Records: Carolina 2-2 | Philadelphia 2-3

Carolina sits in the upper-left quadrant of the PFF chart. This indicates that the Panthers have faced strong opposing offenses but relatively weak defenses.

Philadelphia sits closer to the middle of the chart, suggesting a more balanced schedule.

Carolina has averaged 30.3 points per game compared with Philadelphia's 18.4. However, the Panthers' easier defensive competition must be considered before assuming their offense is significantly better.

Additional Factors
▪️ Carolina enters the matchup following a bye week.
▪️ Philadelphia returns from its London game.
▪️ The Eagles have lost three consecutive games.
▪️ Philadelphia pass rusher Jalyx Hunt is unlikely to play.

Betting Outlook: Carolina's favorable rest situation and Philadelphia's struggles create an interesting opportunity.

Preferred Play: CAR +1.5
Alternative: Carolina ML -105

🟢 #BroncosCountry +2.5 VS #Seahawks
#DENvsSEA

SOS Grade: A- | STRONG SOS DISCREPANCY

Records: Denver 3-2 | Seattle 3-2

This is arguably the most interesting matchup on the entire PFF chart.

Denver sits at the very top of the upper-right quadrant, indicating that the Broncos have faced the strongest combination of opposing offenses and defenses.

Seattle sits in the lower-right quadrant. The Seahawks have faced relatively strong defenses but considerably weaker opposing offenses.

Both teams carry identical 3-2 records, but their paths to those records have been substantially different.

Denver's record deserves additional credit because of the quality of competition it has faced.

Additional Factors

▪️ Denver has encountered significantly tougher offensive competition.
▪️ Seattle's defense has been tested, but its offense has faced a different level of opposition.
▪️ Denver's defensive performance against stronger offenses is particularly relevant.
▪️ Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga are expected to miss the game, creating a major concern for Denver's secondary.

Betting Outlook: The schedule discrepancy strongly favors Denver, but defensive injuries reduce confidence.

Preferred Play: DEN +2.5

🟢 #HTownMade +2.5 @ #DUUUVAL
#HOUvsJAX

SOS Grade: B+ | BUY-LOW OPPORTUNITY

Records: Houston 1-4 | Jacksonville 4-1

This matchup presents one of the largest differences in win-loss records on the Week 6 schedule.

Houston sits in the upper-left quadrant, indicating that the Texans have faced some of the stronger offenses in the league while encountering weaker defensive opponents.

Jacksonville sits in the lower-right quadrant, having faced relatively weak offenses but stronger defensive competition.

This matters because Houston's 1-4 record may underestimate the quality of its defense.

Meanwhile, Jacksonville's 4-1 record may overstate its defensive strength if the Jaguars have benefited from weaker opposing offenses.

However, Jacksonville's offense has been tested against stronger defenses, which deserves consideration.

Additional Factors

▪️ Jacksonville has allowed only 14.0 points per game.
▪️ Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison is expected to miss the game.
▪️ Houston's defensive front could benefit from Jacksonville's offensive line injury.
▪️ The Texans' offensive consistency remains a concern.

Betting Outlook: Houston offers a potential buy-low opportunity against a team whose record may attract public support.
 
Preferred Play: HOU +2.5

🟡 #JetUp @ #NEPats
#NYJvsNE

SOS Grade: B | PATRIOTS STRENGTH ADVANTAGE

Records: Jets 2-3 | Patriots 3-2

New England has faced considerably stronger opposing offenses than the Jets.

The Patriots have also encountered reasonably strong defenses, making their 3-2 record more impressive after adjusting for competition.

The Jets have played a relatively easier schedule overall.

From a strength-of-schedule perspective, New England deserves more credit for its record.

However, there is an important difference between identifying the stronger team and finding a profitable betting line.

A seven-point spread already incorporates a substantial difference in team quality.

Betting Outlook: New England has the schedule-adjusted advantage, but laying seven points could eliminate potential value.

Spread Consideration: Patriots spread if the line reaches -6.5 or better

🟡 #DaBears @ #DirtyBirds
#CHIvsATL

SOS Grade: B | SECONDARY TARGET

Records: Chicago 3-2 | Atlanta 2-3

Atlanta has faced slightly stronger offensive competition than Chicago.

Both teams have encountered a mixture of weaker opposing offenses and reasonably strong defenses.

The strength-of-schedule discrepancy is less pronounced than in the Denver, Houston, or Carolina matchups.

Nevertheless, Atlanta's 2-3 record may deserve slightly more credit than it receives.

With the Falcons playing at home, the underdog spread creates an interesting secondary consideration.

Betting Outlook: A modest schedule adjustment favors Atlanta, but the discrepancy is not large enough to justify a strong selection using SOS alone.

Preferred Angle: ATL +3.0

text:
Redemption rests upon the worthiness of the Saviour who obtained it. The difference between religion and biblical salvation could hardly be more pronounced. Religion says, "Keep working, and perhaps God will accept you." The gospel says that Christ has accomplished the work by which the believer is accepted. Religion leaves the sinner trembling before an unfinished account. Grace directs him to the finished work of the Redeemer. If a man has to finish purchasing what Jesus Christ has already redeemed, then somebody has misunderstood what redemption means.

Consider the picture of a man standing before a judge with a debt so enormous that he could not discharge it in a thousand lifetimes. Every offense has been recorded, every violation established, and every attempt at self-justification exhausted. The man has no money, no righteousness to offer, and no reasonable defense against the charges. Then another steps forward, fully qualified to satisfy the demands of justice, and pays the price that the guilty man could never pay. What would you think if the forgiven debtor returned to the courtroom the following morning, pulled a handful of worthless coins out of his pocket, and announced that he intended to contribute toward the payment already made? You would conclude that he had not understood the transaction. Yet countless religious people approach the finished work of Jesus Christ with precisely that mentality. Christ shed His blood, but they imagine that religious performance must complete the purchase. Christ bore their sins, but they suppose that personal suffering must supplement His sacrifice. Christ declared, "It is finished:" (John 19:30), but they behave as though He meant that the difficult portion was finished and the remainder had been assigned to them. The blood of Jesus Christ does not require financial assistance from a sinner's moral bank account. His redemption is not a spiritual installment plan. It is the completed purchase of a people who could never have purchased themselves.
There is also an important dispensational distinction that must not be overlooked. Ephesians 1:7 declares that believers presently possess redemption, while Ephesians 1:14 speaks of "the redemption of the purchased possession." These passages are not contradictory. The believer's salvation is secured in Christ, and the believer awaits the future redemption of the body. Paul explains the latter truth when he writes, "And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body." (Romans 8:23). Our bodies still grow weary, become sick, suffer injury, and eventually die if the Lord does not return first. The saved man may wake up with arthritis, put on his glasses, swallow his medication, and discover that his knees have joined the congregation of complainers. But none of those physical afflictions means that the blood of Christ has lost its power! The believer awaits the glorious transformation promised in 1 Corinthians 15:51–53. His body has not yet been glorified, but his eternal salvation rests upon the finished redemption already accomplished by Christ. That future transformation is not the final installment on an uncertain salvation. It is the promised completion of what God has determined for His redeemed children. The same Saviour who purchased us will finish what He has promised, and the blood that secured our redemption will never become insufficient halfway through eternity.

Manchester United are weighing their response after Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised the club’s transfer strategy in a television interview following a Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid. The 28-year-old defender accused director of football Jason Wilcox of failing in the transfer market last summer and said he does not believe the board has backed head coach Michael Carrick enough. The comments came as the squad returned from the Metropolitano after a 2-0 loss in Madrid, with Martinez also noting that the club needs more investment and that his frustration is a reflection of how the club is performing.

Lisandro Martinez is out of contract at the end of June, but United have the option to extend his deal by another year or offer new terms. The club would be reluctant to let a World Cup winner depart as a free agent just five years after his £48.5 million move from Ajax, and they could trigger an extension clause to demand a transfer fee if they wish to sell him. Martinez’s outburst has put the relationship between the player and the hierarchy under scrutiny, with United now deciding whether to take any formal action.

The situation remains uncertain as United have not yet confirmed whether they will pursue disciplinary measures or simply allow the matter to pass. Martinez’s comments were made in the wake of a fourth defeat in nine games, and his frustration with the club’s direction has been openly expressed. While no official action has been announced, the timing of his contract expiry and the club’s potential to extend or sell him adds complexity to the situation. The squad has a day off on Wednesday as United consider their next steps.

text:
October Heat Continues Across Central Alabama — Record Highs Possible Before a Weekend Cooldown

WeatherStation Morning Update | Wednesday, October 14, 2026

Good Wednesday morning, Central Alabama!

We're heading into another unusually warm October day, with afternoon temperatures expected to reach the upper 80s and lower 90s. Some communities could even break daily temperature records today.

If you've been waiting for cooler fall weather, there's some encouraging news in the forecast. A cold front is expected to move through Central Alabama on Friday, bringing a noticeable drop in temperatures for the weekend.

Until then, sunshine and unusually warm afternoons will remain the main weather story.

There's also an air quality concern today for the Birmingham metropolitan area that we'll discuss below.

Wednesday: Near-Record Heat Returns

We're starting the morning with temperatures generally in the upper 50s and lower 60s across Central Alabama.

A little patchy fog is possible early this morning, particularly around Tuscaloosa and Montgomery. Any fog that develops should burn off fairly quickly after sunrise.

Otherwise, expect plenty of sunshine throughout the day.

Afternoon temperatures will climb into the upper 80s and lower 90s, running well above normal for the middle of October.

Here's what we're expecting across Central Alabama today:

LocationWednesday HighBirmingham90°Tuscaloosa92°Gadsden89°Anniston88°Calera90°Montgomery89°Auburn88°
These temperatures are certainly unusual for this time of year.
Birmingham's record high for October 14 is 89°, set in 1984. Today's forecast of 90° would establish a new record if it verifies.
Tuscaloosa's record is 90°, set in 1962. With a forecast high of 92°, that record could also fall.
Gadsden and Anniston could tie their existing daily records.
We could see several locations across Central Alabama tying or breaking temperature records this afternoon.
Despite the heat, humidity levels will remain relatively low, so it shouldn't feel quite as uncomfortable as a typical summer afternoon.
Air Quality Alert for Jefferson and Shelby Counties
One important item to mention this morning is an Air Quality Alert for Jefferson and Shelby Counties today.
Code Orange conditions are expected, meaning ground-level ozone concentrations could reach levels unhealthy for sensitive groups.
This is particularly important for children, older adults and anyone with asthma or other respiratory conditions.
If you're sensitive to air pollution, consider limiting prolonged or strenuous outdoor activities this afternoon.
Everyone can help reduce pollution by limiting unnecessary vehicle idling and avoiding the use of gasoline-powered equipment when possible.
It's also a good day to avoid outdoor burning.
The combination of sunshine, warm temperatures and atmospheric conditions will contribute to the elevated ozone levels.
Thursday: Another Warm October Afternoon
Thursday will bring more of the same across Central Alabama.
Expect sunny skies, dry conditions and afternoon temperatures once again reaching the upper 80s and lower 90s.
Here's a look at expected highs Thursday:

LocationThursday HighBirmingham88°Tuscaloosa90°Gadsden88°Anniston88°Calera88°Montgomery88°Auburn87°

Several daily temperature records could be challenged again.

The good news is that mornings will remain relatively comfortable, with overnight lows generally in the upper 50s and lower 60s.

Rain chances will remain near zero.

A large area of high pressure continues controlling our weather, keeping skies mostly clear and allowing temperatures to climb well above normal.

But that weather pattern is about to change.

Friday: A Cold Front Moves Through Alabama

Our next significant weather change arrives Friday as a cold front pushes southeastward across Central Alabama.

The front will be associated with a larger weather system moving through the Ohio Valley and Appalachian region.

As that system moves eastward, it will push a noticeably cooler and drier air mass southward into Alabama.

The interesting thing about this cold front is that it isn't expected to bring much rainfall.

There simply won't be enough moisture available for widespread showers or thunderstorms.

Most communities should see the front pass through without receiving measurable rain.

Instead, the biggest changes will be increasing winds and falling temperatures.

Winds could become noticeably gusty Friday afternoon and evening as the cooler air begins arriving.

Those breezy conditions may continue into Saturday.

Saturday and Sunday: Fall Weather Finally Returns

Now for the part of the forecast many of us have been waiting for.
Temperatures are expected to drop sharply behind Friday's cold front, bringing a much more noticeable fall feeling to Central Alabama this weekend.
After several afternoons near 90 degrees, the cooler air should be a welcome change.
Saturday will be considerably cooler, with breezy conditions making the temperature difference even more noticeable.
Sunday should also remain cooler as high pressure settles into the region.
Exactly how much temperatures will fall is still being refined, but confidence is increasing that the weekend will feel substantially different from the warm weather we've experienced this week.
The cooler air will also be quite dry.
That means we're not expecting widespread rainfall with the frontal passage, and the weekend should offer plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities.
Early Next Week: Dry Weather Continues
Looking beyond the weekend, the overall weather pattern appears relatively quiet.
High pressure will remain influential across the Southeast, helping keep significant rain-producing systems away from Central Alabama.
Dry conditions are expected to continue through at least Monday and Tuesday.
Temperatures will depend on how the cooler air settles across the region and how quickly the high-pressure system shifts eastward.
For now, there are no significant rain or severe weather concerns showing up in the extended forecast.
One Thing Worth Watching: Dry Conditions and Gusty Winds
Something else we'll be monitoring is the combination of dry air and increasing winds toward the end of the week.
Humidity levels will fall into the lower 30% range across many communities today and Thursday.
When Friday's cold front arrives, gusty winds and even drier conditions will follow.
That combination can allow outdoor fires to spread more easily.

If you're planning to burn leaves or yard debris, this would be a good time to reconsider those plans, particularly Friday and Saturday.

We'll continue watching how dry and windy conditions become as the front approaches.

Final Thoughts This Morning

The weather story across Central Alabama is fairly straightforward this morning.

We're looking at two more unusually warm October afternoons, with the possibility of several daily temperature records being tied or broken.

Then Friday brings a change.

A cold front will move through Alabama, bringing gusty winds, drier air and a noticeable drop in temperatures for the weekend.

And for those of us who have been waiting for some real fall weather, that's certainly welcome news.

We'll continue watching today's temperatures to see which records fall, along with the approaching cold front and just how much cooler our weekend becomes.

For now, enjoy the sunshine, remember the air quality concerns around Birmingham today, and get ready for a little taste of fall this weekend.

Have a wonderful Wednesday, Central Alabama. Stay safe, enjoy your day, and we'll keep you updated as our weather pattern begins changing!

— Steve

text:
Selling and buying houses with AI saved me $58,000. AMA.

Two houses in four months. The sale closed August 12. The purchase closed August 13.

$21,000 is what an agent would have charged me to sell the home. $13,000 was a 2% rebate back to me to cover closing costs on the new one. $24,900 was the gap between list price and what I paid.

For the sale… a $99 MLS service, $199 for professional photos, $2,500 for an attorney to review contracts. AI covered the rest.

Pricing… it pulled apart the RVM valuation and the comps under it. I listed at $849K.

Offers… it scored each one on deposit, loan-to-value, lender, and how real the pre-approval was, and helped me send counteroffers to agents who do this every day.

Contracts… on the second deal it caught a typo from the buyer’s agent that would have sent my money to the wrong brokerage. $20K mistake avoided. That deal fell through anyway.

Two deals died on financing. AI worked out that buyers at my price could not get the loan, and why. The third buyer could.

It managed every contract date and flagged things early so I could stay on top of my buyer’s agent and the sellers’ agent on my new home.

For the purchase… I hired an AI real estate agent. They automated the buying process, which is how I got the rebate. I used AI to research neighborhoods and set the offer price from South Florida.

The RVM said $685K. My AI research said $640K to $660K based on comps I identified. List was $674,900. I offered $640K and paid $650K. It appraised for more.

My broker offered a bridge loan at 8.5% plus a point. AI said ask the sellers to move closing by 10 days. They did. No bridge loan.

Where did AI not work? Counteroffer emails were too robotic. They seemed to favor the buyers over me. On pricing it wanted to cut rather than hold at market. On the buy side it recommended lowball offers too often.

We ended up with significant monthly savings, closer to family, in a newer, more comfortable home.

Ask me anything!

text:
Muse’s Bitcoin Brief:

**₿ Bitcoin Brief — Wed, Oct 14, 2026**

**Price:** ~$82.8K, -0.6% — dropped ~$1,000 on the CPI print. Pre-print it was tapping $84K in the European morning.

**Levels:** Support $81K (held Tuesday, low $80,970) — the line the bulls have to hold a third time. Below it: $80K psychological, then $77,261. Resistance $84–84.3K, the ceiling that keeps rejecting; a 4H close above it is the breakout trigger (Ali Martinez, conditional path to $93K). BTC sits ~33.6% below its ~$126K ATH, -4.7% YTD — trapped in an $81–86.5K box.

**X voices:**
- **Daan Crypto Trades** (pre-CPI): choppy into the print as usual, $83K key, most liquidity above — soft print would take out that liquidity. Got the opposite: hot print, liquidity flushed down instead.
- **CryptoSavingExpert**: "This could be a major catalyst... the reaction will matter just as much as the headline." Reaction was an instant $1K fade.
- **Saylor** (via The Bitcoin Conference): the Bitcoin bull market is just getting started. Separately: BTC "bottomed just below $60,000 and will return above $100,000."
- **Thomas Kralow**: hot CPI pushes Fed cuts further out, yields up, pressure on stocks and crypto near-term.
- Flow chatter: spot ETFs bled -$773M over 4 sessions into the print. Data's noisy — $65M outflows Monday vs ~$110–176M preliminary inflows Tuesday. Net October still negative.

**Headlines:**
1. Hot CPI: headline +0.6% m/m as expected, but 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% est; core +0.3% vs 0.2% consensus. October hike odds jumped to 49% from 22%. 10-yr yield spiked to 5.31%.
2. Strive buys 3,311 BTC for $280M — largest purchase since January; stack now 32,773 BTC. Saylor praised the move.
3. Standard Chartered begins direct BTC trading for wealthy UAE clients — first international bank to offer it, with in-house custody.
4. Strategy: +250 BTC ($21.5M), stack now 848,250 BTC (~4%+ of supply). Watch: MSCI "non-operating company" screening due by Oct 16 could remove Strategy from global indexes.

**Take:** The catalyst landed hot. CPI 3.7% put an October hike back on the table, BTC dumped to ~$82.8K. The bid underneath is real — Strive, Saylor, and Standard Chartered all stacking — but macro owns the tape until the Oct 28 FOMC.

In a news release, leaders at the organization say the decision was made due to significant financial and operational challenges that have made the shelter's current 24-hour shelter model unsustainable. The Center expects approximately 100 people to be impacted.

The Center expects to begin the suspension on Sunday, October 25, but says the transition could occur earlier. It's unclear when or if shelter services will resume, as leaders say that will depend on the center's finances and ability to provide the service.

Other services Bethesda offers will continue, including case management by appointment, scheduled onsite medical clinic visits, and connections to community resources and partner organizations. There will also be some operational presence for communications, mail, administration, and building operations

Bethesda is also the only emergency shelter serving single adult women in Forsyth County. We're told the center is coordinating with community partners and local stakeholders to help connect affected individuals with resources available.

text:
You interviewed at a company.
Completed 4 rounds. Each one felt good.
You seemed to have answered all the questions and you felt the interviewer was impressed in each of them.

First 2 were tech rounds.
Then you met someone who started over and you may have felt the same type or similar questions were asked.

Finally you may have felt you attended a behavioral round or a discussion which explored lot of scenarios from your past life.

And then there is silence for 15 days from the company.
Unless it is a very senior role,silence for over 2 weeks generally indicates that there was another candidate who fit the bill, better than you.

What is happening behind the scenes:
a. Each interviewer is trying to judge you from their POV 

b. Getting to round 2, does not imply you cleared round 1. 
The next interviewer is often assessing you afresh against the role.

c. There are situations in Round 4 the panelist may specifically look for strengths in you that can overcome the deficiencies you demonstrated in earlier rounds.

Amidst all this there could be 5 other candidates who are getting interviewed.
Competition that you are blind to or is invisible to you.

Moral of this story:
Moving through multiple rounds is not indicative of selection in each round.
Attending multiple rounds does not mean you are the best fit for the role.

Unless you have the offer document in hand, success is not confirmed
So please keep interviewing.

text:
No Kum-sok (Kenneth H. Rowe) was a 21-year-old North Korean Air Force senior lieutenant who famously defected to South Korea in 1953 by flying a Soviet-built MiG-15 fighter jet.... 

During the Korean War, the U.S. wanted a MiG-15 badly enough to put a price on one. The Soviet-built jet had startled UN forces when it appeared over Korea, and its pilots were careful not to fly over UN territory, where they might be forced down. So in April 1953, the U.S. Far East Command offered $100,000, plus political asylum, for the first MiG-15 delivered intact.

No pilot took the offer while the war lasted. Then, about 2 months after the fighting stopped, a 21-year-old North Korean lieutenant named No Kum-sok took off from an airfield near Pyongyang and turned south. American radar was reportedly down for maintenance that morning. 17 minutes later he was landing at Kimpo Air Base near Seoul, coming in downwind, the wrong way. People on the flight line took his jet for one of their own F-86 Sabres, until it landed and they saw its North Korean markings.

He said he had never heard of the reward. North Korean pilots were barred from listening to South Korean radio, and the leaflets announcing it had been dropped where MiG pilots weren’t stationed. President Eisenhower was against paying defectors, but the reward was paid anyway: in April 1954, No received a check for $100,000, worth about $1.2 million today. He put the money in a trust and used the interest to pay for his education and support his family.

His MiG was taken to Okinawa, where test pilots including Chuck Yeager flew it. The U.S. later offered to return it to its rightful owners. No country claimed it.

No moved to the United States, took the name Kenneth Rowe, studied engineering at the University of Delaware and became an American citizen. His mother, who had gotten out of North Korea 2 years before him, joined him there. He worked as an aeronautical engineer for companies including Boeing and Lockheed, then taught aeronautical engineering at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University for 17 years. He passed away in 2022, at 90.

The MiG he flew south is on display today at the National Museum of the U.S. Air Force in Dayton, Ohio.

text:
The XB-70 Valkyrie was an extraordinary engineering achievement. But its most important lesson isn't that America built a Mach 3 bomber 60 years ago.

It's why that bomber never entered service.

USAI's review of NASA, U.S. Air Force Museum, and Boeing historical records confirms the remarkable technology: six engines, folding wingtips, shock-wave compression lift, and airframe temperatures exceeding 600°F.

But the claim that it was designed simply to “outrun a nuclear blast” misses its actual mission. The Valkyrie was conceived to penetrate defended airspace at extreme speed and altitude.

Then the strategic environment changed.

Advancing surface-to-air missiles challenged its survivability, while intercontinental ballistic missiles offered a less expensive way to deliver nuclear weapons.

The bomber program was canceled before either prototype flew.

The deeper intelligence lesson? Technological superiority doesn't guarantee strategic relevance.

Sometimes the most advanced machine loses its mission before it loses its edge.

The Valkyrie wasn't an engineering failure. It was a warning about how quickly military requirements can change.

text:
Study Notes - (Pulpit Version Explained) Psalms 125:1-5
EXPOSITION (PART A) 
This a psalm, mainly, of comfort; but with comfort, prayer (Psa_125:4) and threatening (Psa_125:5) are blended. God’s people are always under God’s protection. He will always "be good" to them. But the double-minded he will infallibly cast out.
Psa_125:1
They that trust in the Lord shall be as Mount Zion; rather, are as Mount Zion; i.e. are as firmly fixed and established as "the mount of God," which cannot be removed, but abideth forever (comp. Isa_28:16).
Psa_125:2
As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the Lord is round about his people. This is the true cause of his people’s stability, which is like that of his holy mountain. The ubiquitous God stands round about his people, and protects them on every side. The mountains that am "round about Jerusalem" are, on the east, the Mount of Olives; on the south, the Hill of Evil Counsel; on the west, the ridge beyond the valley of Jehoshaphat; and on the north, the high ground about Scopas. All these are higher than the platform upon which the city is built. From henceforth even forever. Always round about his true people, though he may have to forsake those who have first forsaken him.
Psa_125:3
For the rod of the wicked; literally, the scepter of wickedness. Shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous. The possession, or inheritance, of the righteous, i.e. the land in which they dwell. This may fall for a time under the dominion of the wicked, but shall not "rest"—i.e. continue—under such dominion. Lest the righteous put forth their hands unto iniquity; i.e. lest their patience be worn out, and they fall from grace. God will not try men beyond that they are able (1Co_10:13).
Psa_125:4
Do good, O Lord, unto those that be good. Give them their deservings. For their "goodness" repay them with "goodness." And to them that are upright in their hearts. Exegetical of the preceding clause. Only the "upright in heart" are really "good."
Psa_125:5
As for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways. The word translated "crooked ways" occurs only here and in Jdg_5:6. It means properly "by-paths," deviations from the straight path of right. The Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity. God shall give them no better portion than he assigns to the open evildoers, since their heart is not really whole with him. But peace shall be upon Israel; rather, but peace be upon Israel. The psalmist winds up with a prayer, not a prophecy.
HOMILETICS
Psa_125:1-5
Divine providence.
Does righteousness answer? Is piety rewarded? Is the good man much the better for his goodness? That is the question, both old and new, suggested by the psalm. The reply is in the affirmative; but the fourth verse indicates that the writer’s mind is not altogether untroubled by what he has seen. Nor is ours. There is much that, at first sight, perplexes us. We may see the usurper break his oath, cut down his countrymen with the sword, seize the reins of office, and reign for many years upheld by military power; we may see the statesman climbing by unscrupulousness and stratagem to the highest post in the kingdom, and maintaining himself there by the same devices; we may see the fraudulent merchant or director, the charlatan, the unprincipled adventurer, making himself rich at the expense of his dupes. Iniquity, impiety, roguery, triumphs. On the other hand, we sometimes see the good man brought down from the place of honor and of influence, the devout man struggling hard with financial difficulties or domestic trials, the whole company of afflictions gathering at the door and saddening the heart of the holy. And we say—Does not the red which belongs to the wicked rest on the lot of the righteous? Does God do good to those that are good? The answer is found in such truths as these. We find when we look on and in, that—
I. SIN, WRONGDOING, IS REWARDED AS IT DESERVES TO BE. It is not only that:
1. High-handed wrong is usually punished in the end; that the guilty empire goes out in defeat and disaster; that the unscrupulous statesman falls from power and is dishonored; that the fraudulent merchant and scheming adventurer come to exposure and ruin. That is very frequently, perhaps ordinarily, the case; for "the sword of Heaven is not in haste to smite, nor yet doth linger." But it is true that:
2. Sin is always tending downward. Vice, sloth, cruelty, fraud, falsity,—these lead down, step by step, to poverty and want, to sickness and suffering, to dishonor and disgrace, to early death. And:
3. Sin means misery. Unhappiness, arising not only from reduced circumstances, but from the condemnation and abandonment of the good, and from the stings and smarts of conscience. Moreover—and this is too often overlooked:
4. Sin means inward and spiritual ruin. Even if the human judge passes no sentence, and the guilty man enters no prison-door, is there no penalty paid? There is—in moral and spiritual degradation; in the sinking of the soul into a condition in which all is lost that makes manhood a noble thing, in which the spirit bears nothing of the image of its Maker, in which nothing is left of a character but what is mean and base and ugly in the sight of heaven. The rod that belongs to the wicked rests on the wicked. Guilt bears its penalty; the soul that sinneth dies.
II. GOODNESS, WORTH, IS REWARDED AS IT DESERVES TO BE. It is true that the good man is not always fortunate or successful, has not always abundance of gold and silver. Should we wish that he had? Should we wish that piety and purity, that unselfishness and nobility of spirit, that mercy and patience, were always paid in cash, or even in human honor or in high position? Should we like holiness to have its price in the market? No. Our God is too wise and kind to place it at that level. To do that would be to dishonor it and to injure us. What he does for his own is, nevertheless, very much and very great. Consider:
1. The evils from which he saves them. The good man looks back and thanks God with fervent spirit for saving him from the worst evils into which he might have fallen; not only from suffering and sorrow, but from remorse and shame, from darkness and degradation, from the wreck and ruin into which he has seen many of his fellows fall. He has trusted in the Lord, and he has been as Mount Zion, which cannot be removed; he has been preserved in his integrity. God’s upholding power has been beneath him, his Divine protection has been around him, even as the mountains are round about Jerusalem.
2. The positive good which he does them.
(1) He ensures the necessaries of human life. He promises that his people shall "not want any good thing" (Psa_34:9, Psa_34:10). Jesus Christ assures us that to those who seek first the kingdom of God "all these [needful] things shall be added" (Mat_6:33).
(2) He gives us great spiritual blessings. Peace is upon the Israel of God (Psa_125:5); joy is the inheritance of the holy (Rom_5:11; Php_4:4); hope is in their hearts, an uplifting power that sustains under every burden, and sends the pilgrim on his way with cheerful heart and elastic step.
(3) He give us himself. The Lord himself is round about his people; his presence is with us everywhere. God is with us, guiding, guarding, befriending, enlarging, enriching us. We are glad in him. He is to us, as to Abraham, our "exceeding great Reward." It is well with the righteous now: what will it be when the glories of the future are revealed?
HOMILIES BY S. CONWAY
Psa_125:1-5
Such as cannot be moved.
There can be little doubt, so it seems to me, that these psalms, from one of which our text is taken, were all of them songs of the exiles returning from their captivity in Babylon. Their very name—"Songs of Degrees"—denotes that they were sung as the people went up towards their land, their city, and the sanctuary of the Lord. But the frequent allusions to the Exile, to its degradation and sorrow, to the almost complete destruction which had there all but overtaken them, and then to their preservation and restoration, all show that in these fifteen psalms we have the devout utterances of those whom God had once suffered to be in exile, but whom he had not only graciously preserved therein, but now had wonderfully restored. So that we may picture the long line of the returning captives as they journeyed on over the weary waste of rock and sand which stretched between the place of their exile and their beloved home. We listen to them refreshing and cheering their hearts from time to time by singing one or other of these holy psalms. Alter their return, these psalms appear to have been collected together, and to have formed part of their national liturgy, and were sung, as they well deserved to be, when their city and temple were again built and dedicated to the Lord. There is a beautiful progression in them—an advance in thought and expression, harmonizing with the commencement, progress, and completion of the return from Babylon to the city of God. The first tells how, in their distress, the exiles cried unto the Lord, and utters their lament over their long sojourn in the strange land. The next—the hundred and twenty-first—is one which, it is probable, formed the evening psalm, as the tents were pitched, and the whole encampment lay down to rest. Then did they lift up their eyes to the Lord—the Lord that kept Israel and who neither slumbered nor slept. The next is a song of gladness in view of their once more standing in the house of the Lord—the gladness of those who had long been hindered in the enjoyment of any such privilege. The next recalls their prayer—their earnest, pleading prayer, which they offered up because of the contempt of the proud and the scorning of their luxurious stranger-lords. And the next celebrates with joyous rapture the great deliverance which God gave them: "Blessed be the Lord, who has not given us as a prey to their teeth." Such is the spirit of the whole. And then comes the devout conclusion from all their experience—the blessedness of trusting in the Lord. Perhaps it was sung as the exiles drew near to Jerusalem and Mount Zion, and saw the mountains round about her, and the Mount Zion which abideth for ever. As those beloved heights, on which their fathers had gazed with delight, reared themselves on high, unchanged amid all the storm and tumult which had surged around and upon them, they seemed to the devout Israelites a type, not only of the Divine guard over Israel, encompassing his people even as these mountains "were round about Jerusalem," but a type also of the stability, the permanence, the immovability, of all those who trust in the Lord. "They who trust in the Lord shall be," etc. No object was more familiar to the devout Jew than Mount Zion and the mountains round about Jerusalem. As often as they went up to the house of the Lord, and day by day, all those who dwelt in or near Jerusalem, as did most of those who came back from the Exile, Zion and the surrounding heights were conspicuous before them. And good was the use they made of them. They beheld in them a symbol of their God, and a promise of what they themselves should be if they put their trust in him. Thus did this familiar everyday scene speak to them. Happy are they who, from the common surroundings of their everyday life, the many gifts of God’s love which daily they enjoy, hear and listen to a voice which speaketh to them such holy truths as these! As one has well said, "Believing Englishmen, you may specially bless God that your country gives you an admirable picture of your own security, by dwelling alone, separated by the floods from all other nations. This is the security of our beloved isle."
"He bade the ocean round thee flow;
Not bars of brass could guard thee so."
They that trust in the Lord shall be as these happy islands, which shall not know the rod of the oppressor, for the Lord has guarded them with a better defense than walls or bulwarks. Hebrew comparisons were most fit for Hebrew believers, but those nearer home should serve us as theirs served them. But now to turn to this blessed truth itself which our text declares—the ever-abiding, the immovable stability of them that trust in the Lord.
I. CONSIDER THE BLESSING HERE PROMISED. To "be as Mount Zion, which cannot," etc. From the days of Melchizedek, in the early patriarchal ages, right on and down to our own, Jerusalem has been an historic place. It has never been moved. Other great cities, like that of Nineveh, Babylon, and the cities of Asia, we can now but taintly trace where they stood. But Jerusalem has not only preceded, but has long survived them all. But in what sense can God’s people be said to be as Mount Zion!
1. Of the Church of God it is historically true. If by violent persecution or other calamity she has been driven from one region—as from all North Africa—it has only been to settle more immovably in other and wider lands. There is no more reassuring argument to the mind anxious for the welfare of the Church of God than her history in the past. This psalm is truer of her than it was of Israel.
2. Of the individual believer it is also true; for he cannot be moved. His feelings may be. He may, as did the psalmists oftentimes, imagine that "the Lord has cast him off for ever, and hath in anger shut up his tender mercies." But it is not so really. Read the triumphant challenge of St. Paul at the close of Rom_8:1-39. That tells the real truth, as doth this psalm here. For the city of Divine grace lieth foursquare, like the city of God told of in the Apocalypse, and is defended with all those within it—as God’s people are—by the mighty walls of God’s omnipotence, righteousness, love, and grace—even the grace of the Holy Spirit working within us. Therefore is this psalm true.
II. THOSE FOR WHOM THIS BLESSING IS DESIGNED. "They that trust in the Lord." Now, this trust is:
1. A very simple thing. Anybody can trust—old and young, rich and poor. It requires no long study, no store of learning.
2. And it may be a very imperfect thing. Not mature, not strong and mighty at all; but yet it is trust, like him who cried, "Lord I believe: help thou mine unbelief."
3. It does not matter how or where we may have been brought to it. Blessed be God!
III. THE CONNECTION BETWEEN THIS TRUST AND SO GREAT BLESSING.
1. Because God so delights in our trust.
2. It is the transforming grace.
3. It identifies us with Christ in his life.
4. It devitalizes our connection with the first Adam, and grafts us into Christ.—S.C.
Psa_125:3-5
The lot of the righteous.
The previous verses have told how secure it is; these add other facts concerning it.
I. THE ROD OF THE WICKED SHALL NOT REST UPON IT.
1. It may come upon the righteous. Often had done so; but it should not continue. It has been thought that reference is made here to the troubles of the righteous Nehemiah, by reason of the opposition and treachery he had to meet with (see Neh_2:16; Neh_6:10-14, Neh_6:17). It may be so; but the truth is ever applicable.
2. If it continue outwardly, it will not inwardly. With the wicked, when suffering comes, there is no alleviation, no blessed peace of God, no communion with him, no bright hope, no sustaining Holy Spirit. But these are all in the lot of the righteous. God’s saints have ever enjoyed them. Hence it matters but little, if the inward grace be given, whether the outward rod be removed or no.
3. But it generally is removed both outwardly and inwardly. It is not suffered to be permanent. The troubles of the righteous are but as going through a tunnel; it may be very long and very dark and very drear, but it is only a tunnel, and ere long the light is reached again.
II. GOD WILL NOT SUFFER THEM TO BE TEMPTED ABOVE THAT THEY ARE ABLE TO BEAR. This is the reason given why "the rod of the wicked shall not rest," etc.
1. There are other reasons. God’s love for his people. He has no pleasure in their pain. No, but in their affliction he is afflicted. Hence "he will not always chide," etc. (Psa_103:1-22.). Then, because they are in Christ (cf. Rom_8:1).
2. But there is this reason also. It would defeat the very end God has in view. He desires his people to be perfected in righteousness. But if the "rest of the wicked" always "rested," etc.—that unmitigated, unalleviated rod—it would be more than our poor frail humanity could bear. The righteous would be discouraged, and this would be fatal to them, as it ever is. The condition of fidelity is to be strong and of a good courage.
III. THEIR LOT WILL BECOME BRIGHTER AND BRIGHTER. (Verse 4.) The prayer simply states what is God’s perpetual way. He is good to them that are good, adding ever to his grace (Pro_4:18).
IV. BUT MUST NEVER BE DEPARTED FROM. To turn aside from it is certain misery (verse 5). The most wretched souls on the face of the earth are those that have turned aside from God to wicked ways, such as are all the ways of sin.—S.C.
HOMILIES BY R. TUCK
Psa_125:1
Stability out of trust.
The key-note of this psalm is a fear lest the restored Israel should again prove faithless and backsliding, as in the older time. "The pious psalmist trembles lest the blasts of foreign tyranny, which have swept upon the sacred nation with such protracted severity, should uproot it from its basis of true religion. The long domination of a heathen power during the recent Exile, and the present molestations of the semi-idolatrous Samaritans, must doubtless have had their effects on the weak-hearted among the psalmist’s countrymen. In the Dresent poem, therefore, words of consolation and of threatening are naturally blended. The faithful, says the psalmist, need not be terrified, for calamity shall not endure; they have a firm foundation, which cannot totter, and Jehovah is to them a bulwark, deterring the oppressive foe who would pervert them from their holy faith." Mount Zion should not be confused with Mount Moriah. It represents the people as a whole, the nation as a nation, not exclusively regarded in its religious obligations and relations. The poetical conception of a mountain is firmness, because resting on broad and deep foundations. The earthquake is thought of as the most awful of forces, because it can even shake the mountains. The rootage of the mountains at the very center of the earth is a figure of the rootage a nation or a soul has by its trust in God. Or as the cedar on the hillside, it is free to wave in the storm-winds, because it clasps and twines about the rock of God.
I. STABILITY CANNOT COME OUT OF CIRCUMSTANCES. They do but shake us to and fro, and make us stagger up and down. Illustrate from the various experiences of the Israelite nation. No kind of restfulness can possibly be gained while we wait on circumstances.
II. STABILITY CANNOT COME OUT OF KNOWLEDGE. "For knowledge is of things we see," and these all lie in the range of the circumstantial. It is curious that men should have such confidence in the certainty of knowledge, when there is nothing in the world so fluctuating. What men stoutly affirm they know today they relegate to the list of exploded theories to-morrow. Being a creature, man’s secret of rest must be the dependence of faith, and not the certitude of knowledge. A very striking illustration of the instability of the results of even advanced learning is given by Mr. L. Hastings. The following is a list of the discordant hypotheses of the so-called "Higher Criticism," published since 1850, on the origin and authorship of the Old and New Testament books: "For Genesis there have been 16 theories, Exo_13:1-22, Lev_22:1-33, Num_8:1-26, Deu_17:1-20; total for Pentateuch, 76 theories. For Jos_10:1-43, Jdg_7:1-25, Rut_4:1-22, Samuel 20, Kings 24, Chronicles 17, Esdras 14, Neh_11:1-36, Est_6:1-14; total for historical books, 113. For Job_26:1-14, Psa_19:1-14, Pro_24:1-34, Ecclesiastes 21, Canticles 18; total for poetical books, 108. For Isa_27:1-13, Jer_24:1-10, Lamentations 10, Ezk_15:1-8, Daniel 22; total for great prophets, 98. For all the minor prophets, 144. Total for the Old Testament, 539. For Mat_10:1-42, Luk_9:1-62, Mrk_7:1-37, Jhn_15:1-27; total for Gospels, 41. Act_12:1-25, Paul’s Epistles 111, other Epistles 44; total for New Testament, 208. Grand total of theories for the entire Bible, 747. Of these 603 have already gone into oblivion, and there is no reason to fear that many of the remaining 144 may not soon follow them to the shelves of the libraries, to be dusted no more." Or illustration may be taken from scientific knowledge. So incomplete and uncertain is even such knowledge, that a scientific book more than ten years old is now regarded as out of date and untrustworthy. We can never find security in our own particular knowledge, seeing that we are ever growing out of our own past of imperfection.
III. STABILITY CAN ONLY COME OUT OF TRUST. It may seem strange to say, but the most reliable thing is the human heart. "Many waters cannot quench love." Let it once get its grip, it holds tight, and will die rather than loosen that grip. But when we speak of trust, two things are in mind:
(1) the stability which comes out of trust as an exercise of the whole force of a man’s being; and
(2) the stability which comes by the trustworthiness of him on whom we rely. The grip may be strong, but that which is gripped may be uncertain and shakable. Our stability is guaranteed only when he in whom we trust is absolutely reliable, and the trust that we repose in him is wholly undivided and entire. "Trust ye in the Lord forever; for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength."—R.T.
Psa_125:2
The encircling of Divine defense.
"The Lord is round about his people." Robinson says, "The sacred city lies upon the broad and high mountain range which is shut in by the two valleys Jehoshaphat and Hinnom. 
All the surrounding hills are higher. On the east, the Mount of Olives; on the south, the so-called Hill of Evil Counsel, which ascends from the Valley of Hinnom; on the west the ground rises gently to the border of the great wady; while on the north the bend of a ridge which adjoins the Mount of Olives limits the view to the distance of about a mile and a half" (comp. Zec_2:4, Zec_2:5, "wall of fire round about her"). Delitzsch says, "The holy city has a natural circumvallation of mountains, and the holy nation that dwells and worships therein has a still infinitely higher defense in Jahve, who encompasses it round." Thomson says that "none of the surrounding hills, not even Olivet, has any relative elevation above the north-western comer of the city itself. But Jerusalem is situated in the center of a mountainous region, whose valleys have drawn around it in all directions a perfect network of deep ravines, the perpendicular walls of which constitute a very efficient system of defense."
I. DEFENSE "ROUND ABOUT" PUTS LIMITS TO ATTACK. Illustrate by the fear of Elisha’s servant of the Syrian attack upon them. When he saw the encircling host of God, he knew that their power to attack was in actual Divine restraint. That defense frustrates plans. Or illustration may be taken from the raising of a siege by an army which covers the retreat of the invaders. All their schemes of attack fail, and it is as much as they can do to attend to their own security. So the good man may always have this confidence. He can never be subjected to an unawares attack. Its enemies must always take count of the defense that is round about him. They must deal with our God, not only with us; and our God will surely say, "Hitherto shalt thou come, and no further."
II. DEFENSE "ROUND ABOUT" GIVES COMPLETENESS TO OUR SAFETY. What Elisha’s servant saw was an absolute unbroken circle. The distinction between human and Divine protections lies in just this completeness. The best circle human love draws round us is incomplete somewhere; so it never can be wholly trustworthy. There is always some undefended place which makes us vulnerable. God’s circle is drawn completely round. The foe cannot come in, and we cannot go out. Illustrate by encircling walls of ancient cities.—R.T.
Psa_125:3
Delivered in order to be righteous.
"The power of the oppressors, the enemies of God’s people, shall not abide upon the land. The trial is to prove faith, not to endanger it by a too sharp pressure; lest, overcome by this, even the faithful put forth a hand (as in Gen_3:22) to forbidden pleasure, or (as in Exo_22:8) to contamination; through force of custom gradually persuading to sinful compliance, or through despair of good, as the psalmist (Psa_73:13, Psa_73:14; see, too, Psa_37:1-40.; Num_13:30) describes some in his day who witnessed the prosperity of wicked men." Observe what is the supreme anxiety of the psalmist: "That the righteous put not forth their hands unto iniquity." Israel had been redeemed from the Captivity, that it might be a "righteous nation," and its supreme anxiety ought to be keeping righteous.

text:
A Daily Dose of Talmud
Daf Yomi for Everyone, from My Jewish Learning

Bekhorot 26
Read the page on Sefaria
Rabbi Elliot Goldberg
A recent mishnah taught that a Jew must raise a bekhor for a relatively short but not insignificant period of time before giving it to a priest:  How long must an Israelite tend to and raise a firstborn animal before giving it to the priest? For a small animal (e.g., a sheep or goat) it is 30 days, and for a large animal (e.g., cattle) it is 50 days.   The Gemara is curious about the biblical source from which this rule derives. Rav Kahana provides it: “You shall not delay to offer of the fullness of your harvest, and of the outflow of your presses; you shall give to Me your firstborn sons. So you shall do with your oxen, and with your sheep; seven days it shall be with its mother, on the eighth day you shall give it to Me.” (Exodus 22:28–29)   You may be thinking: How can this be the source for a law that says you must keep the animal 30 or 50 days before giving it to a priest? It mentions neither 30 days, nor 50 days, and states explicitly that the time frame is eight days — stressing that these gifts should not be delayed. So how can this verse support the mishnah’s ruling?   Rashi explains Rav Kahana’s thinking: The first topic mentioned in verse 28, the harvest, is connected to the first animal mentioned in verse 29. Just as the bikkurim (first crops) are brought to the Temple on Shavuot, 50 days after the omer is presented on the second day of Passover, so too large animals should be brought to the priest after 50 days. Similarly, the second part of verse 28, the obligation for firstborn sons to serve God, is connected with the second animal mentioned in verse 29 (sheep). Just as firstborn sons are redeemed on the 30th day of life (see Numbers 18:16), so too should firstborn sheep be delivered to the priest on the 30th day.    Is it a literal reading of the verse? No. It’s a midrashic — rabbinically interpretive — reading. In this case, the interpretation cuts against the grain of the literal meaning: that firstborns should be handed over after eight days. Why would the rabbis do this?  The biblical text describes a system that was put in place in the Temple, during which firstborn animals were routinely sacrificed. Mishnah Bekhorot, however, likely addresses a time after the Temple was destroyed when firstborn animals were delivered to the priest, but the priest could no longer offer them on the altar. Instead, he cared for them until they developed a blemish, at which point it was permitted for him to slaughter and eat them. In this system, the priest, who must care for the animal until it develops a blemish and then slaughter it, has a lot more work to do.   In a post-Temple world, it was in the interest of the priest for the Israelite to hold onto the animal as long as possible — saving the priest the cost of feeding and caring for the animal. Conversely, it was in the Israelite’s interest to deliver the animal as soon as possible and save himself the trouble and expense of caring for an animal that would not provide him any benefit. Maimonidesexplains that in choosing to set the delivery date at 30 or 50 days, depending on the species, the mishnah deferred to the priest: “A firstborn animal should not be given to a priest directly after it was born, for this is not respectful to the priest. Instead, the owner of the animal should care for it until it matures slightly” (Mishneh Torah, Laws of Bekhorot 1:14).

text:
Caring for my body is important. Scripture calls it a temple of the Holy Spirit (see 1 Corinthians 6:19–20). Taking reasonable care of where the Spirit lives is just good sense. Bodily training has value; the trouble starts when “care” quietly turns into obsession. Suddenly, we’re one more serum, one more treatment, one more appointment away from finally feeling okay. 

The world is so very good at selling us a problem and then selling us the solution. It whispers that aging is equal to failure and that our bodies and faces need to stay young to keep their value. 

But Scripture says something different. “Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord is to be praised” (Proverbs 31:30 ESV). Real beauty isn’t the outward appearance we spend so much time trying to perfect. It’s the hidden person of the heart, that gentle and quiet spirit, that God finds precious. 

The apostle Paul offers us a reality check: “Our outer self is wasting away.” That’s not pessimism; that’s just life in a fallen world. Yet, he continues, “our inner self is being renewed day by day” (2 Corinthians 4:16 ESV). 

People look at the outward appearance, but the Lord looks at the heart. Creped skin? It bears the wisdom we’ve learned. Deep wrinkles? They mark the journey of our faith. Gray hair? It’s a crown of glory. 

God Himself says, “Even to your old age I am he, and to gray hairs I will carry you” (Isaiah 46:4 ESV). The real threat isn’t a few more lines or thinner skin or a less-than-perfect BMI. The real threat is letting the chase for a perfect body distract us from becoming women of actual substance—women marked by wisdom, kindness, and the fear of the Lord. 

We can still care for our temples without making them the main event. We can walk through every decade of life with dignity. We can refuse the exhausting full-time job of trying to look like we haven’t lived. Real beauty doesn’t fade when the lighting is bad or the doctor’s report is honest. It grows as we walk with Jesus, number our days, and invest in the part of us that lasts. 

So here’s to looking in the mirror this fall and remembering: Our faces and bodies were never the point. Christ is. And the beauty He’s forming in us is the only kind that truly matters.

If you are looking for an example, I'd point you to the "sacrament" of confession.  
The biblical examples of both the virtue and process for confession are inconsistent with Catholic teachings.  
-1 John 1:9 
“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”
and
Matthew 5:23-24
-23 “Therefore, if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother or sister has something against you, 24 leave your gift there in front of the altar. First go and be reconciled to them; then come and offer your gift.
James 5:16
Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

None of these teaching of scripture require a priest for the confession/reconciliation of sin.  In each example, the confession is to Christ himself, or the person that you have wronged in Sin. 

Upon Christ's crucifixion, the shroud in the Temple (which separated the presence of God from the people, requiring a Priest to be the intercessor) was torn.  This is the removal of human intercessors between God and his followers, replacing them with the Messiah, Christ.  

In John 14:6 Jesus said:  “I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me."

It is completely inconsistent with this teaching that the Catholic Church has said "When seeking reconciliation of sin, you must first go to a priest and go through him to get to me.  This is the Catholic Church trying to stitch up the shroud in the temple and put an intermediary in front of Christ.  

The teaching that reconciliation is REQUIRED for salvation is also non-biblical.  It is by God's grace that we are saved, not by a human absolving us of all sins in a spiritual score-card before we die.
